chapters.title: Chapter 62 | Trouble, Heading To The Hero Association
paragraphs: Unfortunately—
She stood there, staring at the beautiful blue gemstone resting on Mira’s neck. Then, she stared at Dexter’s empty hands.
Then, she turned around and walked back to her room without making a single sound.
Dexter immediately felt a massive headache coming.
Giving a highly valuable, beautiful gift to one girl while leaving the other two completely empty-handed was a massive, amateur mistake in household management.
He made a mental note in his head. ’Buy two more matching necklaces as soon as possible. Otherwise, my life in this house will become unlivable.’
After settling the immediate matter, Dexter wrapped his blade in clothing and place it behind him.
After making necessary preparations, he looked toward the girls and spoke.
"I’m heading out to the Hero Association branch now," he said, his tone turning serious.
"I will be officially obtaining my Hero License today."
The girls remained silent.
Then, Mira suddenly spoke, her voice quiet but carrying a rare trace of worry.
"I don’t understand why you are so determined to walk down this path, Dexter."
Dexter paused, looking at her.
Mira’s eyes remained fixed on the television screen.
"We ended up like this because of dungeons. And yet, you are still running toward them with open arms."
She paused.
"I don’t approve of it. But you are a man. So I know you will do whatever you want anyway, regardless of what we say."
Dexter let out a soft laugh, his eyes warm as he looked at her.
"Your reverse psychology won’t work on me, Mira. Just like it didn’t work the first time we met."
Mira snorted.
Dexter’s expression softened, his voice turning incredibly serious and gentle.
"I’ll be careful, Mira. I promise you."
"And don’t worry." He grinned, his white teeth showing. "Your husband is incredibly tough. I’m not that easy to kill."
Mira opened her mouth to retort, but then stopped herself.

She recalled the dead assassins on the bridge. They had been experienced, professional killers, yet Dexter had managed to defeat them completely on his own. He was no longer the weak, unawakened youth she had first met.
Eventually, she simply turned her head away. "Hmph."
Dexter smiled. He waved toward the girls. "I’m leaving now. Take care of yourselves."
He walked to the front door, opened it, and stepped onto the porch.
Two seconds later—
He pushed the door open again, sticking his head back inside.
"And remember, do not open the door for anyone while I am gone. No matter who they claim to be."
The response came instantly, loud and highly irritated.
"You are not our father!" Mira growled.
Dexter chuckled, closed the heavy door, and locked it from the outside.
As he walked down the cracked concrete steps, the cool morning air brushed against his face, clearing his mind.
He was finally ready. Today, he would officially enter the world of Heroes.
As Dexter walked down the quiet, sunlit street, his mind was busy calculating his next moves.
The immediate neighborhood was peaceful, a stark contrast to the chaotic, battle-torn streets during the dungeon outbreak.

He noticed a sleek black car parked near the curb about fifty meters down the road. It was a high-end BMW, its polished metal chassis reflecting the bright morning sun. It looked completely out of place in this run-down neighborhood, where most residents drove old, dented trucks or relied on the squeaky public transit buses.
Dexter walked past it, his eyes lingering on the luxury vehicle for a brief second before continuing forward.
A few steps later, he stopped in front of a familiar house.
Tessa’s house.
The heavy iron gate was closed tightly, and a small brass padlock hung from the latch. The windows were shut, and the heavy fabric curtains were drawn closed, keeping the interior dark and silent.
Seeing her house reminded him of her.
as he looked at her property more closely, his sharp senses registered something unusual.
Her house had survived the outbreak completely unscathed. In fact, out of the dozens of homes on this long, dusty street, only five had remained entirely untouched by the rampaging monsters.
Tessa’s house had been one.
It was a highly unusual statistical anomaly.

Monsters during an outbreak were driven by a chaotic, violent urge to destroy everything in their path. They did not usually bypass specific, wooden houses unless there was a powerful deterrent or a reason to avoid them.
Dexter shook his head, pushing the suspicious thoughts away.
He turned and continued walking toward the main road where he could catch a bus to the Hunter Association branch.
Just then—
The smooth, quiet hum of a high-end engine echoed from behind him.
He stopped and turned around.
The sleek black BMW he had passed earlier was slowly, smoothly rolling forward, pulling up right beside him on the dusty roadside.

The tinted glass window slid down silently and Rachel’s beautiful, smiling face appeared from the air-conditioned interior of the car. Her red hair shifted over her shoulder as she leaned toward the passenger side window.
"Hey there, Dexter!" she waved enthusiastically, her green eyes bright. "Get in! I told you I’d be waiting for you."
Dexter blinked in surprise, looking at the luxury car and then back down the road toward his bungalow.
"You were actually waiting for me?" he asked, a bit dumbfounded.

"Of course I was," Rachel nodded proudly, her lips curving into a playful pout. "I’m your assigned representative, remember? It’s my job to ensure you reach the Association safely and complete your registration without any issues. Besides, it’s much faster than waiting for the old public bus."
Dexter instinctively turned his head, glancing back toward the far end of the street where his small bungalow stood.
The heavy front door remained closed, and there was no sign of his wives at the windows. He let out a silent, massive sigh of relief.

If Mira or Selene were to look out the window right now and see him getting into a luxury car with the very same woman who had just hugged him on their porch, he would probably return tonight to find the house frozen solid or burned to the ground.
He looked back at Rachel, scratching his cheek awkwardly.
Why was this wealthy, high-status woman showing so much personal interest in him?

If they had known each other for years, he would have assumed she had some hidden, calculated motive—perhaps she wanted to use his strength for her own guild, or she wanted to access some non-existent family fortune.
But they had literally just met a couple of days ago. During their brief conversation at the hotel bar, they had simply gotten along well. But that was just a casual chat.
Yet, here she was, waiting for him in her private car, offering him a ride, and teasing him like an old friend.
Dexter could not understand it. Perhaps rich women were simply more forward and direct or perhaps she simply enjoyed the thrill of a challenge.
Rachel pouted from inside the car, her fingers tapping against the leather-wrapped steering wheel.
"Come on, Dexter," she coaxed, her voice soft. "I’m not going to kidnap you or bite you. It’s just a simple, comfortable ride to the branch office. Please?"
Dexter looked at her beautiful, pleading green eyes, and then at the clean, luxurious leather seats of the passenger side.
Seeing a stunning woman making puppy eyes at him while offering a free ride in a luxury car was surprisingly difficult to refuse.
Eventually, he let out a defeated sigh and smiled. "Fine. But just a ride, okay?"
Rachel’s face lit up with a brilliant, beautiful smile. "Deal! Get in."
Dexter opened the heavy passenger door and stepped inside.

The interior of the BMW was absolutely incredible. It felt like stepping into an entirely different world, far away from the dusty, run-down streets of the outer district. The leather seats were incredibly soft, conforming perfectly to his back, and the air conditioning was cool and carried a faint, refreshing scent of pine.
"Seatbelt, Dexter," Rachel reminded him gently, her eyes lingering on his shoulder as she shifted the car into drive.
"Right," Dexter said, pulling the strap down and clicking it into place.
With a smooth, almost silent purr, the black BMW pulled away from the curb, heading down the dusty street toward the main highway that led straight to the central districts of the city.
Meanwhile—
Behind the closed, blinds of the bungalow’s living room window, three pairs of eyes silently, watched the black car disappear around the far corner of the road.
One pair of dark eyes was cold and narrowed in a deep, burning glare.
One pair of pale, blank eyes was motionless, listening to the fading hum of the high-end engine.
And one pair of eyes, hidden behind active AI glasses, was completely expressionless, recording the entire scene.
The atmosphere inside the small living room suddenly became very, very quiet.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 | Crippled Fetish
paragraphs: Rachel turned the wheel, and the car smoothly exited the street before accelerating onto the larger road beyond.
Inside the vehicle, silence filled the air.

Not the comfortable kind of silence that exists between old friends who have run out of things to say and don’t mind. This was the awkward kind. The kind where both people are acutely aware of the quiet and are thinking about it but neither wants to be the first to acknowledge it.

Dexter sat quietly in the passenger seat while Rachel focused on driving. Every now and then, she stole glances in his direction, a small smile lingering on her lips. Not a polite smile. Something more personal. More intimate. Like she was remembering something pleasant and wanted to share it but was waiting for the right moment.
Dexter shook his head slightly at the awkward atmosphere.

He could feel her gaze landing on him every few seconds. Warm. Persistent. Unapologetic. It was the kind of attention that would have made his heart race a month ago. Back when he was nobody. Back when any beautiful woman showing interest in him would have felt like winning a lottery.
But things were different now.

Not because he didn’t find Rachel attractive. He did. Anyone with eyes would. She had the kind of beauty that turned heads on busy streets. The kind that made people forget what they were doing mid-sentence.

But his life had become complicated in ways that left no room for additional entanglements. Three wives. Three broken women depending on him. Three people who needed his attention far more than a beautiful woman in a BMW.
After several moments, Rachel finally spoke.
"Should I turn on the radio?"
Dexter quickly nodded.
"Yeah."
Anything was better than sitting in silence.
Rachel reached over and switched it on.
Unfortunately, fate seemed determined to make things worse.

The first song that played was about romantic tension and unresolved feelings between two people. The lyrics spoke of longing glances and unspoken desires and the space between two people in a car that felt smaller with every passing minute.
Rachel raised an eyebrow.
Dexter stared straight ahead. His jaw tightened slightly. Of all the songs. Of all the stations. Of all the moments.
Then the lyrics became even worse.
The song shifted from romantic tension to blatant sexual tension. The singer’s voice dropped lower. The tempo slowed. Words about heat and skin and temptation filled the car like smoke.
Rachel let out an amused chuckle.

Dexter blinked before immediately turning his head toward the window as if the passing buildings outside had suddenly become fascinating. A mailbox. A fire hydrant. A traffic light. Absolutely riveting. The most interesting traffic light he had ever seen in his entire life.
Rachel struggled to hold back her laughter.
"Should I change it?"
Dexter merely shrugged. Casual. Indifferent. As though he hadn’t just been staring at a fire hydrant for eleven seconds straight.
Rachel switched stations.
The next song was somehow even more unfortunate.
This one was about unrequited love. A woman singing about a man who didn’t know she existed. About watching him from afar. About wishing he would turn around and see her standing right there.
Dexter almost facepalmed.
Was the universe actively trying to make this car ride as awkward as possible? Had he offended some cosmic DJ in a previous life? Was there a deity somewhere laughing at him right now?

Rachel finally burst into laughter. Not polite laughter. Full, genuine, shoulder-shaking laughter that made her grip the steering wheel tighter. The kind of laugh that crinkles the eyes and shows teeth and makes the person hearing it want to laugh too even when nothing is funny.
A moment later, Dexter joined in.

He couldn’t help it. The situation was so absurd that fighting it would have been pointless. Here he was. A man with three wives at home who were probably still furious about the morning’s events. Sitting in a luxury car. Listening to love songs. Next to a woman who had kissed him and showed no signs of regretting it.
The tension in the car eased considerably.
Still chuckling, Rachel switched stations again.
Thankfully, the third song was normal.
No love songs.
No confessions.
No hidden meanings.
Just rap music.
Aggressive, loud, completely inappropriate rap music about money and power and surviving the streets. It was so far removed from romance that it practically existed in a different dimension.
Rachel left it there.
For the first time since entering the car, the two began talking naturally.
"So, Dexter," Rachel began, keeping her eyes on the road, "I didn’t know much about your situation with your three wives before. But after I found out, I looked it up online."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"And?"
Rachel glanced at him.
"There was... a lot."
"What did you read?
Rachel looked genuinely surprised.
"Wait, are you telling me you’ve never searched your own name online?"
Dexter shook his head.
"No."
"You really don’t care what people say about you?"
"I don’t."
He leaned back in his seat. The leather was warm against his back. Comfortable in a way that reminded him how far he still was from providing this kind of comfort for his family.
"People are going to think whatever they want. Their opinions don’t change my life."
He paused.
"Opinions don’t feed my family. Don’t heal their wounds. Don’t keep them safe at night."
Rachel stared at him for a moment before smiling.
"See? That’s one of the reasons I’m attracted to you."
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly.

How could she say something like that so casually? Like telling someone you were attracted to them was the same as commenting on the weather. Oh, nice day today. By the way, I find you attractive. Pass the salt.
Perhaps it was because he already had three wives and women always likes things they can’t get their hands on.
Whatever the reason, he chose not to respond.
Rachel continued anyway.
"Some people online said you were sold off to the three families."
Dexter remained silent and his expression didn’t change. He wasn’t hurt because he had heard worse.
"Others said you begged your father to arrange the marriage because you desperately wanted three wives."
She laughed softly.
"One post claimed you’re secretly a sadist."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
Rachel continued counting on her fingers.
"And then there were the people claiming that disabled women were your dark fetish."
Dexter was stunned. "People have fetishes about crippled people?"

sentences.text: Rachel turned the wheel, and the car smoothly exited the street before accelerating onto the larger road beyond.
Inside the vehicle, silence filled the air.
Not the comfortable kind of silence that exists between old friends who have run out of things to say and don’t mind.
This was the awkward kind.
The kind where both people are acutely aware of the quiet and are thinking about it but neither wants to be the first to acknowledge it.
Dexter sat quietly in the passenger seat while Rachel focused on driving.
Every now and then, she stole glances in his direction, a small smile lingering on her lips.
Not a polite smile.
Something more personal.
More intimate.
Like she was remembering something pleasant and wanted to share it but was waiting for the right moment.
Dexter shook his head slightly at the awkward atmosphere.
He could feel her gaze landing on him every few seconds.
Warm.
Persistent.
Unapologetic.
It was the kind of attention that would have made his heart race a month ago.
Back when he was nobody.
Back when any beautiful woman showing interest in him would have felt like winning a lottery.
But things were different now.
Not because he didn’t find Rachel attractive.
He did.
Anyone with eyes would.
She had the kind of beauty that turned heads on busy streets.
The kind that made people forget what they were doing mid-sentence.
But his life had become complicated in ways that left no room for additional entanglements.
Three wives.
Three broken women depending on him.
Three people who needed his attention far more than a beautiful woman in a BMW.
After several moments, Rachel finally spoke.
"Should I turn on the radio?"
Dexter quickly nodded.
"Yeah."
Anything was better than sitting in silence.
Rachel reached over and switched it on.
Unfortunately, fate seemed determined to make things worse.
The first song that played was about romantic tension and unresolved feelings between two people.
The lyrics spoke of longing glances and unspoken desires and the space between two people in a car that felt smaller with every passing minute.
Rachel raised an eyebrow.
Dexter stared straight ahead.
His jaw tightened slightly.
Of all the songs.
Of all the stations.
Of all the moments.
Then the lyrics became even worse.
The song shifted from romantic tension to blatant sexual tension.
The singer’s voice dropped lower.
The tempo slowed.
Words about heat and skin and temptation filled the car like smoke.
Rachel let out an amused chuckle.
Dexter blinked before immediately turning his head toward the window as if the passing buildings outside had suddenly become fascinating.
A mailbox.
A fire hydrant.
A traffic light.
Absolutely riveting.
The most interesting traffic light he had ever seen in his entire life.
Rachel struggled to hold back her laughter.
"Should I change it?"
Dexter merely shrugged.
Casual.
Indifferent.
As though he hadn’t just been staring at a fire hydrant for eleven seconds straight.
Rachel switched stations.
The next song was somehow even more unfortunate.
This one was about unrequited love.
A woman singing about a man who didn’t know she existed.
About watching him from afar.
About wishing he would turn around and see her standing right there.
Dexter almost facepalmed.
Was the universe actively trying to make this car ride as awkward as possible?
Had he offended some cosmic DJ in a previous life?
Was there a deity somewhere laughing at him right now?
Rachel finally burst into laughter.
Not polite laughter.
Full, genuine, shoulder-shaking laughter that made her grip the steering wheel tighter.
The kind of laugh that crinkles the eyes and shows teeth and makes the person hearing it want to laugh too even when nothing is funny.
A moment later, Dexter joined in.
He couldn’t help it.
The situation was so absurd that fighting it would have been pointless.
Here he was.
A man with three wives at home who were probably still furious about the morning’s events.
Sitting in a luxury car.
Listening to love songs.
Next to a woman who had kissed him and showed no signs of regretting it.
The tension in the car eased considerably.
Still chuckling, Rachel switched stations again.
Thankfully, the third song was normal.
No love songs.
No confessions.
No hidden meanings.
Just rap music.
Aggressive, loud, completely inappropriate rap music about money and power and surviving the streets.
It was so far removed from romance that it practically existed in a different dimension.
Rachel left it there.
For the first time since entering the car, the two began talking naturally.
"So, Dexter," Rachel began, keeping her eyes on the road, "I didn’t know much about your situation with your three wives before.
But after I found out, I looked it up online."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"And?"
Rachel glanced at him.
"There was... a lot."
"What did you read?
Rachel looked genuinely surprised.
"Wait, are you telling me you’ve never searched your own name online?"
Dexter shook his head.
"No."
"You really don’t care what people say about you?"
"I don’t."
He leaned back in his seat.
The leather was warm against his back.
Comfortable in a way that reminded him how far he still was from providing this kind of comfort for his family.
"People are going to think whatever they want.
Their opinions don’t change my life."
He paused.
"Opinions don’t feed my family.
Don’t heal their wounds.
Don’t keep them safe at night."
Rachel stared at him for a moment before smiling.
"See?
That’s one of the reasons I’m attracted to you."
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly.
How could she say something like that so casually?
Like telling someone you were attracted to them was the same as commenting on the weather.
Oh, nice day today.
By the way, I find you attractive.
Pass the salt.

Rachel continued counting on her fingers.

"People have fetishes about crippled people?"

chapters.title: Chapter 64 | Hero Association
paragraphs: Rachael shrugged. "Yeah. There are lots of weird people in this world."
Rachel glanced at him.
"So which one is true?"
Dexter shrugged indifferently.
"They might all be right."
Rachel blinked.
Dexter simply looked out of the window.
The truth was that there was nothing he wanted to explain.
He had married them.
That was all.

The details of his relationship with his wives were personal, and Rachel was still someone he had only recently met. Trust was built over time. Through actions. Through consistency. Not through confessions shared during a car ride with a woman he barely knew.
He had no intention of discussing it further.
Rachel seemed to understand immediately.
She nodded and quietly dropped the subject.
The car continued through the city streets.
Outside the window, the world unfolded before them.

Massive holographic billboards towered above the roads, displaying advertisements for everything from mana-enhancing supplements to the newest combat gear. One billboard showed a hero in gleaming armor slashing through a monster while text flashed: "STORMBREAKER BLADES. WHEN YOUR LIFE DEPENDS ON YOUR WEAPON."
Electronic flyers drifted through the air, projected by nearby advertisement drones. They displayed discount codes for potion shops and recruitment notices for guilds looking to fill their rosters.
The streets were lively and peaceful.

Children laughed as they ran through nearby parks, chasing each other around fountains that shot streams of mana-infused water into the air. The water changed colors as it fell. Blue. Green. Purple. The children screamed with delight every time the colors shifted.
Parents watched from benches nearby. Some talked on phones. Others read. A few dozed in the morning sunlight with their faces tilted toward the sky.

Large signs pointed toward emergency shelters and evacuation centers built to protect civilians during monster outbreaks. The signs were everywhere. Constant reminders that the peace these people enjoyed existed on a knife’s edge. One breach. One outbreak. One dungeon that spiraled out of control. And this peaceful street would become a battlefield.

In the distance stood enormous Guild Headquarters buildings, their banners fluttering proudly above their entrances. Each guild had its own colors. Its own emblem. Its own identity. They competed for members, resources, and territory like medieval houses vying for power.

Numerous academies could be seen throughout the city, each training the next generation of hunters, warriors, and awakened individuals. Young students in matching uniforms walked along tree-lined paths toward campus entrances. Some carried practice weapons. Others carried stacks of books. A few carried both.
Unlike in the old world, people openly carried weapons on the streets.
Swords rested at people’s waists.
Spears were strapped to backs.
Firearms designed for monster hunting were visible everywhere.

A businessman in a suit walked past carrying a briefcase in one hand and a mana pistol at his hip. A mother pushed a stroller with one hand while a short sword hung from a sheath on her opposite hip. An elderly man sat on a park bench feeding pigeons with a staff leaning against the bench beside him.
No one found it unusual.
Above them, patrol drones flew through the sky, silently monitoring the city below. Their red sensors swept across streets and buildings in systematic patterns. Always watching. Always ready.

Maglev trains powered by mana technology raced across elevated rails overhead. They moved so fast they were barely visible. Silver streaks cutting through the morning sky. Inside them, hundreds of commuters traveled to work, school, and daily obligations while the city hummed with activity below.
The city was alive.

Modern technology and supernatural power existed side by side, woven together into the fabric of everyday life. Magic and machinery. Tradition and innovation. The ancient and the futuristic. All coexisting. All necessary. All part of what kept humanity alive in a world that wanted them dead.
Dexter watched the passing scenery through the window in silence.
For all its chaos and dangers, the world was strangely beautiful.
The journey toward the Hero Association took nearly thirty minutes.
As the city buildings gradually thinned out, Dexter finally saw it in the distance.
His eyes widened.
The Hero Association headquarters wasn’t a building.
It was a fortress.

A massive concrete and alloy structure stretched across several city blocks on the outskirts of Stargate City. It dominated the landscape. Everything else around it looked small. Insignificant. Like the entire city had been built in the shadow of this single structure.
Tall defensive walls surrounded the compound.
Watchtowers stood at every corner.

Anti-air turrets and mana cannons were mounted along the walls, their dark metallic surfaces gleaming beneath the sunlight. Each one was positioned with mathematical precision. No blind spots. No weaknesses. No way in that wasn’t watched and guarded and ready to fire.

From above, the entire facility looked like a mixture of a military fortress, research laboratory, academy campus, and training ground all merged into one gigantic complex. It was as though someone had taken every aspect of the hero world and compressed it into a single location.

Massive banners bearing the Hero Association emblem fluttered in the wind. The emblem was a shield crossed by a sword and a mana circle. Simple. Powerful. Meaningful. Protection. Strength. And the supernatural force that made both possible.
Countless heroes moved in and out of the compound.
Some wore combat armor that covered their bodies from neck to toe. Scratches and dents in the metal told stories of battles fought and survived.
Some wore long coats that billowed behind them as they walked. The kind of dramatic clothing that seemed impractical but somehow looked perfectly natural on someone who could punch through a wall.

Others carried weapons larger than ordinary people could even lift. A woman walked past carrying a hammer the size of a small car over one shoulder. She didn’t seem bothered by the weight. She was eating an apple with her free hand.
Swords, spears, mana rifles and even cannons.

Even beast companions could occasionally be seen following some heroes. A man walked past with a lion the size of a massive horse walking silently beside him. Its fur shimmered with a faint golden glow. Its eyes scanned the crowd with intelligence.
The atmosphere was busy but disciplined.
Professional and incredibly dangerous.
Dexter stared through the window.
"So this is the Hero Association..."
Rachel smiled proudly.
"Impressive, isn’t it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 65 | Ultra Rank
paragraphs: Dexter nodded honestly.
This place alone was enough to make anyone understand why the Hero Association was considered one of humanity’s greatest powers.
Standing here, watching heroes walk past like ordinary commuters going to work, it was easy to forget that each one of them could probably level a city block if they wanted to.
Near the entrance stood an enormous holographic display.

It displayed rankings, achievements, dungeon statistics, and city-wide alerts. Numbers scrolled constantly. Dungeon clear rates. Monster activity reports. Hero deployment statuses. The information was endless and updated in real time.
One section caught Dexter’s attention immediately.
Hero Classification System
F-Rank Heroes. Entry-Level Heroes who have successfully cleared at least one dungeon.
E-Rank Heroes. Competent Heroes who have cleared at least three dungeons.
D-Rank Heroes. Experienced Heroes who have cleared at least five dungeons.
C-Rank Heroes. Professional Heroes who have cleared ten or more dungeons, including C-Rank Dungeons.
B-Rank Heroes. Elite Heroes who have cleared twenty or more dungeons, including B-Rank Dungeons.
A-Rank Heroes. Master-Class Heroes capable of clearing S-Rank Dungeons.
S-Rank Heroes. Legendary Heroes capable of changing the fate of entire cities.
Dexter read through the classifications carefully. Each rank represented a different level of power, experience, and responsibility.
The gap between F-Rank and S-Rank was so vast that an F-Rank hero might as well be an ant standing before a dragon.
Yet every hero started somewhere.
Even the legends were once beginners who entered their first dungeon with trembling hands and racing hearts.
As Rachel approached the entrance gate, she produced an identification card.
Several guards immediately saluted.
Dexter, however, wasn’t looking at the card.
He was staring at the guards.
Every single one of them radiated immense pressure.
Superhuman Realm.
Peak Superhuman Realm.
Every single guard.
Dexter couldn’t hide his shock.
Peak Superhumans were supposed to be powerful experts.
The kind of people that ordinary heroes spoke about with respect and caution.
Yet here they were.
Working security.
Standing at gates and checking IDs. Waving cars through. Like bouncers at a nightclub. Except these bouncers could probably flatten the nightclub if they sneezed too hard.
Rachel noticed his expression and laughed softly.
"Superhuman Heroes aren’t nearly as rare as ordinary people think."
She pointed toward one of the guards.
"Besides, working for the Hero Association pays incredibly well. About 500k annually. "
"Many heroes prefer stable income over risking their lives in dungeons every week."
Dexter was stunned. That’s almost a billion in one year!
She shrugged.
"If I didn’t already enjoy field work, I probably would’ve become a guard too."
Dexter was genuinely surprised.
Being a guard actually paid that much?
Maybe becoming security wasn’t such a bad career choice after all. Standing at the gate all day, doing nothing but scanning the IDs and getting paid handsomely without dungeon hunting.
It sounded almost peaceful.
Rachel drove toward the parking area and parked the car.
Both of them stepped out.
The inside of the compound was even larger
There were separate buildings everywhere.
The Dungeon Registration Hall. A wide building with a constant flow of heroes entering and exiting.
Some looked excited. Others looked exhausted. A few looked like they had seen things they wished they could forget.
The Hero Licensing Center. A more formal structure with official banners and a line of nervous newcomers waiting outside.
The Medical Wing.
The Hero Hospital. Larger than the Medical Wing. Several heroes on stretchers were being wheeled inside by medical staff while concerned teammates followed behind.
The Research Division. A futuristic building covered in sensors and antennas. Drones flew in and out of open windows carrying samples and equipment.
The Beast Material Exchange Department. Heroes walked out carrying bags of materials. Monster parts. Herbs. Crystals. All harvested from dungeons and brought here for evaluation and sale.
The Auction Hall. An elegant building with marble pillars. Through the open doors, Dexter could hear an auctioneer’s voice calling out prices.

The Training Complex. The largest building visible. Multiple combat arenas were visible through transparent reinforced glass walls. Inside, heroes sparred while instructors observed from elevated platforms.
The Combat Arena. A circular colosseum-like structure that roared with the sound of explosions and cheering crowds.
The Hero Academy Liaison Office. A smaller building with young students in uniforms entering and exiting.
There was even a private shopping district exclusively for registered heroes.
Heroes could buy weapons, armor, artifacts, potions, and dungeon supplies there at discounted prices.
Mana-powered trains connected different sections of the compound together.
Small platforms dotted the pathways where heroes waited for the next train.
The entire place felt like a miniature city.
A city built by heroes and for heroes.
Rachel smiled as she watched his expression.
"Not what you expected?"
Dexter shook his head honestly.
"Not even close."
He had expected an office building.
Instead, he found an entire civilization built around heroes. A self-sustaining ecosystem where every need was catered to.
Rachel laughed.
"Welcome to the center of Stargate City’s power."
She led him toward the main entrance.
Heroes constantly passed by them.
Some were chatting casually about recent dungeon runs. Comparing kills and sharing strategies.
Some looked exhausted. Others looked injured. One hero walked past with half his face covered in fresh bandages.
Several carried freshly harvested monster materials.
Dexter even spotted someone carrying the severed claw of a monster larger than a truck.
Suddenly.
His steps suddenly slowed and his pupils constricted as a powerful aura swept past him.
He instinctively turned his head.
An Ultra Rank Hero.
The pressure radiating from the man was unlike anything Dexter had ever felt before.
The man walked through the crowd and people parted around him without being asked. Without even thinking about it. Like water flowing around a stone in a river.
It felt as though a mountain had walked past him.
Before he could fully process it, another figure emerged from the building.
This time, the entire entrance hall fell silent.
People moved aside instinctively for this woman without hesitation.
Dexter looked up.
A woman stepped out of the building.
Long silver hair flowed behind her like a river of moonlight.
She wore a black combat coat with silver trim. The coat was fitted perfectly to her body.

This time, the entire entrance hall fell silent.
People moved aside instinctively for this woman without hesitation.
Dexter looked up.
A woman stepped out of the building.
Long silver hair flowed behind her like a river of moonlight.
She wore a black combat coat with silver trim.
The coat was fitted perfectly to her body.

chapters.title: Chapter 66 | Meeting With Teammates
paragraphs: On her chest was an S-rank badge.
A genuine S-Rank Hero.
Following his gaze, Rachel chuckled.
"That’s Aurora."
"She became an S-Rank Hero just last month after successfully clearing her first S-Rank Dungeon."
Dexter stared.
Aurora walked calmly through the courtyard as though she didn’t notice the countless eyes watching her.
"Her talent is Sky Manipulation," Rachel continued.
"A ridiculously rare ability that lets her control almost anything connected to the sky."
Dexter’s eyes widened.
"That’s absurd."
Rachel nodded.
"It is."
"Wind. Weather. Lightning. Even the air itself bends to her will."
"Some people believe she’ll become one of humanity’s strongest heroes someday."

As Aurora disappeared into the distance, paparazzi gathered at the front gate. They didn’t dare enter the Hero Association grounds. That would have been like walking into a lion’s den with a camera and a death wish. But they hovered at the boundary, lenses extended, trying to get better photos of her as she walked away.
Dexter slowly looked back toward the towering Hero Association building.
For the first time since arriving in this world.
He truly felt it.
The world was bigger than he had imagined, much bigger.

The heroes he had fought, assassins he had killed. All of it felt significant in the context of his small life. But standing here, surrounded by people who could probably destroy city blocks without breaking a sweat, he understood how small his world had been.
And somehow.
For the first time.
That thought excited him.
Not because he wanted to compete. But because there was so much room to grow. So much strength to gain so much investment to be made.
"Alright," Rachel said as she led Dexter deeper into the Hero Association headquarters.
Finally, they arrived at a towering silver building.
Large words were engraved above the entrance.
HERO LICENSING CENTER
"This is where your journey officially begins," Rachel said.
The hall inside was enormous.
Far larger than Dexter had expected.
Hundreds of people moved through the building.
Some were newly awakened heroes that couldn’t contain their excitement.
Others were veterans renewing licenses or submitting reports.
Several queues stretched across the hall.
Rachel pointed toward one of them.
"You’ll need to register first."
Dexter looked toward the line.
Around fifteen people were already waiting.
Rachel lowered her voice slightly.
"The licensing examination itself isn’t complicated.
She crossed her arms.
"Usually it’s a controlled dungeon environment."
"You’ll be observed while fighting monsters alongside several other candidates."
"They’ll evaluate your combat ability, teamwork, decision making, adaptability, and overall potential."
Dexter listened carefully.
Rachel continued.
"Clearing the first wave automatically grants an F-Rank Hero License."
"If you perform better than expected and clear additional waves, your evaluation score increases."
"The Association keeps records of promising newcomers."
"Those with high scores are given priority for dungeon requests, emergency missions, and sponsored expeditions."
Dexter nodded.
That sounded reasonable.
However, Rachel suddenly smiled mischievously.
"Although..."
"Don’t try too hard."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
Rachel shrugged.
"The more talented you appear, the more attention you’ll attract."
"The Hero Association values talent."
"But dangerous missions tend to find talented people first."
"If an unusually dangerous F-Rank Dungeon appears. The outstanding rookies are usually among the first names considered."
Dexter understood immediately.
Outstanding talent brought opportunities.
But opportunities often came with risks. Sometimes fatal ones.
"I’ll keep that in mind," he replied.
Rachel smiled.
"Good."
Then she leaned slightly closer.
"Try not to die, alright?"
Dexter laughed.
"I’ll do my best."
She smiled flirtatiously before turning around and leaving.
"Good luck, Dexter."
He watched her disappear into the crowd, then he joined the queue.
Fifteen people stood ahead of him.
He took ticket number sixteen and waited patiently.
Twenty minutes later, his number was finally called.
The receptionist was a beautiful young woman with glasses and a completely expressionless face.
She barely looked up from her computer.
"Purpose of visit."
"Hero License Registration."
She typed something. Her fingers moved with mechanical speed across the keyboard.
"Current cultivation level."
"First Rank Superhuman."
"Talent rank?"
"E-Rank."
For the first time, her fingers stopped moving.
She looked up as her expression shifted slightly.
Superhuman Realm wasn’t particularly impressive inside the Hero Association.
There were thousands of Superhumans within Stargate City alone.
But an E-Rank talent holder reaching the Superhuman Realm at such a young age.
That was different.
It usually meant one of two things.
Exceptional background.
Or exceptional luck.
The receptionist studied him for a moment before returning to her work.
"Identification card."
Dexter handed over his ID.
She scanned it, entered several details into the system, then returned it.
"For F-Rank Hero Licensing, candidates must clear at least one monster wave inside a controlled dungeon environment."
She handed him a temporary identification card.
"This is your temporary candidate license."
She pointed toward a hallway.
"Proceed to Building Twenty-One."
"Next."
Dexter accepted the card and headed toward the designated building.
The door to Building 21 slid open with a soft hiss.
Dexter stepped inside and immediately noticed that he wasn’t the first to arrive.
Four people were already seated in the briefing room.
The first was a tall and handsome young man with sharp features and a confident expression.

He sat lazily with one leg crossed over the other, his posture radiating arrogance and superiority. Everything about him screamed money and privilege. From his tailored clothes to his perfectly styled hair to the expensive-looking sword resting against his chair.

The second was a massive young man built like a tank. His muscles strained against his shirt, and his thick arms looked as if they could crush stone with ease. He sat still with his arms folded across his chest and an enormous shield rested against the wall beside him.
The third was an athletic young woman with shoulder-length black hair and two daggers hanging from her waist.
She looked energetic and approachable, with sharp eyes.
The fourth was a quiet girl sitting in the corner of the room.
A longsword rested against the chair beside her.
The moment Dexter entered, all four pairs of eyes turned toward him.
Or more specifically.
Toward the temporary identification card hanging on his chest.
The large letter printed on it was impossible to miss.
F-Rank Talent Holder.

chapters.title: Chapter 67 | Preparations!
paragraphs: The tall young man frowned immediately.
"What the hell? Why did they assign an F-rank to our group?"
He stood up slightly from his chair and stared at Dexter as though looking at a stray animal that had wandered into the wrong room.
"Seriously? Out of everyone they could have picked, they sent us an F-rank?"
His expression twisted with annoyance.
"Great. Looks like we’ll have to babysit dead weight."
Before Dexter could respond, the young woman with the daggers suddenly stood up.
"Ignore him."
She walked over with a smile and extended her hand.
"Hi. My name is Fiona Chen."
Dexter shook her hand politely.
She pointed toward the tall young man.
"That grumpy idiot over there is Marcus Webb."
Marcus snorted. "I’m sitting right here."
Fiona ignored him completely and pointed toward the muscular giant.
"The mountain of muscles is Gregor Halt."
Gregor opened one eye, glanced at Dexter for a second, then nodded before closing it again.
Finally, Fiona pointed toward the quiet girl in the corner.
"And the silent one over there is Lena Park."
Lena glanced at Dexter briefly before returning her attention to the floor.
Fiona shrugged helplessly.
"She’s not very talkative."
Dexter nodded.
"Nice to meet all of you. I’m Dexter Ashford. "
The moment he said his full name, however, the room became noticeably quieter.
Marcus narrowed his eyes.
"...Ashford?"
His expression slowly changed.
Then he smirked.
"Oh."
Realization flashed across his face.
"So you’re that Ashford."
"The bastard son of the Ashford family."
Marcus laughed heartily.
"I didn’t expect to meet a celebrity here."
Dexter remained silent. His expression didn’t change one bit.
Marcus leaned back in his chair.
"I also heard you recently married three beautiful women."
His grin widened.
"The three crippled daughters from three famous families, right?"
His eyes carried obvious mockery.
"So."
"How do they taste?"
The room instantly fell silent.
"I’m sure you’ve been enjoying yourself the past two weeks.
Marcus laughed.
"After all, they’re crippled, they can’t exactly run away from you."
Fiona’s expression darkened instantly.
"Marcus!"
She slammed her hand onto the table.
"What the hell is wrong with you?"
Marcus merely shrugged.
"What? I’m just asking questions."
"Sit the hell down and shut up."
For the first time, genuine anger appeared on Fiona’s face.
Marcus stared at her for a few seconds before sneering.
He looked back at Dexter.
"Just make sure you don’t slow us down in there."
"If you get yourself killed, don’t expect me to save you."
With that, he sat back down.
Fiona turned toward Dexter apologetically.
"Sorry about that."
Dexter shook his head.
"You don’t have to apologize."
"It isn’t your fault."
He calmly walked over to an empty chair and sat down.
Marcus’ words didn’t bother him.
Compared to everything he had experienced over the last few weeks, it was nothing.
He had been looked down on his entire life. One more person looking down on him was just another drop in an ocean.
Fiona sighed in relief before glaring at Marcus one final time and returning to her seat.
The room gradually fell silent once more.
All five candidates waited quietly for the arrival of the proctor.
Five minutes later, the door opened.
A middle-aged man wearing an expensive suit entered the room. His hair was graying at the temples and hw stood with straight posture.
His eyes were sharp despite his age as he smiled at the group.
"Welcome, candidates."
His smile widened.
"Or should I say."
"Welcome, future heroes."
Several of them straightened their backs immediately. Because they were a reminder of why everyone was here. To become heroes. To protect people.
The man activated a holographic display.
A map appeared in the air.
"Your examination will take place inside a controlled dungeon environment."
"The monsters are real."
"The danger is real."
"Only the environment itself is controlled."
The room grew quiet.
"The dungeon currently contains monsters ranging from One Star to Six Star."
He glanced at the candidates.
"Our strongest participant today is a Third Rank Superhuman."
He turned to look at Marcus.
"Therefore, the Association has limited the highest threat level accordingly."
The candidates visibly relaxed.
The instructor continued.
"There will be three monster waves."
"Clear Wave One and you earn your F-Rank Hero License."
"Clear Wave Two and your rookie ranking score increases significantly."
"Clear Wave Three and your name enters the Association’s Novice Leaderboard."

Several candidates became excited immediately. The Novice Leaderboard was where every rookie dreamed of appearing. It was the first step toward recognition. Toward sponsorships. Toward the kind of career that turned names into legends.
The instructor nodded.
"High rankings bring benefits."
"Higher mission priority."
"Higher dungeon invitations."
"Emergency response opportunities."
"Sponsorship offers."
"Resources."
"Training recommendations."
Then his expression became serious.
"The Association tracks every participant individually."
"The more monsters you kill, the higher your score."
"Cooperation is encouraged but not required."
"If a candidate suffers fatal injuries, emergency extraction protocols will activate immediately."
"Death inside the testing dungeon is extremely unlikely."
He paused.
"However."
"Injury is very real."
"Broken bones are common."
"Severe injuries are not uncommon."
The room became silent once more.
The instructor smiled.
"If you’re afraid, now is the time to leave."
Nobody moved.
"Excellent."
The instructor turned toward the exit.
"Follow me."
As the group stood and followed him toward the dungeon entrance, Dexter listened with only half his attention.
The other half of his attention was busy calculating.
Because among everyone present.
He could already roughly estimate their strength.
Marcus was Tier 3 Superhuman. But his arrogance would make him predictable.
Gregor was Tier 2.
Fiona was Tier 1.

Lena was also Tier 1 and for himself, his actual cultivation was Tier 3 Superhuman but because of his bloodline, he could actually control the energy wave his body releases, making himself a walking Tier 1 Superhuman.
But his real combat strength far exceeded that.
Following the instructor, the group headed deeper into the Hero Association headquarters.
They eventually arrived at a large elevator located at the end of a heavily guarded corridor.
The instructor stepped inside first and the six candidates followed behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 | Mana Hurricane!
paragraphs: The apartment felt strangely peaceful after Dexter left.
Silence settled over the house.

The apartment had been completely restored by the Hero Association. Every cracked wall had been repaired and repainted and even the shattered window had been replaced with new glass so clear it seemed invisible and every damaged piece of furniture had been restored or replaced with identical items.
If someone had never seen the destruction caused by the monster attack, they would never believe anything had happened here.
Even the kitchen looked brand new. The countertops gleamed. The stove sparkled.
The refrigerator hummed quietly in the corner.
The lingering aroma of breakfast still floated through the apartment. Diamond Rice had a unique scent that lingered for hours. It was subtle and pleasant, like the memory of a beautiful dream.

Lyra sat on the couch, hugging a pillow as she lazily rubbed her full stomach. Her feet were tucked beneath her. Her smart glasses reflected the light on the ceiling and beside her rested several empty bowls stacked carelessly on the table. A pile that would have embarrassed any ordinary person.
She had folded and eventually eaten the ordinary rice Dexter had prepared
The food had been delicious.
No...
It had been unbelievable.

She had never tasted anything like it. Every grain of rice had seemed alive on her tongue. Every bite had been like swallowing pure energy. The warmth had spread from her stomach to her fingertips to the roots of her hair.

She wasn’t even cultivating but the Grand Cosmos Scripture was automatically circulating, draining in mana from the void by itself after her absorption speed increased so massively. Her muscles felt loose and relaxed and her mind felt sharp and clear.
She couldn’t understand how Dexter’s cooking kept improving every single day. It wasn’t a gradual improvement either.
Meanwhile...
Selene quietly returned to her room.
She closed the door behind her with a soft click and sat cross-legged on the bed with her back straight and her palms resting on her knees. She closed her eyes and breathed in slowly.
She breathed out slowly.
Golden streams of mana drifted through the room like invisible currents. With the permanent increase of absorption speed, mana flowed like a flood into her, through her pores.
They flowed through the air in spirals before being drawn toward the dormant Star Node within her body.
Unlike ordinary cultivation techniques that relied on shattered meridians...
The Grand Cosmos Scripture ignored them entirely.

Every strand of mana bypassed the broken pathways inside her body and flowed directly toward the sleeping Star Node. It was like water finding a new route around a collapsed dam. The mana didn’t force its way through. It simply went around.
It was nothing short of miraculous.
There was no burning sensation nor was there any sharp stabs in her chest or feeling of her meridians tearing apart under pressure.
Just mana flowing into her ceaslessly.
A faint smile unknowingly appeared on Selene’s lips. It was small and barely visible. But it was real.
She treasured this feeling. She held onto it like a precious gem found in the dark and this was all due to Dexter. Her life changed when she met him and he hadn’t stopped surprising them yet.
Outside the room...
Mira rested quietly on her wheelchair near the living room window. The morning sunlight streamed through the glass and warmed her face. Her eyes remained closed as she also cutivated.
Streams of energy flowed through her like a dam released. Even the window shook with pressure as mana surged directly towards her.

If it wasn’t for the barrier, the neighbors with sharp mana affinity would be stunned to see as mana roared and surrounded the entire house like a barrier surging around as though a mana vaccum was in side the room.

They called this phenomenon Mana Hurricane. It was rumored that only when someone with SSS rank mana affinity was cultivating or when a Transcendent level Hero was cultivating did this phenomenon happen. And right now, it was happening in Dexter’s house.
Simultaneously, orange glowing spectral arms floated behind her.
Although she had awakened them yesterday, controlling them still felt awkward. It was like trying to write with her feet, it was clumsy.
She needed practice.Lots of practice but Still...
Compared to lying helplessly in bed, unable to move, unable to reach for a cup of water, unable to scratch her own nose...
This tiny improvement was enough to give her hope.
Hope that perhaps... One day...
She would stand again.
Hours quietly passed.

The apartment remained silent except for the faint sounds of breathing as the three girls immersed themselves in cultivation. The clock on the wall ticked steadily. Sunlight crept across the floor in slow steps, just like a thief.
It was nearly noon when Selene finally opened her eyes.
Her throat felt slightly dry. Cultivating for extended periods always left her dehydrated.
Without disturbing the others, she slowly stood up from the bed. She pushed herself upright with both hands and waited a moment for her balance to stabilize.
Although blind, she had memorized every corner of the apartment within two days after moving in. She had walked the space countless times since then, mapping it in her mind.
She quietly made her way toward the kitchen. Her bare feet touched the floor softly, making almost no sound.
Her fingers lightly brushed against the wall as she walked. The texture of the wallpaper guided her forward. Smooth. Cool. Familiar.
Ten more steps...
Five...
Three...
She reached the kitchen.

Using memory alone, she stretched her hand toward the cabinet where the drinking glasses were stored. Her fingers found the edge of the counter. She traced along it until she reached the correct spot, her hand moving with the confidence of someone who had done this exact motion hundreds of times.
At that exact moment, a sharp sound echoed overhead.
CRACK!

The wall-mounted cabinet suddenly tilted forward without warning. One of the screws holding it in place had apparently loosened during the previous repairs. The repair team had replaced the cabinet but hadn’t checked the mounting brackets thoroughly.
The entire wooden cabinet detached from the wall. It swung downward heavily.
Straight toward Selene’s head.

sentences.text: The apartment felt strangely peaceful after Dexter left.
Silence settled over the house.
The apartment had been completely restored by the Hero Association.

Every cracked wall had been repaired and repainted and even the shattered window had been replaced with new glass so clear it seemed invisible and every damaged piece of furniture had been restored or replaced with identical items.
If someone had never seen the destruction caused by the monster attack, they would never believe anything had happened here.
Even the kitchen looked brand new.
The countertops gleamed.
The stove sparkled.
The refrigerator hummed quietly in the corner.
The lingering aroma of breakfast still floated through the apartment.
Diamond Rice had a unique scent that lingered for hours.
It was subtle and pleasant, like the memory of a beautiful dream.
Lyra sat on the couch, hugging a pillow as she lazily rubbed her full stomach.
Her feet were tucked beneath her.
Her smart glasses reflected the light on the ceiling and beside her rested several empty bowls stacked carelessly on the table.
A pile that would have embarrassed any ordinary person.
She had folded and eventually eaten the ordinary rice Dexter had prepared
The food had been delicious.
No...
It had been unbelievable.
She had never tasted anything like it.
Every grain of rice had seemed alive on her tongue.
Every bite had been like swallowing pure energy.
The warmth had spread from her stomach to her fingertips to the roots of her hair.
She wasn’t even cultivating but the Grand Cosmos Scripture was automatically circulating, draining in mana from the void by itself after her absorption speed increased so massively.
Her muscles felt loose and relaxed and her mind felt sharp and clear.
She couldn’t understand how Dexter’s cooking kept improving every single day.
It wasn’t a gradual improvement either.
Meanwhile...
Selene quietly returned to her room.
She closed the door behind her with a soft click and sat cross-legged on the bed with her back straight and her palms resting on her knees.
She closed her eyes and breathed in slowly.
She breathed out slowly.
Golden streams of mana drifted through the room like invisible currents.
With the permanent increase of absorption speed, mana flowed like a flood into her, through her pores.
They flowed through the air in spirals before being drawn toward the dormant Star Node within her body.
Unlike ordinary cultivation techniques that relied on shattered meridians...
The Grand Cosmos Scripture ignored them entirely.
Every strand of mana bypassed the broken pathways inside her body and flowed directly toward the sleeping Star Node.
It was like water finding a new route around a collapsed dam.
The mana didn’t force its way through.
It simply went around.
It was nothing short of miraculous.
There was no burning sensation nor was there any sharp stabs in her chest or feeling of her meridians tearing apart under pressure.
Just mana flowing into her ceaslessly.
A faint smile unknowingly appeared on Selene’s lips.
It was small and barely visible.
But it was real.
She treasured this feeling.
She held onto it like a precious gem found in the dark and this was all due to Dexter.
Her life changed when she met him and he hadn’t stopped surprising them yet.
Outside the room...
Mira rested quietly on her wheelchair near the living room window.
The morning sunlight streamed through the glass and warmed her face.
Her eyes remained closed as she also cutivated.
Streams of energy flowed through her like a dam released.
Even the window shook with pressure as mana surged directly towards her.

If it wasn’t for the barrier, the neighbors with sharp mana affinity would be stunned to see as mana roared and surrounded the entire house like a barrier surging around as though a mana vaccum was in side the room.
They called this phenomenon Mana Hurricane.
It was rumored that only when someone with SSS rank mana affinity was cultivating or when a Transcendent level Hero was cultivating did this phenomenon happen.
And right now, it was happening in Dexter’s house.
Simultaneously, orange glowing spectral arms floated behind her.
Although she had awakened them yesterday, controlling them still felt awkward.
It was like trying to write with her feet, it was clumsy.
She needed practice.Lots of practice but Still...
Compared to lying helplessly in bed, unable to move, unable to reach for a cup of water, unable to scratch her own nose...
This tiny improvement was enough to give her hope.
Hope that perhaps...
One day...
She would stand again.
Hours quietly passed.
The apartment remained silent except for the faint sounds of breathing as the three girls immersed themselves in cultivation.
The clock on the wall ticked steadily.
Sunlight crept across the floor in slow steps, just like a thief.
It was nearly noon when Selene finally opened her eyes.
Her throat felt slightly dry.
Cultivating for extended periods always left her dehydrated.
Without disturbing the others, she slowly stood up from the bed.
She pushed herself upright with both hands and waited a moment for her balance to stabilize.
Although blind, she had memorized every corner of the apartment within two days after moving in.
She had walked the space countless times since then, mapping it in her mind.
She quietly made her way toward the kitchen.
Her bare feet touched the floor softly, making almost no sound.
Her fingers lightly brushed against the wall as she walked.
The texture of the wallpaper guided her forward.
Smooth.
Cool.
Familiar.
Ten more steps...
Five...
Three...
She reached the kitchen.

Her fingers found the edge of the counter.

CRACK!

The repair team had replaced the cabinet but hadn’t checked the mounting brackets thoroughly.
The entire wooden cabinet detached from the wall.
It swung downward heavily.
Straight toward Selene’s head.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 | I can See You
paragraphs: The entire wooden cabinet detached from the wall as it swung downward heavily.
Straight toward Selene’s head.
Everything happened in less than a second.

Lyra had been watching Selene curiously ever since she came out from the room. So when the cabinet started to shake. She saw it and also watched saw as the cabinet fell with Selene standing directly beneath it.
Her mouth opened to scream out with warning, but no sound came out.
Mira’s eyes instantly snapped open. Superhuman Heroes hearing range was about a 100 meter radius so she heard as the cabinet started to fall.
She turned around only to watch the cabinet fall directly on Selene.
"Selene!"
Neither Mira nor Lyra could react in time.
The cabinet was already falling. Gravity pulled it down with relentless force. Glasses and cups spilled from inside, shattering against the counter below.
Yet...
At that very instant —
Something shocking happened.
"Crack!"
Something snapped inside of her, like a dam breaking inside her soul.
"BOOM!"

An invisible pulse exploded outward from her body, expanding in every direction like a shockwave made of pure energy. It passed through walls, furniture, and air without disturbing any of it physically.
But to Selene...
The world suddenly changed.
Ripples spread through the air like circles across a still lake. Each ripple carried information. Each wave painted a picture.
Every vibration...
Every heartbeat...
Every movement...
Everything around her became astonishingly clear and she suddenly realized with astonish shock that... she could see.
She couldn’t see with her eyes, but With sound instead.

The pulse she had released bounced off every surface and returned to her. The returning waves carried shapes, distances, and textures. Her brain processed them instantly, constructing a three-dimensional image of her surroundings.
She could feel the cabinet falling above her, she could tell its weight, its speed and even Its trajectory.
Her hand shot upward instinctively.
"Bam!
The heavy cabinet landed firmly in her palmx stopping it from falling on her, barely an inch above her head.
The impact sent a jolt through her arm. The wood was heavy. The edges dug into her skin. But she easily held it with her strength.
Silence filled the entire apartment.
Broken glass lay scattered across the counter and floor. A coffee mug rolled in a slow circle, its handle snapped off.
Lyra froze in place. One foot was mid-step about to activate her movement technique. Her hand was still reaching toward the kitchen.
Mira’s pupils contracted to pinpoints. Her Spectral Arms had already formed halfway when this shocking thing happened.
Even Selene herself stood motionless. Her breath came in short gasps. Her arm trembled under the weight of the cabinet.
Slowly...
Very slowly...
She lowered the cabinet onto the floor. It landed with a heavy thud as the glasses inside clinked against each other.
Her breathing became uneven. Her chest rose and fell rapidly. Sweat beaded on her forehead.
"What..."
She whispered as her voice trembled in shock.
She slowly turned her head.
Although her empty eyes remained unfocused...
She could perceive the outlines of the kitchen. Shapes appeared before her like shadows painted on black canvas.
She couldn’t see colors but she could see clearly in black and white. And the shapes were extremely clear but the details not soo much.
The kitchen counter stretched before her like a long flat shadow.
The refrigerator hummed to her right, its outline clearer than everything else because of the constant vibration of its motor.
The dining table stood in the center of the room, four chairs tucked around it.
Everything appeared like pale silhouettes floating inside an endless black world. Like watching ghosts move through dark water.
She lifted a trembling hand toward her own face.
Tears suddenly welled inside her eyes before spilling over.
"I can..."
Her voice cracked as though she still couldn’t believe it.
"I can really see...
The words barely escaped Selene’s lips before tears spilled down her cheeks. They ran in silent streams, dripping from her jaw onto the floor.
Her entire body trembled from overwhelming emotion that had been locked inside her for years.
For years, she had lived in endless darkness without shapes colors or form, missing countless sunrise and moonlight. Nor even able to see shadows or light of any kind.

Nothing but an eternal black world. A void that swallowed everything. She had forgotten what her own hands looked like. She had forgotten what the sky looked like. She had forgotten what faces looked like.
Yet now...
Although the world before her was slightly blurry and colorless...
Although it was made of vibrations rather than light...
It was still a world and a world she could perceive, a world that existed beyond the darkness.

She slowly lifted both hands, staring at them with disbelief. Rather than seeing flesh and skin, she perceived two hazy silhouettes outlined by countless vibrating waves. She could see her fingers. She could see them move when she wiggled them.
Everything around her was the same.
The walls...
The table...
The chairs...
Even the air itself seemed alive with rippling vibrations. Every surface reflected her pulse back to her, creating a constantly updating image of her surroundings.
It was unlike normal vision.
It was something completely different.
Something that transcended sight itself and she felt that she could see farther and more detailed than true sight even though it isn’t as detailed as real eyes.
She couldn’t see the moles or pores or her finger nails or details like that, but it was still amazing.
"...I can really see..."
Her knees nearly gave out beneath her. She grabbed the edge of the counter to steady herself.
"Selene!"
"Are you alright?"
Selene turned toward the familiar voice and saw Mira in the wheelchair, her neck turned as she faced her and looked at her worriedly.
For the first time...
She wasn’t merely listening to the voice, she could actually distinguish Mira’s figure.
A blurry silhouette sitting in a wheelchair. She could see the wheels. She could see Mira’s arms. She could see her hair falling over her shoulders.
Selene gasped in disbelief and excitement. She slowly walked towards Mira and stopped before her. Bending down slightly,
"I can see you..."
Mira froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 | Selene’s Second Awakening
paragraphs: "What?"
"I can see you..."
Selene repeated, her voice shaking as she spoke.
"It isn’t clear..."
"I can’t see colors..."
"Everything is black and white. But... I can see..."
She didn’t try to wipe the tears in her face. She didn’t even notice she was crying at this point.
Her hands reached forward, and they accurately touched Mira’s shoulders.
She knelt beside the wheelchair and she gently cupped Mira’s face with trembling hands.
Her fingertips slowly traced Mira’s cheeks. The curve of her jaw. The bridge of her nose. The softness of her skin.
As she touched each feature, the blurry outline in her strange vision became clearer. The combination of touch and vibration created a more detailed image than either sense alone.
"You’ve gotten much thinner. Since the accident."
She smiled through her tears. The smile was raw and completely unguarded. It was the most honest expression Selene had worn in years.
"You’re beautiful regardless."
Mira remained speechless. Her mouth opened slightly but no words came out. Her eyes glistened. She blinked rapidly, as though trying to hold back her own tears
She had never seen Selene cry this much before. Not even after the accident.
But today...
She cried like a little girl.
Lyra quietly walked to them, watching silently. Her smart glasses translated what was been said rapidly to texts for her.
Her lips pressed together tightly as she was stunned when she read what was been said.
Selene sensed another familiar presence. The new sight was fully 360, unlike normal sight, so she could see behind her as Lyra approached.
She turned toward Lyra.
Although the outline was slightly blurrier than Mira’s, she could still make out the young woman’s figure. Her slender frame, her glasses, and the way she tilted her head when observing something.
She reached out.
Selene gently held Lyra’s cheeks. Her trembling fingers carefully explored every contour of her face.
A smile slowly appeared on Selene’s face.
"You look so much different now."
Lyra’s eyes became moist. She blinked several times. A single tear escaped and rolled down her cheek, touching Selene’s fingertip.
She couldn’t hear Selene’s voice. She hadn’t heard a single word spoken in the kitchen.
But even without the glasses, she could understand from her lips.
She nodded gently.
Selene chuckled softly.
"As time went on, my senses lost their perspective, and my memories weren’t what they once were. Everyone’s faces gradually got lost, and I thought I would never see your faces again."
She looked at the two girls with a grin. "Now I can see your faces."
The two girls faintly smiled at her.
Several minutes passed before Mira finally broke the silence. She cleared her throat softly.
"...Tell me, what exactly happened?"
Selene took a deep breath as she thought back to it with furrowed brows.
"I have no idea either. The cabinet was falling, I heard your voice and thought there was an assassin, and then..."
"The entire world suddenly opened."
She closed her eyes.
The strange perception didn’t vanish instantly.
"It doesn’t work with my eyes," she murmured as she covered her ears.
Suddenly, the strange perception diminished but didn’t disappear.
"When I close them, it reduces..."
She closed her ears again. Then opened them. Closed. Opened.
Each time, the vibration-sight appeared and disappeared.
"It feels..."
She searched for the right words. Her brow furrowed in concentration.
"...like I’m hearing vibrations."
"I don’t see light."
"I don’t see colors."
"I only see movement."
"The stronger the vibration..."
"The clearer it becomes."
She pointed toward the refrigerator. "That’s the clearest thing in the room. Because it’s always humming."
Then she pointed toward Lyra. "You’re the blurriest. Because you barely move. I think it’s due to your shadow talent."
Mira’s expression gradually became serious. Her mind was already working. Her eyes widened as a thought struck her.
"A talent..."
Selene blinked in confusion; so did Lyra, as they looked at her curiously.
"A talent?"
Mira nodded slowly as she remembered what happened to her.
"I think you’ve awakened a second talent."
The room instantly fell silent.
Second awakening.
Those two words carried enormous weight.
Throughout the entire city...
Double Awakeners were almost nonexistent. The probability was so astronomically low that most people considered it a myth. A fairy tale told to young awakeners to give them false hope.
The chance of awakening a second talent was less than one in a hundred thousand.
Many people with low talent spent their entire lives hoping for such a miracle. They risked their lives in dungeons searching for items that might trigger a second awakening.
Most died without ever experiencing it.
Yet...
Selene had just awakened one. Sitting in a kitchen and catching a falling cabinet.
Mira stared thoughtfully at her. Her eyes narrowed slightly.
"If I’m right..."
"It should be an A-Rank sensory talent."
"A talent that allows you to perceive the world through vibrations."
Selene slowly nodded.
"It does feel like that..."
"I don’t use my eyes..."
"I use..."
She hesitated. The sensation was still so new. So foreign.
"...everything around me."
Lyra suddenly began typing rapidly on her phone. Her thumbs flew across the screen.
A second later, the AI speaker spoke in its mechanical voice.
"Like a bat?"
Selene blinked.
Her eyes slowly widened.
"Exactly like a bat."
"I send something out..."
"And it comes back."
"That’s how I can see."
Mira tilted her head, and she thought of a talent that fits the description.
"...Echolocation."
"The talent is called Echolocation."
"It’s a rare sensory talent. "
The three girls exchanged stunned looks as the information settled on them.
Suddenly, Mira closed her eyes and then two orange spectral arms emerged from behind her. Even Selene could see those arms as they floated in the air.
The two girls were shocked.
"W-what is that?"
Mira inhaled and replied. "I also awakened a second talent yesterday. I call it mana arms."
Lyra and Selene were really surprised. "You awakened yesterday, and now Selene awakens today. Which means I might awaken a second talent tomorrow."

"Something is not right."
Selene looked toward her, the blurry outline of Mira’s face turning in her direction.
"What do you mean?"
Mira frowned. The lines on her forehead deepened.

"A second awakening is not something that simply happens. It has an extremely low probability. In the entire city, there has not been a confirmed Double Awakener in years. Maybe decades. And now you suddenly awaken one too?"
She shook her head slowly.
"It does not make sense."
Selene lowered her head. She stared at her own hands. The blurry silhouettes of her fingers wiggled back at her, still strange and wonderful even as doubt crept into her mind.
"I do not know," she admitted quietly.
"I awakened mine and thought I was lucky. But now you awakened one too. That changes everything."
Lyra quickly typed on her phone.
The AI voice echoed through the room.
"Could it be that strange accident that did this to us?"
Selene was the first to shake her head slowly.

"I do not think it was the accident. There were many injured people along with us during the expedition. If the accident caused this, others should have awakened too. We would have heard about it from our families."
Mira agreed.
"Exactly. So it was not the accident. The accident just caused this. It did not give us anything new."
Lyra typed another question.
"Then what do we all have in common?"
"The food?" Selene suggested. Her voice was hopeful but uncertain.
Mira immediately shook her head.
"I awakened mine before we ate the meal. It can’t be the tea"
"The cultivation technique?" Selene asked again. It was the only thing that made sense.
Mira frowned deeper, the crease between her eyebrows becoming more pronounced.

"I have never heard of a cultivation technique granting talents. No matter how powerful. The Grand Cosmos Scripture is incredible, but it is still just a cultivation method. It helps you gather and circulate mana. It does not create talents. Talents come from the soul, not from mana."
Again, silence.
The three girls sat quietly in the room, thinking.
Then, almost simultaneously, the same name surfaced in all three of their minds.
"Dexter," Mira whispered.
Selene’s pupils contracted behind her white eyes.
Lyra slowly looked toward Dexter’s empty room. His door was open and she could see half way into his room.
Everything had started after meeting him.
The miraculous tea, the astonishing meals, and the impossible cultivation technique that appeared out of nowhere.
And now two second awakenings. Both happening within days of each other. Both happening to people living under the same roof as Dexter.
None of it made sense unless you connect Dexter to it.
Selene slowly muttered, "It cannot be him. No one can grant talents."
Her voice was uncertain, and she wanted to believe it was impossible. But the evidence was piling up, and each new piece fit the pattern too perfectly to ignore.
Mira nodded.
"I know. It should not be possible. Talents are innate."
She paused, her gaze drifting around the apartment.
"But the only common factor between us is Dexter."
Lyra’s fingers slowly hovered above her phone. She wanted to type something but could not find the right words.
Instead of typing, she closed her eyes.
A thought surfaced inside her mind.
What if I awakened too?
The thought took hold, and it refused to let go no matter how much she tried to push it away.
She slowly sat cross-legged on the couch, and both Mira and Selene looked at her curiously.
"What are you doing?" Mira asked.
Lyra opened one eye before typing.
The AI speaker responded.
"If both of you awakened, maybe I have one too.
Mira blinked, caught off guard by the statement.
"That is," she started, then stopped to think. Her frown deepened as she considered the possibility. Then slowly, reluctantly, she nodded.
"It is not impossible. If there really is a common trigger, and all three of us were exposed to the same things, then perhaps you should try sensing your body."

Selene smiled encouragingly. Through her vibration sight, she could see Lyra sitting on the couch. The blurry outline of her folded legs. The way her hands rested on her knees, palms up in a meditation posture.
"Close your eyes. Do not think about anything else. Just feel."
Lyra nodded.
She slowly closed her eyes.
The apartment fell completely silent. Even the refrigerator seemed to quiet its humming, though that was probably just her imagination.
She regulated her breathing.
She focused on her body.
Something that would indicate a hidden talent waiting to be discovered.
Minutes passed, but nothing happened.
She searched every corner of her body with her mind, looking for anything different, anything new, but there was nothing—just the darkness of the endless void and the three blazing star modes.
Apart from that’s sh has nothing.
After nearly ten minutes, she slowly opened her eyes and shook her head.
Nothing.
Mira smiled gently.
"Do not force it. Maybe it just needs more time. Or maybe it will come when you least expect it. That is how these things usually work."
Lyra sighed quietly in disappointment.
She had honestly been hoping for a miracle after seeing Mira’s Spectral Arms and Selene’s Echolocation, but it didn’t happen.
Still, seeing Selene smile for the first time in years, seeing Mira regain a little independence with her new arms, she was genuinely happy for them. That happiness outweighed her own disappointment.
Even if she remained the same, she could still see what they were saying with the AI glasses. It was nice.
Lyra let out another quiet sigh and slowly stood up to go to the room.
Just as she was about to leave the kitchen, she heard a voice speaking.
"Don’t try to give up. Just try again."
Lyra frowned and looked towards Mira. She clearly didn’t see her mouth move, so how did she speak? Not to mention. She heard her eardrum had been thoroughly destroyed, so how could she hear anything?
’It must have been the wind.’
