chapters.title: Chapter 72 | Lyra’s Awakening II
paragraphs: Seeing Lyra gaze at her like that, Mira raised an eyebrow.
"What happened?"
Lyra blinked in confusion. She quickly typed on her phone.
"Did you say something just now?"
The AI glasses read the words aloud in their flat, emotionless tone.
Mira looked puzzled. Her brow furrowed.
"No. I only spoke a minute ago. I have not spoken since then."
Selene nodded in agreement.
"I did not hear her say anything either."
Lyra froze.
A strange feeling crept into her chest. It was Like standing at the edge of a cliff in the dark, knowing something was there but not being able to see it.
Then the voice came again.
"So sad. She’s truly desperate to awaken a second talent to help her hear sounds again."
Lyra’s breathing hitched, and her heart skipped a beat.
This time the voice sounded clearer, and she saw Mira didn’t open her mouth, but she clearly heard her voice.
And it was coming from inside her head.
She looked deeply at Mira again. Her eyes were wide. Searching.
"You really did not say anything and are not tricking me?"
Mira slowly shook her head. Her expression was serious now, concern replacing her earlier confusion.
"No. I have been quiet this whole time."

Selene’s expression gradually turned serious as well. Through her vibrating sight, she could see Lyra’s heartbeat increasing. The vibrations coming from her body were accelerating, her chest pulsing faster than before.
"Lyra, a-re you actually hearing voices?"
Lyra swallowed. Her throat felt tight and dry.
She slowly typed.
"It sounds like Mira’s voice."
Mira frowned.
"But I never said it, and you also can’t hear anything."
The AI glasses translated the words, and the apartment became eerily quiet.
A chill ran down all three of their spines simultaneously.
Lyra slowly sat back down on the couch in dejection. Maybe she really was wishing she had a second talent and was hallucinating Mira’s voice.
’Try again.’
The voice sounded out, and this time it was Selena’s voice.
Lyra didn’t bother checking if it was hallucinations but closed her eyes and tried again.
This time she really calmed herself down and listened.
Nothing happened as expected.
But after 7 minutes, a strange frequency seemed to spread through the room. It radiated outward from her mind like a pulse, similar to Selene’s echolocation but different.
It was faint at first. Almost impossible to notice. Like hearing a whisper from across a vast field, carried on wind that kept shifting direction.
Yet the more she focused, the louder it became.
Then a gentle voice echoed inside her mind.
’Come on. One more try. You can do it.’
Lyra’s eyes snapped open.
She looked directly at Selene. Her expression changed, and her lips parted slightly.
Selene blinked.
"What?"
Lyra immediately began typing furiously. Her thumbs hammered the screen, making mistakes in her haste.
The AI speaker read her words correctly without including the mistakes.
"You keep encouraging me."
Selene stared at her.
"I did not. I swear on my life, I did not say anything."
Lyra’s fingers paused above the screen.
First it was Mira, and now it was Selene.
If it was not them, then whose voice was she hearing?
Suddenly her body trembled violently.
A sharp pulse exploded inside her mind. It was like a door being kicked open. A wall collapsing. A dam breaking after years of holding back pressure.
"BOOM!"
The world around her suddenly became noisy.
Countless voices flooded into her consciousness all at once.
Fragments of thoughts from everywhere.
The neighbor on the left thinking about what to make for lunch, the words drifting through her mind like smoke.
A child on the street below wondering if it would rain, a dog somewhere nearby feeling hungry but loved playing toss and chase.

Random emotions washed over her in waves. Confusion. Hunger. Sleepiness. Boredom. Excitement. Loneliness. They came from every direction, overlapping and mixing until she could not tell where one ended and another began.
Everything rushed into her mind at once—a tidal wave of unfiltered consciousness from every living thing within range.
"Mmm."
She made a sound of discomfort. She couldn’t feel pain due to Dexter taking her pain away, but she still felt the discomfort.

Lyra instinctively covered her head with both hands. Her fingers pressed against her temples hard enough to hurt. Her face turned pale, and her body curled inward, making herself as small as possible.
Mira immediately wheeled herself forward. Her Spectral Arms reached out, the crimson limbs extending toward Lyra.
"Lyra! What is wrong?"
Selene hurried over as well. She could see Lyra’s body shaking and the rapid pulsing of her heart even from across the room.
Lyra squeezed her eyes shut. The voices became even louder and more insistent.
Dozens of minds pressing against hers simultaneously, all of them unaware that she could hear them.
Then one voice suddenly became clear. Crystal clear. It cut through the noise like a blade through static.
’What’s wrong with her?’
’Is this a backlash?’
Lyra’s body froze.
That voice.
It belonged to Mira.
She recognized the tone. She had heard it 2 years ago, during the expenditure.
Slowly, Lyra opened her eyes.
She looked at Mira without blinking.
Mira frowned.
"What?"
Lyra typed with trembling fingers.
The AI speaker spoke.
"You were thinking about me."
Mira blinked.
"Of course I was. You just collapsed. I am worried about you."
"No." Lyra shook her head firmly, her expression intense.
She typed again.
"I think I heard your thoughts."
"Eh?"
The room fell completely silent.
Selene stared at her in disbelief. Her mouth hung open slightly.
Mira’s pupils contracted.
"What?"
Lyra took a deep breath.
She closed her eyes again.
The strange frequency returned. This time she controlled it and focused it solely on the person sitting directly in front of her, blocking out everything else.
Immediately a stream of thoughts entered her mind.
’Did she really awaken too?’
Lyra opened her eyes again in shock then she unconsciously spoke to them.
’Mira, you just said this in your mind. ’Did she really awaken too? It will be best if all three of us awakened with no one left behind.’’
Mira’s face changed slightly.
"I, I never said those aloud. But I was thinking of them. Which means you’ve also awakened and you can read minds."
She stopped as her eyes widened when she realized Lyra didn’t actually use the AI glasses to speak, she spoke directly into her mind.
Selene was stunned as she also heard Lyra’s voice.
Their eyes widened as they both stared at Lyra as though she had grown two heads.
Lyra only realized after they told her.
’You can hear us and speak now? Your second talent is truly amazing.’
’Since it’s not just reading minds but speaking directly into them, it’s called Telepathy Talent.’
Mira nodded her head with a small smile
Lyra stared blankly at them. She had actually awakened too, and for the first time in two years, she could hear people’s voices and also express herself.

chapters.title: Chapter 73 | First Dungeon
paragraphs: Following the instructor, the group walked deeper into the Hero Association headquarters.
They finally reached a large elevator at the end of a heavily guarded corridor.
Two massive guards stood on either side.The instructor nodded at them and pressed a button on the wall, and the elevator doors slid open.
The instructor stepped inside first. The six candidates followed behind him.
As soon as everyone entered, the instructor pressed a button. -15.
Dexter raised his eyes in surprise.
Only now did he truly notice the enormous list of floors beside the elevator panel.
There were thirty floors above ground, but beneath them, another thirty floors went deep into the earth, from 0 to -30.

It felt like the Hero Association was not just a building but was was practically an underground city. Thirty floors of secrets buried beneath the soil, Dexter couldn’t help but image what was hidden down there.
The elevator doors closed with a soft thud, and immediately the platform began descending.
The whole elevator stayed silent during the fall, nobody speaking.

Perhaps it was because six strangers were trapped together inside a small metallic box. Perhaps it was the knowledge of what waited below. Perhaps it was the simple fact that the earth was pressing in around them and the only direction was down.
Dexter could even hear the breathing of everyone around him.
Behind him, the tall young man crossed his arms impatiently while tapping his fingers against his arm.
The dagger woman leaned lazily against the wall. While the muscular giant remained expressionless.
The quiet girl in the corner lowered her head and said nothing
Meanwhile, Dexter’s thoughts had already drifted elsewhere. Specifically How exactly was he going to find two necklaces similar to the one he had given Mira?
Giving one wife a gift without giving the other two the same gift.
That was simply asking for trouble.
He had already seen the look in Lyra’s eyes when she noticed the necklace on Mira and knew and didn’t know what to think of it. He could only purchase two more similar necklaces for them.
And Selene.
She probably hadn’t noticed the necklace yet. But when she did...
He shook his head and chuckled silently. He had become one of those people scared of their wives. And not only did he have just one. He has three of them.
Forty-five seconds later.
"Ding."
The elevator stopped and the doors slid open.
The six of them stepped outside. Instantly, Dexter’s eyes narrowed slightly as he saw two people staring outside the elevator.
They were guards and their energy wave was extraordinary. They were both
Superhuman Realm heroes!
Dexter couldn’t help wondering exactly how many Superhuman experts existed inside Stargate City.
Because ever since arriving at the Hero Association, they seemed to be everywhere. Guards, receptionists, instructors and even the Maintenance workers.
The instructor stepped forward and showed his identification.
The two guards nodded immediately.
One of them pressed his hand against a scanner. A blue light swept across his palm, reading mana signatures and comparing them against stored data.
The other pressed a massive red button mounted beside the wall.
Rumble.
A gigantic metallic gate, nearly three meters tall, slowly split apart from the middle. The thick steel doors ground open with a heavy mechanical groan.
Behind the gate was a portal floated in midair, a glowing violet portal swirling like a whirlpool made of light.
Dexter’s eyes widened, for this was his first time seeing one. And he was not the only one stunned.

The lady with the dagger stared with sharp interest, her lips parting slightly, her natural curiosity pushing aside her attempt to look professional. The muscular man raised his eyebrows a tiny bit, even the quiet girl could not hide her curiosity,
Only the tall young man and the instructor appeared unaffected.
Clearly, they had seen portals before.
The portal resembled a gigantic glowing amoeba suspended in space, its surface constantly rippling like water touched by a gentle breeze.

Colors shifted endlessly within it: purple, blue, black, silver, all swirling and blending. It looked as though an entire universe had been compressed into a single doorway, stars and darkness and light dancing together in an endless, silent song.
Beautiful and terrifying, the sight was strangely mesmerizing and very hypnotic.
It made Dexter want to reach out and touch it to feel what the portal felt like against his fingertips.

The instructor suddenly spoke "This is a modified F-Rank Dungeon. We have changed parts of it for this licensing examination to match your strength." He turned toward the group. "You will enter as a team. You may cooperate if you wish, or you may act independently. That decision is yours alone."

The instructor reached into a metal case and removed several black wristbands. One by one, he handed them out. The moment Dexter put his on, the band automatically adjusted itself around his wrist. A soft beep confirmed activation, and a tiny light on its surface blinked green once before going dark.

"This is your emergency extraction device. If you wish to leave the dungeon, press the button on the side, and you will immediately be pulled out." His expression became serious, his eyes hard. "However, if you voluntarily withdraw from today’s examination, you will need to wait three months before applying for another Hero License examination."
The candidates’ expressions shifted slightly. Three months was a long time.
The instructor nodded. "Do not throw away your life for pride, but do not surrender too easily either." He stepped aside. "Good luck. Now enter the dungeon."
The candidates looked at one another, nobody moving right away.
Everyone seemed to be waiting for someone else to take the first step.
Just as Dexter was considering entering, Marcus suddenly snorted.
"Cowards."
A confident smirk appeared on his face and without hesitation, he stepped forward.
The moment his body touched the portal, he suddenly disappeared like he had never been there at all.
Fiona clicked her tongue.
"Show off."
She stepped forward next, her figure melting into the violet light.
The muscular giant entered third, walking forward with heavy steps and vanishing without a sound.
The quiet girl followed shortly after, her small form swallowed by the portal.
Only Dexter remained.
He stared at the swirling portal for a few seconds. This was his first dungeon and also his first step into the world of heroes.
Taking a deep breath, Dexter stepped forward. The moment his body touched the violet light, his vision exploded into countless colors, and the world around him disappeared completely.

sentences.text: Following the instructor, the group walked deeper into the Hero Association headquarters.
They finally reached a large elevator at the end of a heavily guarded corridor.
Two massive guards stood on either side.The instructor nodded at them and pressed a button on the wall, and the elevator doors slid open.
The instructor stepped inside first.
The six candidates followed behind him.
As soon as everyone entered, the instructor pressed a button. -15.
Dexter raised his eyes in surprise.
Only now did he truly notice the enormous list of floors beside the elevator panel.
There were thirty floors above ground, but beneath them, another thirty floors went deep into the earth, from 0 to -30.
It felt like the Hero Association was not just a building but was was practically an underground city.
Thirty floors of secrets buried beneath the soil, Dexter couldn’t help but image what was hidden down there.
The elevator doors closed with a soft thud, and immediately the platform began descending.
The whole elevator stayed silent during the fall, nobody speaking.
Perhaps it was because six strangers were trapped together inside a small metallic box.
Perhaps it was the knowledge of what waited below.
Perhaps it was the simple fact that the earth was pressing in around them and the only direction was down.
Dexter could even hear the breathing of everyone around him.
Behind him, the tall young man crossed his arms impatiently while tapping his fingers against his arm.
The dagger woman leaned lazily against the wall.
While the muscular giant remained expressionless.
The quiet girl in the corner lowered her head and said nothing
Meanwhile, Dexter’s thoughts had already drifted elsewhere.
Specifically How exactly was he going to find two necklaces similar to the one he had given Mira?
Giving one wife a gift without giving the other two the same gift.
That was simply asking for trouble.
He had already seen the look in Lyra’s eyes when she noticed the necklace on Mira and knew and didn’t know what to think of it.
He could only purchase two more similar necklaces for them.
And Selene.
She probably hadn’t noticed the necklace yet.
But when she did...
He shook his head and chuckled silently.
He had become one of those people scared of their wives.
And not only did he have just one.
He has three of them.
Forty-five seconds later.
"Ding."
The elevator stopped and the doors slid open.
The six of them stepped outside.
Instantly, Dexter’s eyes narrowed slightly as he saw two people staring outside the elevator.
They were guards and their energy wave was extraordinary.
They were both
Superhuman Realm heroes!
Dexter couldn’t help wondering exactly how many Superhuman experts existed inside Stargate City.
Because ever since arriving at the Hero Association, they seemed to be everywhere.
Guards, receptionists, instructors and even the Maintenance workers.
The instructor stepped forward and showed his identification.
The two guards nodded immediately.
One of them pressed his hand against a scanner.
A blue light swept across his palm, reading mana signatures and comparing them against stored data.
The other pressed a massive red button mounted beside the wall.
Rumble.
A gigantic metallic gate, nearly three meters tall, slowly split apart from the middle.
The thick steel doors ground open with a heavy mechanical groan.
Behind the gate was a portal floated in midair, a glowing violet portal swirling like a whirlpool made of light.
Dexter’s eyes widened, for this was his first time seeing one.
And he was not the only one stunned.
The lady with the dagger stared with sharp interest, her lips parting slightly, her natural curiosity pushing aside her attempt to look professional.
The muscular man raised his eyebrows a tiny bit, even the quiet girl could not hide her curiosity,
Only the tall young man and the instructor appeared unaffected.
Clearly, they had seen portals before.
The portal resembled a gigantic glowing amoeba suspended in space, its surface constantly rippling like water touched by a gentle breeze.
Colors shifted endlessly within it: purple, blue, black, silver, all swirling and blending.
It looked as though an entire universe had been compressed into a single doorway, stars and darkness and light dancing together in an endless, silent song.
Beautiful and terrifying, the sight was strangely mesmerizing and very hypnotic.
It made Dexter want to reach out and touch it to feel what the portal felt like against his fingertips.
The instructor suddenly spoke "This is a modified F-Rank Dungeon.
We have changed parts of it for this licensing examination to match your strength." He turned toward the group.
"You will enter as a team.
You may cooperate if you wish, or you may act independently.
That decision is yours alone."
The instructor reached into a metal case and removed several black wristbands.
One by one, he handed them out.
The moment Dexter put his on, the band automatically adjusted itself around his wrist.
A soft beep confirmed activation, and a tiny light on its surface blinked green once before going dark.
"This is your emergency extraction device.
If you wish to leave the dungeon, press the button on the side, and you will immediately be pulled out." His expression became serious, his eyes hard.
"However, if you voluntarily withdraw from today’s examination, you will need to wait three months before applying for another Hero License examination."
The candidates’ expressions shifted slightly.
Three months was a long time.
The instructor nodded.
"Do not throw away your life for pride, but do not surrender too easily either." He stepped aside.
"Good luck.
Now enter the dungeon."
The candidates looked at one another, nobody moving right away.
Everyone seemed to be waiting for someone else to take the first step.
Just as Dexter was considering entering, Marcus suddenly snorted.
"Cowards."
A confident smirk appeared on his face and without hesitation, he stepped forward.
The moment his body touched the portal, he suddenly disappeared like he had never been there at all.
Fiona clicked her tongue.
"Show off."
She stepped forward next, her figure melting into the violet light.
The muscular giant entered third, walking forward with heavy steps and vanishing without a sound.
The quiet girl followed shortly after, her small form swallowed by the portal.
Only Dexter remained.
He stared at the swirling portal for a few seconds.
This was his first dungeon and also his first step into the world of heroes.
Taking a deep breath, Dexter stepped forward.
The moment his body touched the violet light, his vision exploded into countless colors, and the world around him disappeared completely.

chapters.title: Chapter 74 | Fight! First Wave
paragraphs: The moment the five candidates stepped through the portal, the world around them changed.
The sensation was indescribable.
Dexter felt as though his body had been torn apart into countless tiny fragments before being stitched back together again.
It wasn’t painful like Dexter had thought, but it was deeply unsettling. For a brief moment, it felt as though something foreign was probing his body, his mind, and even his soul.
Then as the feeling appeared, it vanished.
Just like that.
His feet touched solid ground.
"Blurgh!"

Before Dexter could properly regain his balance, his stomach twisted violently. He turned aside and vomited onto the grass. Some of the legendary food he had eaten, wasted just like that. Luckily there essence had been absorbed.
Not far away, the quiet swordswoman, Lena Park, was experiencing exactly the same thing.
Dexter wiped his mouth with the back of his hand. His face slightly flushed and his stomach was still churning but it was bearable.

Lena looked even worse. Her face was completely white. She gripped her sword with one hand while holding her stomach with the other. Her lips were pressed tightly together as though she was fighting a second wave.
Marcus burst into laughter.
"Hahaha! Seriously? You two are vomiting from portal sickness?"
He shook his head with obvious contempt.
"Pathetic."
Fiona rolled her eyes.
"Not everyone has the opportunity to enter a dungeon early like us, Marcus. Im pretty sure yours was words than this."
Gregor merely grunted and said nothing.
Dexter wiped his mouth and took a deep breath.
So this was dungeon transfer sickness.
He had read countless things about heroes and monsters, but somehow nobody had mentioned portal sickness.
’Maybe it’s a running joke between heroes.’
He raised his head and finally looked around.
The dungeon had fully materialized around them.
The air was thick with so much mana it was denser, heavier, and strangely alive. Like breathing in air that had weight.
Each breath filled his lungs with energy that was more potent than anything back in earth.
The five of them stood in the center of a large clearing about 300 meters in radius.
But that clearing was surrounded by towering trees. Thetrees themselves had dense fog covering the forest in every direction.
Tall grass reached all the way to their waists, swaying gently beneath an invisible wind.
Above them hung a single silver moon.
Its pale light illuminated the clearing while leaving the surrounding forest hidden beneath darkness and mist.
Everyone’s expression became solemn.
Marcus immediately stepped forward.
"I’ll take point."
His voice carried unquestionable confidence.
"Gregor, take the rear."
"Fiona, left flank."
"Lena, right flank."
Marcus finally turned toward Dexter, his eyes landing on the F-Rank symbol displayed on Dexter’s temporary badge.
Open contempt flashed across his face. "And you." He smirked.
"Stay in the center."
His tone became colder.
"And try not to get in our way."
The others moved into formation almost immediately. Fiona looked as if she wanted to say something, her mouth opening, then closing.
She glanced at Dexter with an apologetic expression before moving to her position.
Lena frowned slightly, not agreeing with Marcus’s attitude, but she was too quiet to object.
Neither of them spoke up.
Dexter simply stood in the center of the formation.
He was not surprised.
Marcus was a Tier 3 Superhuman, Gregor was Tier 2, Fiona and Lena were Tier One.
Meanwhile, his displayed rank was merely F-Rank.

From Marcus’s perspective, placing the weakest member in the safest position was the logical choice, actually good leadership: protect the weakest link, maximize the team’s effectiveness, play to everyone’s strengths.
’Fine by me.’
The less attention he drew, the better.
The dungeon wasted no time. A long howl suddenly echoed through the fog-covered forest.
"Awooooo!"
A second howl answered it. "Awooooo!"
Then a third. The sounds surrounded them from every direction, not from one point but from everywhere.
The pack was already circling, already hunting, already deciding who would be the first to fall.
Everyone immediately tensed up as rustling sounds came from the tall grass.
Then.
Figures burst from the fog, they were Grey Wolves and 12 of them.
Each stood nearly as tall as a horse and possessed glowing yellow eyes filled with hunger and pure rage.
Their brown fur blended almost perfectly with the darkness. If not for their glowing eyes, they might have been invisible.
[Monster Classification: Mutated Class (1 - 12), Fiend Class (1 - 12), Transcendent Class (1-12), Abomination Class (1 to 4 stars), Calamity Class (1 to 4 stars) and Ender Class (1 to 4 stars) ]

[Hero Classification: Awakened Hero also called Meta Heroes (1 to 12), Super Hero (1 to 12), Ultra Hero (1 to 12), Transcendent (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), Supreme (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), and Legend.]
Marcus narrowed his eyes. "Fiend Class, Level 1 Grey Wolves."
"Graaah!"
The creatures spread out, slowly circling the group as they growled, revealing fangs as spit drooled down their faces.
The wolves continued circling them, strangely waiting and watching.
Suddenly, a louder and sharper howl echoed from deeper within the forest.
"AWOOOOO!"
"Awoo!" "Awoo!" "Awoo!"
Instantly, the entire pack attacked, the wolves exploding forward from all directions.
Marcus face hardened as he roared.
"Kill them!"
The first wolf bristled towards him and Marcus smirked as he clenched his hand.
Immediately, his talent erupted and blue flames exploded in his fist as he struck first at the first Wolf.
"BOOM!"
His fist smashed directly into the skull of the leading wolf, the creature’s head exploding instantly as its body crashed lifelessly into the grass.
Without pausing, Marcus drew his sword, silver flash arced through the air.
"Slash!"
Another wolf collapsed. "Slash!" Then another.
At the same time, Fiona moved like flowing water. Her twin daggers danced through the battlefield.
One wolf lunged toward her throat.
Clang!
She redirected its claws with one dagger while the second blade sliced cleanly across its neck.
Blood sprayed into the air.
Before the body even hit the ground, she had already spun toward another target.
Slash!
A second wolf fell. In the blink of an eye, four out of twelve grey wolves were dead.

chapters.title: Chapter 75 | Second Wave
paragraphs: Gregor was even more brutal.
One wolf jumped toward him. Instead of dodging, he caught the beast by the throat with one massive hand.
"Rawoooo!"
The wolf struggled violently. Its claws raked against his arm causing blood to appeared but Gregor did not flinch.
Instead, he locked the beast neck into a vice grip and slowlydrove his sword through the creature’s neck.
"Crunch."
The wolf whimpered in pain and its body shook violently before itwent limp.
Thw next second, his dropped the dead beast, twisted his waist as he slammed into another wolf’s skull with force.
"Squelch!"
The skull cracked as the beast died instantly.
Lena was the least experienced fighter among them.
The first wolf nearly caught her off guard. She blocked awkwardly, the impact almost knocking her off balance.
Fear flashed in her eyes. But she gritted her teeth and stubbornly glared at the wolf.
Suddenly, she flashed forward and her sword flashed with speed.
The blade sliced across the wolf’s neck before it could realize what was happening, letting blood pour out as the creature stumbled several steps before collapsing.
Meanwhile, more wolves continued rushing towards them.
Marcus, Fiona and Gregor killed them with speed.
Lena slowly found her rhythm and she was able to kill another beast.
Five minutes later, silence returned to the clearing and 12 wolf corpses littered the grass.
Not a single monster remained alive. Blood soaked the ground and the metallic scent hung heavy in the air.
Dexter stood exactly where Marcus had ordered him to stay. He had not even drawn his sword and the wolves had never reached him.
Every monster that came close had been intercepted and killed by the others before he even had the opportunity to move.
"AWOOO!"
The alpha grey wolf was enraged as it charged at them. It’s claws immediately struck out with force.
Gregor’s eyes hardened and he immediately stepped forward with his sheld as he roared
"Parry!"
"Ding!"
The beast paused for a second, Fiona used the opportunity to charge at it and slashed at its ankles causing it too stumble.
Marcus grin widened and he leapt five meters upwards and descended like a meteor.
"Slash!"
The head of the beast was immediately severed into two.
Marcus looked around at the battlefield, breathing hard, and grinned proudly.
"Too easy.
He wiped blood from his sword.
"The first wave is complete."
He rolled his shoulders confidently. "F-Rank licenses secured already."
Fiona wiped blood from one of her daggers before sliding it back into its sheath. "Looks like the first wave really was just a formality."
She glanced toward the dark forest surrounding them. "The second wave should be much stronger."

Gregor silently picked up his shield and tightened the strap around his forearm. Lena carefully cleaned the blood from her sword with a piece of cloth. Her hands trembled slightly from leftover adrenaline.
The first wave had barely lasted five minutes. 13 wolves. 13 corpses. Not a single injury among them.
Marcus glanced back at Dexter and smirked. "Congratulations, F-Rank. You officially contributed absolutely nothing and still earned your Hero License."
Fiona frowned. "Marcus."
He shrugged. "What? The wolves didn’t even get close to him. He spent the entire fight standing there looking pretty."
He paused before adding with a grin, "Actually, scratch that. Standing there looking ugly."
Fiona rolled her eyes. Marcus ignored her. "The least you can do is harvest the Nexus Cores. Otherwise you’ll be completely useless in here."
Dexter looked at the corpses around him and smiled inwardly.
Perfect.
That gave him the perfect excuse. He crouched beside the first corpse and placed his hand against it and curated the Extraction System.
[Extraction Successful.]
+3 Strength
+5 Agility
+2 Mana
+1 Physique
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly with excitement. He quickly moved to the second corpse, then the third, then fourth, fifth. One after another.
[Extraction Successful.]
+2 Strength
+4 Agility
+1 Mana
[Extraction Successful.]
+4 Strength
+3 Physique
+2 Mana
The notifications continued appearing inside his mind. By the time he reached the final wolf, a warm, tingling current surged through his entire body.
His muscles became denser. His bones felt heavier, sturdier. His mana circulation smoothed our and his body had become noticeably stronger.
According to the system, he was still a Tier 3 Superhuman.
However, his physical attributes had risen tremendously. If his previous strength represented an average Tier 3 Superhuman, then his current physical power was already approaching Tier 6 to 7.
Dexter suppressed the excitement in his eyes. This was the main reason why he wanted to enter the dungeon. Because if the extraction system.
The value of dungeons to him was simply absurd.
In his hand rested twelve glowing Nexus Cores.
Looking at the perfectly nearly aplit head of the wolves without bashing the skull in, Marcus sneered. "Looks like you’ve found your calling. You’d make a pretty decent porter."
He crossed his arms. "Honestly, your next dungeon run should probably be as support staff." He laughed. "Carrying luggage suits you perfectly."
"Marcus!"
Fiona glared at him and the turned to Dexter. "Don’t take it personally. He’s always a jerk."
Dexter merely smiled. "I wasn’t planning on taking it personally."
Marcus snorted.
"Ding!"
They watch suddenly rang out as an holographic screen appeared above each device.
[Wave One Cleared.]
[Preparing Wave Two.]
[Preparation Time Remaining: 60 Seconds.]
Instantly, the atmosphere changed and the casual confidence disappeared from everyone’s expressions.
Gregor frowned deeply. "The mana density increased."
Dexter had already noticed.
In fact, he had been the first to notice with his SS-Rank Mana Affinity, which allowed him to sense changes in mana far earlier than ordinary heroes.
The mana floating through the forest was becoming increasingly violent. Even the fog itself began twisting into slow swirls.
Then, a growl echoed through the darkness.
"Grrrrrr."
Another followed.
"Grrrrrr."
Suddenly, pairs of glowing eyes appeared throughout the forest.
Ten pairs, twenty pairs, thirty pairs and the darkness itself seemed alive.
Lena tightened her grip on her sword. "There are more than before."
Fiona’s expression darkened. "A lot more." Marcus slowly nodded. "Formation."
Immediately, everyone moved.
Marcus took the front. Gregor guarded the rear. Fiona moved to the left flank. Lena took the right.
As for Dexter, he remained in the center.
Marcus glanced back toward him and smirked. "Same as before. Stay in the middle and don’t become a burden." Dexter did not reply. He had no interest in arguing.

The mana floating through the forest was becoming increasingly violent.
Even the fog itself began twisting into slow swirls.
Then, a growl echoed through the darkness.
"Grrrrrr."
Another followed.
"Grrrrrr."
Suddenly, pairs of glowing eyes appeared throughout the forest.
Ten pairs, twenty pairs, thirty pairs and the darkness itself seemed alive.
Lena tightened her grip on her sword.
"There are more than before."
Fiona’s expression darkened.
"A lot more." Marcus slowly nodded.
"Formation."
Immediately, everyone moved.
Marcus took the front.
Gregor guarded the rear.
Fiona moved to the left flank.
Lena took the right.
As for Dexter, he remained in the center.
Marcus glanced back toward him and smirked.
"Same as before.
Stay in the middle and don’t become a burden." Dexter did not reply.
He had no interest in arguing.

chapters.title: Chapter 76 | Joining The Battle
paragraphs: The countdown on their wristbands ticked downward.
"BOOM!"
Immediately, the forest exploded into motion as tall grasses bent violently as monsters burst from every direction, the fog rippling as dark shadows raced through it.
This time, they were not ordinary wolves.
These monsters were nearly twice the size of the previous wave, their fur darker, their bodies leaner and more muscular.
Crimson eyes glowed beneath the moonlight while strange markings covered their bodies like natural tattoos, their claws long enough to rival daggers.
Even Fiona’s expression changed.
"Direwolves." Marcus licked his lips as he spoke.
"Level two this time."
There were not merely two or three of them, they were about fifteen.
Then suddenly, another figure stepped out from the forest, and everyone froze.
Unlike the others, this beast stood nearly three meters long, its fur darker than the night itself and seeming to shimmer beneath the moonlight.
Ther was a scar in across its left eyes, while its remaining eye radiating cold intelligence, and the pressure it emitted was on an entirely different level. Gregor’s expression darkened.
"Alpha Direwolf." Marcus cursed immediately. "Damn it."
The Alpha slowly raised its head toward the moon.
"ROOOOOAR!!"
The entire forest trembled.
The fifteen Direwolves moved simultaneously, like soldiers responding to their king’s command, and they charged.
Marcus struck first.
"BOOM!"
His gauntleted fist collided with the claws of the nearest wolf, a shockwave erupting outward as the beast was blasted backward through the grass.
Before it even landed, another wolf lunged toward his throat.
Marcus grinned, his sword flashing. "Slash!"
Blood sprayed into the air as the wolf’s head separated from its body.
"Ocean Flame Erupt!"
"Whoosh!
Blue flames ignited across his blade, as he activated hus Ocean Flame Talent.
The flames wrapped around his sword and intensified its cutting power tremendously.
Another Direwof leapt at him as it struck its cake at Marcus head.
"Whoosh!"
Marcus slashed backwards at the claw and the Ocean flames burned through the claw as the sword easily sliced through the wolf’s body, letting blood spray in the air as it fell tk the ground.
At this moment, Marcus had become even powerful with such a talent.
Fiona pupils dilated as she also didn’t hesitate and activated her talent.
"Time Dilation!"
"Whoosh!"
Everything around her slowed down in her eyes as she processed information at astonishing speed and her body also responded at that same speed.
The wolves becoming sluggish and predictable. Her daggers transformed into silver streaks dancing across the battlefield. As she cut through them rapidly.
Blood erupted everywhere. Fiona moved like flowing water through the battlefield, elegant, precise, and lethal.
Gregor was an entirely different monster. The massive young man roared as muscles bulged beneath his armor, his talent activating.
"Super Strength."
His already terrifying strength increased by over fifty percent.
A charging Direwolf met his shield head-on.
"BOOM!!" The impact shattered the beast’s ribs instantly, and before it could recover, his sword pierced through its neck.
Another wolf lunged toward him, and Gregor simply swatted it away with his shield, causing the wolf to fly several meters before crashing lifelessly into a boulder with a sickening thud.

Lena struggled the most. Her movements lacked experience, and one Direwolf nearly tore open her shoulder. She barely managed to roll away as claws tore through the ground where she had stood moments earlier.
But despite her inexperience, her fundamentals were excellent. She recovered instantly, her sword piercing into the side of the beast’s neck.
"Shink!"
Blood splattered across the grass, and the wolf collapsed.
Meanwhile, Dexter remained standing at the center of the battlefield, watching.
Marcus possessed overwhelming offensive power, Gregor possessed monstrous physical strength, Fiona was incredibly fast and deadly, and Lena lacked experience but had remarkable foundations.
For an ordinary F-Rank team, they were exceptional.
Then, his expression changed. His Danger Sense exploded, every instinct in his body screaming a warning.
Without hesitation, Dexter stepped backward.
"WHOOSH!"
A massive shadow tore through the air where he had been standing a fraction of a second earlier.
"BOOM!!"
The ground exploded, dirt and shattered stone flying everywhere.
Every face in the clearing shifted instantly.
Standing within the crater was another wolf.
No, calling it a wolf felt wrong.
This creature stood nearly three meters tall at the shoulder, jet-black fur covering its body, its claws shining silver beneath the moonlight.
Golden eyes stared coldly at the battlefield, and the pressure pouring from its body alone made Lena’s face turn pale.
Marcus’s confident expression disappeared instantly. "A Level three Fiend monster."
Silence filled the clearing. The wolf slowly rose to its feet, ignoring Marcus, Fiona, Gregor, and Lena.
Its golden eyes locked directly onto Dexter.
The monster’s lips slowly curled upward, revealing rows of razor-sharp teeth.
"Grrrrrr."
A low rumble escaped its throat. For some reason, out of everyone present, it had chosen him. Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "Interesting."
The Third-Star Dire Wolf lowered its body, muscles tightening beneath its dark fur.
Then it vanished.
"BOOM!"
The ground exploded beneath its feet as the beast transformed into a black blur racing toward Dexter at terrifying speed.
Itwas far faster than any of the previous wolves.
Fiona’s expression changed. "Watch out!" But
Dexter had already moved. His hand reached over his shoulder and drew the weapon wrapped in cloth, a beautiful black sword appearing in his hand.
"CLANG!"
Sparks erupted as the Dire Wolf’s claw smashed against Dexter’s blade, creating a shockwave that swept through the clearing and bent the surrounding grass flat against the ground.
Everyone froze in shock. Marcus’s eyes widened, Fiona stopped moving, Gregor stared in disbelief, and even Lena looked shocked.
Dexter had blocked the attack effortlessly, not even taking a single step backward, only the earth beneath his feet shattering under the impact.
They quickly continued their battle but were keeping an eye on Dexter.
The Dire Wolf flipped in mid air and landed several meters away then slowly began circling him.
Its instincts were knew there was something not right about Dexter.
Dexter glanced down at his sword before looking back at the beast, a smile slowly spreading across his face. "So you’re stronger than the others."
His eyes drifted toward the Alpha Wolf standing silently atop the distant boulder. "If this thing is this strong, then how strong is the Alpha?"

chapters.title: Chapter 77 | Alpha Wolf!
paragraphs: Around them, the battle continued. One wolf fell, then another.
Their talents allowed them to hold the line, but the battle was becoming a slow grind. Blood. Sweat. Heavy breathing. The kind of fighting that wore you down inch by inch.
Meanwhile, Dexter’s attention remained fixed entirely on the Third-Star beast before him.
The wolf moved first. Its body blurred. A black afterimage remained where it had been standing.
"Skill: Phantom Moonstep."

A movement skill possessed by elite Dire Wolves. By flooding their limbs with mana, they momentarily merge with their own shadow, allowing them to move with explosive bursts of speed that create afterimages and distort an opponent’s perception.
To weaker opponents, it appears as if the wolf has teleported.
The Dire Wolf reappeared behind Dexter. Its jaws opened wide as it lunged toward his neck.
"CLANG!"
Dexter casually swung his blade backwards and intercepted the bite.
The beast twisted in midair, performing an impossible flip before landing lightly on the ground several meters away.
Before it could move again, Dexter vanished.
The wolf’s instincts screamed. It barely turned its head before Dexter appeared beside it.
His blade shot toward its throat.
The wolf immediately activated Phantom Moonstep once more. Its body dissolved into a blur and reappeared behind Dexter. Its claws flashed toward the back of his head.
"Swish!"
But instead of flesh, it actually hit nothing. The wolf’s eyes widened as it realized it was an afterimage and Dexter had disappeared.
The beast looked around but couldn’t find Dexter.
It’s eyes widened in panic but suddenly it felt a heat sensation above.
Three meters above it, Dexter seem to hovered in mid air with his sword raised, he activated his bloodline talent.
"Flame Slash."
The black blade erupted with crimson fire as Dexter slashed downwards.
A two-meter crescent of blazing energy descended toward the wolf with overwhelming speed.
"Rooooar!"
The Dire Wolf roared and swung its claws toward the attack.
The flames sliced through its claws as though they were paper, then continued onward.
"SHING!"
The beast split cleanly into two halves. Its body crashed heavily onto the ground.
"THUD."
Silence fell across the battlefield. Marcus stared. Fiona blinked. Gregor’s mouth slowly opened. Lena simply looked at Dexter as though seeing him for the first time.
The Tier 3 Dire Wolf had died in less than a minute.
Killed by the supposed F-Rank burden.
Meanwhile the others were still struggling against the remaining beasts.
The battle resumed and the beast fell one after the other until only the Alpha remained. The massive beast stood silently atop the boulder overlooking the battlefield.
Its crimson eyes watched them with intelligence that no ordinary monster should possess.
Even as its entire pack died around it, it never moved and It simply watched.
Then slowly, the Alpha raised its head toward the moon.
"ROOOOOOAR!!"
The entire forest trembled and the fog rolled violently. The mana in the air suddenly became heavier.
Everyone felt it as the pressure increased.
Their eyes narrowed on the alpha.
"Everyone, be vigilant." Marcus suddenly spoke as he locked his gaze in the alpha. Bht he didn’t say anything to Dexter this time.
"Whoosh!"
The Alpha suddenly vanished.. It was as though a drawing wiped clean from a canvas.
Marcus’s face changed instantly. "Where did it go?!"
Gregor reacted first as he activated his skill.
"Guardian’s Will!"
He slammed his shield into the ground. Golden light erupted outward, forming a protective barrier around the group.
Less than a quarter of a second later, a massive shadow appeared before them and a gigantic claw descended beside Marcus.
"BOOOOOOM!!"
The impact shook the entire clearing. The barrier trembled violently as cracks spread across its surface.
"CRACK!"
The shield shattered.
But those precious fractions of a second had been enough.
Everyone immediately flew off with speed.
Marcus leapt backward.
Fiona disappeared in a silver blur. Lena rolled to safety. Gregor threw himself aside. Dust exploded into the air.
The Alpha stood where the barrier had once been. Moonlight reflected off its dark fur. Its body was nearly four meters long.
Silver claws extended from its paws. Its single remaining eye glowed with fierce intelligence.
The scar crossing the other eye somehow made it look even more terrifying. The pressure pouring from it dwarfed every monster they had faced so far.
Marcus swallowed.
"It’s actually a level 5 beast."
Fiona’s face paled. "That’s impossible. Shouldn’t it be level 3?"
Gregor tightened his grip on his shield. Lena unconsciously stepped backward.
The Alpha slowly looked across the battlefield, Then its gaze settled on Dexter.
The beast’s lips curled upward into what almost looked like a smile.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. The Alpha had chosen its prey. And strangely enough, Dexter felt the exact same way.
The Alpha Dire Wolf slowly lowered its body. Its single golden eye remained fixed on Dexter. Marcus tightened his grip on his sword.
"Everyone spread out! Don’t let it trap us together!"
The Alpha’s muscles suddenly tensed. Then, it disappeared.
"Left!"
Dexter shouted.
The Alpha appeared beside Fiona,
Fiona activated time dilation as she immediately reacted with break neck speed.
"BOOM!"
its massive claws crashed heavily into the ground where she had been standing only a moment earlier.
The impact sent dirt and grass flying in every direction. Fiona’s face paled. "That speed is ridiculous!"
Marcus immediately charged forward. Blue flames erupted around his sword. "Blue Flame Slash!"
His blade cut toward the Alpha’s neck. The beast twisted unnaturally in midair and vanished once more.
Phantom Moonstep.
Marcus’s attack sliced through empty air.
"Behind you."
Dexter’s voice came out again and the Alpha reappeared behind him. Its claws descended.
"CLANG!"
Marcus barely turn his body and managed to block.
Even then, he was sent skidding backwards through the grass. His arms trembled violently. "What kind of monster strength is this?"
The Alpha did not stop. It lunged toward Lena next.
Lena’s eyes widened. She raised her sword but she was too slow.
"BOOM!"
Gregor slammed his shield into the Alpha’s side.
The massive wolf was knocked several meters away.
Gregor planted himself in front of Lena. "I’ve got you."
The Alpha slowly stood. Its gaze swept over the battlefield.
Then it raised its head.
"ROOOOOOOAR!"
A wave of mana exploded outward. Everyone felt their bodies become heavier. Their movements slowed slightly. Even breathing felt more difficult. The alpha had activated its crowd control skill.
"Lunar Predator Aura,"

"BOOM!"
The impact drove him to one knee. Cracks spread across the surface of his shield. A second strike followed immediately.
"CRACK!"
The shield shattered and Gregor’s expression changed.
The Alpha opened its jaws to chomp on his head when, silver flashed.
Fiona appeared beside the beast as she activated her Dilation. Everything around her slowed as her daggers struck the Alpha’s shoulder three times in rapid succession.
"Clang. Clang. Clang."
Her face changed as she realized her dagger only death superficial wounds on its boys.
"Rooar!"
The Alpha swung its tail and Fiona was sent flying backwards. She rolled across the ground before stopping herself.
"It has defensive enhancement too?!" Marcus clenched his teeth. "This thing is ridiculous."
The Alpha ignored everyone. Its gaze returned to Dexter. Dexter sighed. "I was hoping to stay low profile."
The Alpha disappeared. Danger Sense exploded inside Dexter’s mind.
Without hesitation, he moved.
"BOOM!"
A claw struck where he had been standing. The earth collapsed inward.
The Alpha appeared beside him. Its claws flashed mutiple times.
Dexter raised his sword.
"CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!"
Shockwaves rippled through the clearing as the others stared with stunned expression.
Marcus could hardly believe his eyes. The Alpha was actually being pushed back. The supposedly useless F-Rank was matching the boss monster head-on.
The Alpha suddenly leapt backwards. Its fur suddenly began glowing crimson.
The mana in the surroundings rushed toward it.
Gregor’s face darkened. "It’s powering up!"
The beast raised its head toward the moon.
"ROOOOOOOOOAR!"
Crimson energy erupted around its body. Its muscles expanded. Its claws grew longer and it eye became blood red. Blood Moon Frenzy. Marcus cursed. "It can still get stronger?!"
The Alpha vanished.
This time even Dexter almost lost sight of it. Almost.
The wolf appeared above him. Its claws descended like falling blades. Dexter raised his sword.
"BOOM!"
The ground beneath him exploded. Cracks spread across the clearing. For the first time, Dexter took a step backwards. The Alpha landed gracefully. Its lips curled upward. It was enjoying this.
Dexter smiled. "So you wanted a real fight."
His grip tightened around his sword. Flames slowly began spreading along the black blade.
The surrounding temperature started rising. Marcus stared. "Fire attribute?" Fiona frowned. "No. That’s not ordinary fire."
The Alpha sensed danger. Its instincts howled.
As it hesitated. For the first time since the battle started, the predator felt fear.
Dexter lowered his stance. The mana around him gathered toward him as Crimson flames condensed on his blade.
The Alpha lunged forward, activating Phantom Moonstep in the blink of an eye.
Three afterimages suddenly appeared around it as Flfour wolves charged simultaneously at Dexter.
Dexter smirked as he casually slashed out horizontally casually.
"Crimson Flame Arc."
The flames expanded into a massive crimson crescent over ten meters wide.
"FWOOOSH!"
The afterimages were slashed into two and they vanished instantly. The real Alpha tried to dodge it it was too late.
The attack crossed the clearing entering deep into the forest and severing mutiole trees behind before it dissipated and turned into more mana.
Suddenly silence followed. The Alpha landed several meters away took two steps forward and then stopped.
A thin line appeared across its chest. The line expanded and with two separated thuds, the beats at body collapsed to the ground.
"THUD."
The dungeon immediately became silent. For several seconds nobody spoke.
Marcus stared blankly, basically everyone had the same expression in their faces. The one they had looked down on was actually the one who killed the Tier 4 beast?
Finally Marcus was able to open his mouth and he spoke. "You’re no F-Rank. You been deceiving all of us, hiding your true strength."
Dexter glances indifferently at Marcus who immediately choked up.
He ignored him and simply went to the corpse of the Alpha Dire Wolf then used extraction on the beast.
[Phantom Moon Step (Rare Grade Skill) Extracted]
[+10 Agility]
Suddenly, the silence was broken by a mechanical voice.
[Wave Two Cleared.]
[Wave Three Beginning In 20 Seconds.]
Everyone froze. Marcus frowned. "Another wave so soon."
Fiona frowned as well.
Gregor’s expression darkened. "And if the second wave already had a Tier-4 Alpha.
Nobody finished the sentence. Because they all knew the answer. If the second wave had a Tier-4 alpha then the third wave would be much much more terrifying.
Marcus immediately raised his wrist. "We leave."
He looked at everyone and they all nodded their heads. Nobody objected. The objective had already been completed.
They had earned their licenses.
There was absolutely no reason to continue. "Alright. Then let’s all press the extraction button and leave."
Marcus pressed the extraction button. Nothing happened. He frowned and pressed again. Still nothing.
Fiona tried hers however, it was also nothing.
Gregor’s expression slowly changed as he clicked his own and it failed. Lena pressed hers repeatedly. Still nothing.
Dexter looked down at his wrist and pressed his own. Silence.
Marcus slowly lowered his arm. "That’s not funny."
Fiona’s face turned pale. "Is this supposed to happen?"
Gregor looked around the clearing. "Not all five at once."
Silence. An ugly answer slowly formed in their minds. Sabotage.
Someone had trapped them inside. Lena spoke for the first time in several minutes.
"We’re trapped." Nobody corrected her. Because she was right.
A deep rumble echoed throughout the forest.
The ground shook and the fog surrounding the clearing suddenly thickened.
The moon overhead slowly shifted color as the white became crimson.
Then came the footsteps.
"Boom. Boom. Boom."
The trees at the edge of the forest trembled.
[Wave Three Initiating.]
The mechanical voice vanished. The world became quiet. Then, the forest exploded.
"CRASH!!"
Trees snapped apart and a gigantic creature burst into the clearing.
It was four meters tall and its body was covered in dark armored scales.
Its claws alone were larger than swords and its crimson eyes scanned the battlefield.
Marcus’s face changed. "Tier 4 Armored Bear."
Before anyone could react, another Armored bear emerged, then another, then another until they were 30 Armored Bear surrounding the clearing.
"30 freaking Armoured Bear? How are we supposed to survive?"
Everyone’s face paled.

chapters.title: Chapter 79 | Get Them Out!
paragraphs: The observation room sat twelve floors above the dungeon floor, enclosed behind reinforced walls and lined with state of the art monitoring equipment.
Ten meter wide rows of screens displayed feeds from various examinations ongoing in different dungeons.
Rachel sat near the back, her eyes fixed on a particular screen. She had bribed her way into this room specifically for this.
Her friend, a frazzled blonde girl with a security clearance smuggled her in for a favour.
She wanted to watch Dexter battle. That was all. She simply wanted to see that man fight with her own eyes.
On the screen, the first wave of beasts poured into the clearing.
Dexter stood among his team, but he didn’t attack and the team seem to be protecting him instead.
Rachel tilted her head, watching and pondering why he was at the middle and the it seemed like the team was protecting him instead.
The other participants engaged the creatures, but Dexter simply observed.
"I have no idea why you came here to watch that weakling. You can teased the favour for something else." Her friend whispered to her.
"Just keep on watching."
She knew better than to think he was helpless from the beginning she knew there was singing different about him.
The first wave ended and the beasts were easily dealt with by the others.
Rachel smiled as the second wave came.
They were the Dire wolves this time, circling the participants with coordinated precision.
It was then she saw Dexter finally move killing both the beta Dire Wolf and the Alpha Dire wolf easily!
Rachel leaned forward in her seat, her grin spreading wide across her face.
"I knew it! I knew he was stronger than he let on."
The blonde girl beside her shot a sharp look and pressed a finger to her lips. "Shh. Keep your voice down. If teh boss knows I snuck you in here, we are done for."
Rachel covered her mouth with one hand and nodded, but the smile did not leave her face.
At the front of the room, the Head Supervisor stood with his arms folded, his gaze locked on the screens.
He was a broad man with a square jaw and a strict behavior.
Around him, several other invigilators monitored their assigned stations, though more than a few of them kept glancing at the same screen Rachel was watching.
They recognized the Ashford bastard and in just a few minutes, there was a quiet wager circulating through the room.
People had placed bets on which wave Dexter’s group would fail. First wave, second wave, third wave, or fourth. A few optimists had even bet on seventh wave.

When Dexter and the others decided to exit the dungeon, the workers who had bet on the first two waves collected their earnings with satisfaction. One man near the left terminal actually chuckled as he pocketed his winnings.
Suddenly. They saw from the feed that the extraction device wasn’t working
The mood immediately shifted.
An invigilator near the center console frowned and tapped his earpiece. "Extraction watch is not responding."
A murmur rippled through the room. The Head Supervisor turned sharply. "What do you mean, not responding?"
"The extraction watches on the participants, sir. They are not activating."
The Supervisor frowned. "Then activate a remote extraction."
The worker immediately got to work but a red alert filled his screen.
"Sir! The system is not acknowledging the command."
The man who had just collected his winnings slowly closed his hand around the money in his pocket. His smile disappeared.
The Supervisor stepped forward, his face hardening as he growled at the workers. "Fix it. Immediately."
Immediately, tens of workers fired at their keyboards.
Three different operators began running diagnostics simultaneously, their faces illuminated by the pale blue glow of their screens.
The room had somehow gone quiet. The only sounds were the tapping of keys.

Thirty seconds passed. Then one of the operators raised his hand without looking away from his monitor. "Sir, it has been sabotaged internally. This is not a system error. The extraction protocol has been deliberately tampered with from inside the watch units themselves."
The silence that followed was intense.
Rachel’s smile vanished. She turned to her friend. "What the fuck does that mean?"
"Calm down," the blonde girl said, though her own fingers had already started moving across her keyboard. "Let me work."
Before anyone could process the implications of the first alert, a second one fired. A sharp, shrill tone cut through the room, and every screen flashed red with a cascading warning message.
[Dungeon 1435: WAVE 3 TRIAL UPGRADED TO WAVE 5 TRIAL.
Every operator in the room went still. The Head Supervisor’s face drained of color. If they could barely handle wave 3 just what would happen in wave 7?
"Sir," another operator said, his voice tight, "the watch protection bubble has also been destroyed. The participants have no defensive barrier active."
The Head Supervisor’s face finally paled.
"Bang!"

"Fix it immediately. We cannot allow this to continue. The others, fine, but if an Ashford dies in this facility, there will be consequences that none of us can survive. Do you understand me? Even the director will not be able to protect us from what the Ashford family would do. Fix this now."
He straightened up and pointed toward the elevator. "Open the gate manually. Send a team down to extract them physically."
Three guards and two technicians immediately moved for the elevator.
Rachel was on her feet before she fully realized she was moving, and she slipped into the elevator just before the doors closed. Nobody stopped her as no one was paying attention to her.
They descended fifteen floors and came down.
At the far end was the heavy arc door, the entrance to the dungeon zone. The lead guard placed his palm on the access panel.
Nothing happened. He tried again. The panel flickered but the door remained sealed.
"Override it," one of the technicians said.
The guard entered a manual code. The panel flashed red. He tried a second code. Red again. He tried a third.
Still nothing.
"Back to the observation room," the lead guard said through gritted teeth. "Now."
When they returned and delivered the news, the Head Supervisor looked as though he might strangle someone.
"Do you understand what happens if Dexter Ashford dies in there?" he growled with gritted teeth.

"The others are expendable. He is not. Find a way to override the system and get a team inside that dungeon. I do not care what you have to do. Hack it, break it, tear it apart if you must. Get them the fuck out."

chapters.title: Chapter 80 | Leaving The Dungeon
paragraphs: Every operator in the room attacked their keyboards like warriors battling in ancient times.
Minutes crawled past like hours as they tried to figure out a solution.
Rachel stood near the back, her hands clenched at her sides, her face flushed red.
She could not hear what the operators were saying anymore as she focused on Dexter who wasthe screen. There were about 30 Armored Bears that had rushed towards them!
Still, Dexter hadn’t move at this point but his teammates were getting injured.
"BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!"
The screen displaying Dexter’s dungeon suddenly went black!
The Head Supervisor face turned extremely dark and he slammed both hands onto the nearest desk.

"What is happening? Is there someone in this building actively sabotaging us? Find them. Find whoever is doing this. We need a scapegoat if this goes wrong. If an Ashford dies here, someone will answer for it. Find a name."
The room descended into controlled chaos.
Operators shouted over one another. Security personnel made calls. The blonde girl beside Rachel was typing so fast her fingers were a blur.
Ten minutes passed.
Ten minutes of black screen and rising panic and the suffocating weight of a family name that could end careers and lives with equal indifference.
Then a voice sharply cut through the noise.
"Sir. I fixed it."
The Head Supervisor spun toward the speaker, a young man at the far right terminal who was staring at his screen with wide, disbelieving eyes. "Activate instant teleportation immediately."

The young man hesitated. His fingers hovered over his keyboard. "Sir, I was not able to restore the instant teleportation function. The sabotage there is too thorough. But I was able to find a weakness in the arc seal on the physical door. I exploited it and forced the arc open. That is the only thing I could do."
The Head Supervisor roared.
"Call the medics to follow me!"
He walked past everyone and headed straight into the elevator. Rachel followed and Two guards Pek Superhumans followed her. They descended in silence.
The lead guard placed his palm on the access panel.
The door opened with a puff sound.
The Head Supervisor did not wait for the guards to go first. He stepped through the arc and into the dimensional zone, and Rachel was right behind him.
They emerged into the clearing and they stopped dead in their tracks, stunned.
Dexter stood in the center of a wide, open space, his chest rising and falling ss he panted.
Blood covered him from head to toe, soaking his clothes, streaked his arms, and dripped from his fingertips onto the grass beneath his feet.
In his left hand, he held the head of a massive beast. The skull was thick, encased in plates of bone armor that gleamed dully in the pale light of the dimensional zone.
It was the head of the seventh tier armored bear. The boss beast. The alpha.
Around Dexter, spread across the clearing in every direction, were the corpses of thirty armored bears.
Some were fourth tier. Some were fifth tier. A handful were sixth tier.
All of them were dead. Sliced, apart, crushed, or simply burnt. The ground was filled with sword scars and craters.
Dexter’s teammates lay scattered behind him.
Marcos was conscious but barely, clutching his left arm, which hung from his shoulder by nothing but tendon and a thin strip of flesh.
Gregor was on his back, a long, savage claw mark carved across his chest, the wound was so deep his white bones could be seen.
Lena lay face down, as a matching claw mark running the full length of her back, her breathing shallow and irregular.
Fiona was sitting upright, which was more than could be said for the others, but her face was utterly bloodless. Her eyes were half closed and her body swayed slightly where she sat.
She had pushed her time dilation ability to its absolute limit, making her look as though she was halfway to death’s door.
Nobody spoke for a long moment.
But Rachel moved.
She walked past the Head Supervisor, past the corpses and the blood and the devastation, and she threw her arms around Dexter.
Dexter went rigid and his mind went blank.

The massive head slipped from his grip and hit the ground with a heavy, wet thud that shook the earth slightly. He stood there with his arms at his sides, unsure of what to do, as Rachel pressed her face against his blood-soaked chest.

"Thank goodness you are alright," she said, her voice muffled against him. "Thank God. Thank goodness you are alright. Are you really alright? Whose blood is this? Is this your blood? Do you need medical attention?"
Dexter cleared his throat awkwardly. "I do not need medical attention. It is not my blood. It is the blood of the beasts."
He gently tilted his head toward his fallen teammates. "But the others are injured. They need medical attention immediately."

Rachel pulled back and finally looked at the ground around them. She glanced indifferently at the others injured. She didn’t care for them so it wasn’t her problem. She was only concerned about Dexter.

The Head Supervisor approached Dexter and placed a firm hand on his shoulder. "It is good that you are alright. We apologize for what happened. The malfunction, the failure of the extraction system, all of it. We take full responsibility."
Dexter frowned. "What actually hap..."

"What the fuck happened?" Marcus roared from the ground, his face twisted in pain and fury. "What the fuck actually happened? Where the hell were you people? We were almost killed in there! You said this was a controlled dungeon! This does not look fucking controlled to me! It went way out of control! I am suing you! I am telling my father to sue every single person in this fucking establishment!"

The Head Supervisor did not flinch. "It was not a malfunction. It was an intentional sabotage. Someone deliberately tampered with the extraction watches, the protection bubbles, and the wave progression system. We have not yet identified the responsible party, but the director himself will personally oversee the investigation. You will receive a full explanation and compensation for what you have endured."

"I do not need medical attention.
It is not my blood.
It is the blood of the beasts."
He gently tilted his head toward his fallen teammates.
"But the others are injured.
They need medical attention immediately."
Rachel pulled back and finally looked at the ground around them.
She glanced indifferently at the others injured.
She didn’t care for them so it wasn’t her problem.
She was only concerned about Dexter.
The Head Supervisor approached Dexter and placed a firm hand on his shoulder.
"It is good that you are alright.
We apologize for what happened.
The malfunction, the failure of the extraction system, all of it.
We take full responsibility."
Dexter frowned.
"What actually hap..."
"What the fuck happened?" Marcus roared from the ground, his face twisted in pain and fury.
"What the fuck actually happened?
Where the hell were you people?
We were almost killed in there!
You said this was a controlled dungeon!
This does not look fucking controlled to me!
It went way out of control!
I am suing you!
I am telling my father to sue every single person in this fucking establishment!"
The Head Supervisor did not flinch.
"It was not a malfunction.
It was an intentional sabotage.
Someone deliberately tampered with the extraction watches, the protection bubbles, and the wave progression system.
We have not yet identified the responsible party, but the director himself will personally oversee the investigation.
You will receive a full explanation and compensation for what you have endured."

chapters.title: Chapter 81 | Registration
paragraphs: Immediately he heard the name Director Klein, Marcus’s mouth which opened to complain immediately snapped shut.
Everyone knew Director Klein was one of the seven Transcendants in the city.
Even Marcus understood that if the director was involved, things would move. The director’s reach was long, and his temper was legendary.
"Medic," the Head Supervisor said into his earpiece. "Get here now."
The medical team arrived in a flash. They poured through the arc door in organized pairs, carrying stabilized stretchers and emergency healing kits.
Healers with active healing talents moved among the injured, their hands glowing with soft, warm light as they knelt beside Marcus, Gregor, Lena, and Fiona.
Marcus was stabilized first, his severed arm carefully secured to prevent further damage. Gregor’s chest wound closed slowly under the healer’s touch.
Lena was rolled onto her side and treated with delicate precision. Fiona was simply lifted onto a stretcher and connected to an IV drip, her eyes already closed.
Dexter was guided toward the medical bay as well.
Dexter tried to wave them off, but the supervisor shook his head.
"No arguments. You might have hidden injuries. Internal damage you can’t feel yet. We need to be certain."
They guided Dexter to the medical bay. Rachel stayed with him every step.
Rachel walked beside him the entire way.

The medical bay was clean and bright, a sharp contrast to the blood and carnage of the clearing. A healer directed Dexter to stand before a large pane of translucent glass mounted in the center of the room.
"Spread your arms," the healer said.
Dexter complied. The glass hummed softly, and a moment later his entire body became visible through the pane as a detailed, three dimensional skeletal and muscular projection.
The healer studied the readouts for a long time, then looked at Dexter with a puzzled expression. "You are as healthy as they come. No fractures, no internal bleeding, no tissue damage, you’re good."
Dexter smiled slightly. "Alright."
Rachel exhaled a breath she had been holding since the clearing and hugged him again.
Dexter stood there, arms at his sides, staring at the ceiling. He had no idea what to do with this girl. He had told her, plainly and directly, that he had three wives.
Most people heard that and immediately backed off. But Rachael seemed even more attached to him.
He gently but firmly extracted himself from the hug and took a step back. "Where do I go to get my license card?"
Rachel stared at him for a moment. Then she erupted into laughter.
"You almost died in there," she said, still laughing, "and the first thing you are worried about is your license card?"
Dexter shrugged. "That is what I came here for."
Rachel shook her head, a wide grin still on her face. "Alright. Let me take you to the licensing hall."
They left the medical bay and walked through a series of corridors that led to a spacious hall with polished floors and a high ceiling.
A single queue stretched from the service counter toward the door.
There were five people ahead of them.
Rachel waited with him this time.
She stood beside him in the line, quiet for once, her earlier panic slowly fading.
Neither of them spoke. They simply stood there, waiting.
Under 10 minutes later, it was Dexter’s turn.
He stepped up to the counter.
The receptionist was a young woman with neat auburn hair pulled into a tight bun and thin reading glasses perched on the tip of her nose.
"Your temporary ID?"
Dexter produced it.
She took the temporary ID card from Dexter’s hand and typed his name into the system. Her eyes moved across the screen, and then they stopped moving.
She blinked. She adjusted her glasses. She read the screen again.
"Mr. Dexter Ashford," she said, her tone shifting. It seemed she saw something.
" You have passed the entry registration exam exceptionally."
She looked up at him over the rims of her glasses. "Also, your potential rating is very high. In fact, let me check the official rankings."
Her fingers clicked across the keyboard. A new window populated on her screen.
"You rank number 9 of the top 10 in the official F Hero rankings. That puts you well within the upper percentile of all F rank Heroes.
Dexter raised an eyebrow but he wasn’t surprised.
The receptionist straightened in her chair and offered a polite smile. "Welcome, Mr. Dexter. Please head through the inner doors for your proper registration."
Dexter nodded and walked past the counter, through a set of frosted glass doors, and into a long corridor.
At the end of the corridor was a single room. The door was open. Inside, a woman stood waiting beside a sleek, modern terminal.
She was truly stunning as she stood there.
High cheekbones, dark hair and calm eyes.
She wore the white coat of a medical professional, but it fit her like it had been tailored specifically for her.
"Good morning," she said, her voice smooth and unhurried. "How are you?"
"Quite alright," Dexter replied.
"Please place your hand on the scanner."
She gestured to a flat, translucent panel mounted on the desk beside the terminal.
Dexter placed his right palm on it. A soft blue light passed beneath his hand, and he felt a faint warmth spread through his fingers as it processed his data.

"Mana signature is being registered," the doctor said, watching the screen. "This is a unique biometric identifier tied to your internal energy. No two signatures are alike. It will be embedded into your license card and used to verify your identity at any licensed facility or checkpoint."
The scan completed. A detailed waveform appeared on the screen, representing the specific frequency and pattern of his mana.
"Next, I will need a retinal scan for visual verification," she said, turning to a small device mounted on an adjustable arm. "Please look straight ahead and keep your eyes open."
Dexter complied.

"Now a small blood sample for genetic archiving," she continued, producing a sterile lancet and a glass vial. "This is standard procedure. The sample is encrypted and stored only for identity verification in the event of disputed license use. It is not shared with any third party."
She pricked his fingertip, collected a few drops into the vial, and sealed it. The entire process took less than ten seconds.
"Lastly, emergency contact information."
