chapters.title: Chapter 82 | You Are The Product
paragraphs: Dexter provided the necessary details. The doctor entered them, reviewed everything one final time, and then pressed a button on the terminal.
A moment later, a small slot beneath the desk whirred to life, and something slid out into a velvet lined tray.
The doctor picked it up and held it out to Dexter.
It was a license card. But it was not the card Dexter had expected.
Most license cards issued to new registrants were F rank, which was standard for first time examinees.
The F rank cards typically came in normal plastics. But for top 10,000, they receive theirs in Iron.
Iron cards for those in top 10,000, Bronze for those in top 1,000, Silver for top 100 and Gold for those in top 10.
This card Dexter was given was pure gold.
’Damn. They really went all out.’
Dexter chuckled in his mind as he looked at the card, then at the doctor.
"The card functions as identification, bank account access, dungeon authorization, mission registration, medical insurance verification, and emergency extraction identification."

She paused and then continued. "The gold card is issued exclusively to top ten registrants. It grants priority access to licensed dungeons, expedited processing at all guild affiliated facilities, and a few additional privileges that will be detailed in the document packet I am about to give you. The gold card also carries Tier 3 clearance—access to classified information and restricted databases that standard bronze and silver cardholders cannot view."

She turned to a folder on the desk and handed him a thick, sealed envelope. "This contains your full registration documents, a handbook of license holder privileges and restrictions, and a directory of training centers, guilds and facilities in your region."

"You will also receive a monthly stipend. Bronze-ranked licensees which is top 10,000 receive 1,000 dollars. Gold, like yours, receives 100,000 dollars monthly." She paused, something flickering in her eyes.
"As for Diamond cards, they are reserved for the top three and receives one million. Individuals like Aurora, for instance."
Dexter eyes widnened slightly when he heard the amount he would receive monthly.
It was insane.
’Hundred thousand dollars for doing nothing? There’s definitely a catch!’
If something is for free then you are the product. It was something that had stuck with Dexter for a long while and he squinted his eyes.
"What’s the catch?"

The doctor smiled prettily. "It’s actually not much. You will be requested to clear an F or E rank dungeon at least 3 times a month and also tasked with immediate response to any dungeon outbreak close to you."
’As expected.’

Dexter chuckled internally. But he wasn’t worried. Since he was getting paid, he would naturally work for the 100,000 dollars. Moreover, to grow stronger, he needed money to spoil his wives and increase his strength.
The doctor continued her speech.
"Your profile is already live on the Hero Association website," the doctor continued.
The doctor then did something that surprised him.
She bowed slightly.
"Congratulations, Mr. Ashford. And welcome to the licensed ranks."
From that point on, the staff treated him differently. Every person he passed in the corridor on his way out offered a nod or a polite greeting.
Dexter moved through it all calmly.
He tucked the gold card into his pocket, held the envelope under his arm and stepped back into the main corridor.
The supervisor from the observation room was waiting for him. Two staff members flanked the man in step.
"Mr. Ashford," the supervisor said, stepping forward. He held out an envelope, thick with documents or credits or both.

"One hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Compensation for the failures during your examination. I know it cannot compare to nearly losing your life, but I hope you can accept it as a gesture of our sincerity."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. These people truly didn’t want him to sue them.
He sighed and took the envelope.
He needed the money, his wives’ needs, his household’s expenses, the constant drain of maintaining even a modest noble lifestyle.
"Thank you."

"When the beast corpses from the examination are processed and sold," the supervisor added, "your share of the profits will be transferred by tomorrow. Standard procedure for participants, but given your... performance, it will be substantial."
Dexter nodded again. "Alright. I’m in a hurry so I will take my leave."
The Supervisor smiled and waved as Dexter left, then his eyes turned cold as he turned back to his staff members behind him.
"How the fuck did you two fail a simple task?"
Rachel was waiting for him in the main lobby.
She had been waiting since he went in. She fell into step beside him as he walked toward the exit.
"You got the gold card," she said. It was not a question. She had known he would eventually get a gold card.
Dexter nodded.
"I knew you would," she said simply.
They walked through the massive front doors of the building and out into the open air. The sun was high and the day was warm.
The garage where Rachel had parked was a short walk across a wide plaza paved with pale stone.
"Let me drive you home," she said. "Or at least to the bus station. Please."
Dexter shook his head. "I need to get some things first. For my wives."
Rachel looked at him for a moment. Then she smiled playfully.
"You really care about them, don’t you? It really makes me wish I was one of them."
Her eyes brightened up as she smirked.
Dexter stared at her with a raised eyebrow.
’What exactly does she mean?’
"Thank you, Rachel," he said, and extended his hand. "For everything today. I will see you around."
Rachel looked at his hand then looked at him.
"You’re truly cruel Dexter."
She took his hand and shook it but didn’t let go as she tilted her head and asked.
"Have you heard of a Finger trap?"
Dexter was a bit caught offguard by the change in subject.
’She’s up to something.’
He slowly nodded his head. "Yes, I’m familiar with it."
She smiled brilliantly and seductively. Her perfectly set, white teeth, pink lips and pink tongue as she licked her lips made Dexters heart trickle.
"The more you struggle..."

chapters.title: Chapter 83 | 250,000 Dollars!
paragraphs: "The more you struggle..."
With that she turned around and left. Her hips swaying seductively in the afternoon sun.
Dexter inhaled sharply and decisively turned away.
"Vixen."
He exited the Hero Association. He didn’t even inquire about Fiona, Gregory, Lena or Marcus, he simply just left.
Once he was a comfortable distance away, he pulled out his phone and opened the map application.
The screen loaded a detailed layout of the surrounding area, his current location marked with a small blue dot. He zoomed out slightly, scanning the nearby streets and districts.
He needed to find a market. His eyes immediately landed on a location.
Stargate Central Market.
Distance: 2.3 kilometers.
Dexter nodded. ’Its within walking distance’
Perfect.
He still needed two necklaces.
If he returned home with a gift for only Mira...
He had a feeling surviving another dungeon would somehow be easier than surviving Lyra and Selene’s jealousy.
He set off at an easy pace, his phone tucked back into his pocket, and allowed himself to take in the city as he moved through it.
The district surrounding the Hero Association building was unlike anything he had seen in the quieter parts of the city.
The buildings here were tall and modern.

Massive billboards clung to the sides of the tallest structures, advertising everything from high-end relic dealerships to serum clinics to luxury fashion brands that Dexter had only ever heard about in passing.

Dexter found himself stopping more than once. He stared at a billboard for a relic manufacturer that depicted a warrior encased in a futuristic glowing combat armor, it looked very masculine and attractive.
Dexter sighed and continued walking.
He enjoyed the walk through the city, forgetting the pain he was feeling at the moment.
By the time he reached his destination, he was satisfied with the sightseeing and he stepped through the entrance of the shop.
The shop was massive. It was a single, large establishment that dealt primarily in relics.
The interior was spacious and dimly lit, with display cases lined up in neat rows along the floor and mounted on the walls.
Each case held items categorized by type and tier.
Simple relics like Type 1 relics occupied the front of the store, like basic mana conductors and low-grade enhancement trinkets.
Further back, the items grew more complex and more expensive.
Type 3 relics sat behind reinforced glass with individual price tags that made Dexter’s eyebrows rise slightly.
The type 4 and type 5 relics were kept in a sealed section at the very back, visible only through a transparent barrier.
Dexter moved through the displays with a specific goal in mind. He was looking for a necklace.
Specifically, a necklace similar to the one he had given Mira.
He had not planned to buy matching jewelry when he gave Mira hers, but seeing the way the Lyra had looked at it, he felt like he needed to.
He searched every display case on the floor.
But nothing matched. There were necklaces, certainly. Pendants, chokers, chains adorned with small relics. But none of them was the same as the one he gave Mira.
He walked to the clerk’s desk. The clerk was a young woman with a patient expression and a name tag that read Elise.
Dexter pulled out his phone, then turned the screen toward Elise.
"Have you seen anything like this in your inventory? Or something similar?"

Elise leaned in, studied the image carefully, and then shook her head. "I am sorry, sir. We do not carry anything like that. The design is quite specific. It looks like it may be a custom piece or from a specialized dealer."
Dexter frowned slightly, thanked her, and left the store.
He stood on the sidewalk outside and looked around.
The advantage of being this close to the Hero Association building was that the surrounding district was packed with specialty stores.

Relic shops, art galleries, fashion boutiques, serum clinics, and medicine shops lined the streets in both directions, each one competing for the attention of the licensed heroes and wealthy patrons who frequented this area.
He spotted a medicine shop two blocks down and entered it.
The woman behind the counter was middle-aged, her eyes scanning Dexter as he entered.
Dexter approached the counter. "I need a month’s supply of Ice suppressant serum. The high quality version, not the standard grade."
The woman raised an eyebrow slightly but did not comment.
She turned to a locked cabinet behind her and retrieved a small box.
"This is the premium grade," she said, placing the box on the counter. "2000 dollars per vial. So 60,000 dollars total. However, we do offer a slight discount for full month purchases. 59,500 even."
Dexter’s eyebrows trembled. He bought something worth 60,000 dollars and all they removed from discount was just 500 dollars? Was the discount even needed?
With the compensation he had received and the monthly stipend for ranking in the top ten, he had about 250,000 dollars but right now 60,000 was gone already.
The cheaper suppressants were unreliable, and he was not about to compromise on something Seven needed.
"I will take it," he said.
As the woman began processing the transaction, Dexter’s thoughts drifted to the pain he was feeling and trying to block out.
He had been managing it for the past few days, pushing it to the back of his mind.
He contemplated on buying pain relief for the girls to relieve himself.
He was considering asking the woman for a mild pain reliever when a notification chimed softly in his mind.
DING!
A familiar notification echoed inside his mind.
[Endurance Buddha Scripture has advanced]
[Second Layer Iron Bones Completed.]
[Third Stage Golden Organs Unlocked.]
Rewards:
→ +100 Strength
→ +100 Agility
→ +100 Physique
→ +100 Mana
Dexter froze.
His muscles trembled as a surge of power flooded his being, within seconds, his body trembled as his strength increased even further.
His body felt light and impossibly dense at the same time, as though every cell had been replaced with something fundamentally better.
Then the sensation faded, leaving his body warm and tingling.
The pain was still there too. But it was different now. As if the Golden Organ stage had created a layer of separation between the pain and his awareness of it.
He could still feel it if he focused on it, but it no longer demanded his attention.
He looked at the woman behind the counter, who was waiting with a packaged box and a receipt. He had been standing in silence for several seconds.
He shook his head slightly. There was no need for the pain relief after all. He was used to the pain, and now, with the Golden organs active, it was even better.
He paid the fifty-nine thousand five hundred dollars, took the packaged box of Ice suppressant serum, and left the medicine shop.

sentences.text: "The more you struggle..."
With that she turned around and left.
Her hips swaying seductively in the afternoon sun.
Dexter inhaled sharply and decisively turned away.
"Vixen."
He exited the Hero Association.
He didn’t even inquire about Fiona, Gregory, Lena or Marcus, he simply just left.
Once he was a comfortable distance away, he pulled out his phone and opened the map application.
The screen loaded a detailed layout of the surrounding area, his current location marked with a small blue dot.
He zoomed out slightly, scanning the nearby streets and districts.
He needed to find a market.
His eyes immediately landed on a location.
Stargate Central Market.
Distance: 2.3 kilometers.
Dexter nodded. ’Its within walking distance’
Perfect.
He still needed two necklaces.
If he returned home with a gift for only Mira...
He had a feeling surviving another dungeon would somehow be easier than surviving Lyra and Selene’s jealousy.
He set off at an easy pace, his phone tucked back into his pocket, and allowed himself to take in the city as he moved through it.
The district surrounding the Hero Association building was unlike anything he had seen in the quieter parts of the city.
The buildings here were tall and modern.

Massive billboards clung to the sides of the tallest structures, advertising everything from high-end relic dealerships to serum clinics to luxury fashion brands that Dexter had only ever heard about in passing.
Dexter found himself stopping more than once.
He stared at a billboard for a relic manufacturer that depicted a warrior encased in a futuristic glowing combat armor, it looked very masculine and attractive.
Dexter sighed and continued walking.
He enjoyed the walk through the city, forgetting the pain he was feeling at the moment.
By the time he reached his destination, he was satisfied with the sightseeing and he stepped through the entrance of the shop.
The shop was massive.
It was a single, large establishment that dealt primarily in relics.
The interior was spacious and dimly lit, with display cases lined up in neat rows along the floor and mounted on the walls.
Each case held items categorized by type and tier.
Simple relics like Type 1 relics occupied the front of the store, like basic mana conductors and low-grade enhancement trinkets.
Further back, the items grew more complex and more expensive.
Type 3 relics sat behind reinforced glass with individual price tags that made Dexter’s eyebrows rise slightly.
The type 4 and type 5 relics were kept in a sealed section at the very back, visible only through a transparent barrier.
Dexter moved through the displays with a specific goal in mind.
He was looking for a necklace.
Specifically, a necklace similar to the one he had given Mira.
He had not planned to buy matching jewelry when he gave Mira hers, but seeing the way the Lyra had looked at it, he felt like he needed to.
He searched every display case on the floor.
But nothing matched.
There were necklaces, certainly.
Pendants, chokers, chains adorned with small relics.
But none of them was the same as the one he gave Mira.
He walked to the clerk’s desk.
The clerk was a young woman with a patient expression and a name tag that read Elise.
Dexter pulled out his phone, then turned the screen toward Elise.
"Have you seen anything like this in your inventory?
Or something similar?"
Elise leaned in, studied the image carefully, and then shook her head.
"I am sorry, sir.
We do not carry anything like that.
The design is quite specific.
It looks like it may be a custom piece or from a specialized dealer."
Dexter frowned slightly, thanked her, and left the store.
He stood on the sidewalk outside and looked around.
The advantage of being this close to the Hero Association building was that the surrounding district was packed with specialty stores.

Relic shops, art galleries, fashion boutiques, serum clinics, and medicine shops lined the streets in both directions, each one competing for the attention of the licensed heroes and wealthy patrons who frequented this area.
He spotted a medicine shop two blocks down and entered it.
The woman behind the counter was middle-aged, her eyes scanning Dexter as he entered.
Dexter approached the counter.
"I need a month’s supply of Ice suppressant serum.
The high quality version, not the standard grade."
The woman raised an eyebrow slightly but did not comment.
She turned to a locked cabinet behind her and retrieved a small box.
"This is the premium grade," she said, placing the box on the counter.
"2000 dollars per vial.
So 60,000 dollars total.
However, we do offer a slight discount for full month purchases.
Dexter’s eyebrows trembled.
He bought something worth 60,000 dollars and all they removed from discount was just 500 dollars?
Was the discount even needed?
With the compensation he had received and the monthly stipend for ranking in the top ten, he had about 250,000 dollars but right now 60,000 was gone already.
The cheaper suppressants were unreliable, and he was not about to compromise on something Seven needed.
"I will take it," he said.
As the woman began processing the transaction, Dexter’s thoughts drifted to the pain he was feeling and trying to block out.
He had been managing it for the past few days, pushing it to the back of his mind.
He contemplated on buying pain relief for the girls to relieve himself.
He was considering asking the woman for a mild pain reliever when a notification chimed softly in his mind.
DING!
A familiar notification echoed inside his mind.
[Endurance Buddha Scripture has advanced]
[Second Layer Iron Bones Completed.]
[Third Stage Golden Organs Unlocked.]
Rewards:
→ +100 Strength
→ +100 Agility
→ +100 Physique
→ +100 Mana
Dexter froze.
His muscles trembled as a surge of power flooded his being, within seconds, his body trembled as his strength increased even further.
His body felt light and impossibly dense at the same time, as though every cell had been replaced with something fundamentally better.
Then the sensation faded, leaving his body warm and tingling.
The pain was still there too.
But it was different now.
As if the Golden Organ stage had created a layer of separation between the pain and his awareness of it.
He could still feel it if he focused on it, but it no longer demanded his attention.
He looked at the woman behind the counter, who was waiting with a packaged box and a receipt.
He had been standing in silence for several seconds.
He shook his head slightly.
There was no need for the pain relief after all.
He was used to the pain, and now, with the Golden organs active, it was even better.
He paid the fifty-nine thousand five hundred dollars, took the packaged box of Ice suppressant serum, and left the medicine shop.

chapters.title: Chapter 84 | Purchasing CloudWeave Bed
paragraphs: The jewelry store next door was larger than the relic shop he had visited earlier.

The air was different here. The display cases near the entrance held rings and earrings, but Dexter walked past them without a second glance. He moved deeper into the store, until he reached the necklace section at the far end.
He still couldn’t find it.
Then he pulled out his phone, opened the image of Mira’s necklace again, and walked to the clerk’s desk.
The clerk was a woman also. Dexter turned the phone screen toward her.
"I am looking for something that matches this," Dexter said.
The clerk studied the image on Dexter’s phone for a long time.
"This is a type three relic, possibly type four," she said in a professional tone.

"Pieces like this do not circulate through standard retail channels. They are typically commissioned by the major families. The Ashfords, the Vances, the Hargroves. When items of this caliber are produced, they are reserved for the wives and daughters of those households. You would not find one in a public shop."
Dexter’s frown deepened. "What about the auction houses?"

The clerk shook her head slowly. "Even at auction, a piece like this would draw fierce bidding from the major families. A private individual without family backing would find it nearly impossible to secure. I am not saying it is impossible, but it would be very, very difficult."
Dexter was quiet for a moment.
"Can I get an imitation?" he asked.
The clerk’s expression tightened. She glanced toward the front of the store, then back at Dexter. "I am not supposed to discuss that,"
She said quietly. "Recommending imitation goods to a customer is against store policy. I could lose my position."
Dexter held her gaze for a moment, then reached into his pocket. "Two thousand. Just for the information."
The clerk frowned and shook her head.
"Three thousand."
She shook her head again, but this time she did not step back.
She did not walk away. She stood exactly where she was, her fingers resting on the edge of the display case, her eyes flickering with something that was not quite refusal.
"Five thousand," Dexter said.
The clerk was still for several seconds.
She looked at the floor, then at the ceiling, then at the front of the store where a manager was visible through the glass partition, sorting through inventory paperwork.
Then she looked back at Dexter and gave a small, slow nod.
"There is a place," she said, her voice barely above a whisper. "About an hour from here, east of the commercial district, past the old warehousing blocks. Tell them Mara sent you."
Dexter smiled as he nodded. "Thank you."
The clerk smiled, tilting her head slightly, and said, "You are welcome. Please come back and purchase more items if you wish. I am always here to help."
Dexter pursed his lips and rolled his eyes.
She was shrewd. Five thousand for a sentence, and now she was already angling for a return visit that might bring more. But she knew her business, and he could not fault her for that.
He turned and left the store without another word.
The black market was an hour away, and he fully intended to go there.
But on his way, he passed a building that caught his attention.

It was a furniture store, but not the ordinary kind. The storefront was wide and grand, with large display windows showcasing elegantly arranged room sets that looked like they belonged in a mansion rather than a retail floor.
The sign above the entrance readCelestine Home, and beneath it, in smaller script,
Furnishings for the Extraordinary.
Dexter paused. He wanted to purchase beds for the girls and himself so he went inside.
As expected, it looked really nice. A sales representative approached him with a polite smile, but Dexter waved her off and headed straight for the elevator.
"Which floor has the beds?" he asked as the doors closed.
"Third floor, sir."
The third floor opened into a long, wide gallery lined with beds.
Dozens of them. They ranged from simple platform frames to elaborate four poster designs with canopies and carved headboards.

Each bed was made up with premium linens and arranged in its own small vignette, complete with nightstands, lamps, and accent pillows, as though inviting the customer to imagine falling asleep right there in the store.
Dexter walked the length of the gallery, scanning each option. Queen sizes, king sizes, California kings.
He sat on several of them, testing the firmness, but they didn’t meet his requirements.
Then he reached the end of the gallery and found a bed that stopped him in his tracks.
It was a king size platform bed with a low, sleek frame made from dark ironwood, a material so dense that it was rumored to be slightly resistant to mana.
The frame alone was striking, but the mattress was what commanded attention. It was thick, easily a foot and a half deep, and it had a slight iridescent quality to its surface,
Dexter sat down on the edge.
The mattress yielded beneath him like sinking into warm water.
It was soft, impossibly soft, but it did not collapse.
There was structure beneath the softness that rose up to meet his weight and distribute it evenly, so that he felt supported and cradled at the same time.
He shifted his weight, leaned back, and felt the mattress adjust to the new position without a sound.
No creaking. No springs pressing against him. Just a smooth, effortless conformity to his body.
A female assistant appeared at his side. She was tall and composed, with her hair pulled back in a neat ponytail and a tablet clutched against her chest.

"That is the Cloudweave Sovereign," she said, a note of pride in her voice. "The mattress is constructed from layered Cloudwool sheared from lunar rams, which are raised on the high altitude pastures of the northern mountain ranges. Cloudwool is naturally temperature regulating, hypoallergenic, and possesses a unique cellular structure that distributes pressure so evenly that it eliminates virtually all contact stress on the body. The inner core is made from compressed essence silk, which provides the structural support. The outer covering is woven from moon thread, which gives it that slight shimmer you are seeing."

chapters.title: Chapter 85 | Black Market
paragraphs: Dexter head was almost exploding with all the information she was dropping.
He ignored her and simply ran his hand across the surface. It was smoother than most things he had touch.
But never smoother than Mira...
"This bed has been extremely popular among licensed heroes,"
The assistant continued. "In fact, it is the same model used by Blitz, the speed star herself. She endorsed the Cloudweave line after our parent company became one of her sponsors."
Dexter glanced to the side and saw the advertisement mounted on the wall beside the bed.

It showed Blitz, the renowned female Ultra hero, seated on the edge of an identical Cloudweave Sovereign, her silver hair catching studio lighting, one hand resting on the mattress with an expression of casual satisfaction.
The caption beneath read, "Even the fastest need the best rest. Cloudweave by Celestine Home."
Dexter was not particularly impressed by celebrity endorsements. But the bed itself was another matter. He could already imagine how the girls would react to sleeping on something like this.
They would love this bed.
"How much?" Dexter asked.
The assistant smiled but did not answer immediately.

She tapped something on her tablet, scrolled, tapped again, and then looked up at him with the particular expression that salespeople wore when they were about to deliver a number they knew would provoke a reaction.
"Thirty thousand dollars," she said.
Dexter stared at her.
"Thirty thousand," he repeated flatly.
"Yes, sir."
"For one bed."
"The Cloudweave Sovereign is a premium product, sir. The materials alone...
"Is it made of heavenly clouds?" Dexter asked, his voice perfectly calm but his eyes slightly wider than usual. "Because I genuinely do not understand why a single bed costs thirty thousand dollars."
The assistant covered her mouth with one hand and shook her head as though Dexter had made the most charming joke she had heard all week.
Dexter sat on the edge of the Cloudweave Sovereign and said nothing.

He was not joking. In a world where people could manipulate fire, bend the earth to their will, and tear holes in the fabric of space, it was not unreasonable to wonder whether someone with the ability to shape the sky could fashion a bed from actual clouds.
He kept the thought to himself, however, because explaining it would only prolong a conversation he did not want to have.

He calculated Two beds would cost sixty thousand. It would drain his money as he still needed to prichasw a lot of things like foodstuffs, ingredients and jewelries for the girls., but it was workable.
He made his decision.
"I will take two," he said.

The assistant’s smile widened. She tapped furiously on her tablet, her earlier laughter replaced by the brisk efficiency of a closing sale. "Excellent choice, sir. If I may ask, will you be taking them with you today, or would you like them delivered?"
"Delivered," Dexter said. "What is the timeline?"
"Standard delivery is next day. However, we do offer an expedited option for an additional five thousand dollars, which would have them at your address within four hours."
Dexter shook his head. "Next day is fine."

The assistant nodded and guided him through the purchasing process. He provided his address, confirmed the delivery details, and signed the digital receipt. The total came to exactly sixty thousand dollars.
The assistant printed a physical copy of the receipt, placed it inside a sleek Celestine Home folder along with a care guide for the Cloudwool mattress, and handed the package to him with both hands.
"Thank you for your purchase, sir. We are certain the ladies in your life will be very pleased."
Dexter took the folder, tucked it under his arm alongside the medicine shop packaging, and left the store.
The walk to the black market took just under an hour. Dexter followed the directions the jewelry clerk had given him,
He found the iron door at the end of a narrow alley between two warehouses.
’I hope this isn’t some organ trafficking thing.’
Dexter opened it and stepped inside.
What he found was not what he had expected.

He had imagined something dark. Something dangerous. An underground marketplace lit by flickering torches or bare bulbs, where shadowy figures conducted illicit business in hushed tones and everyone watched everyone else with suspicion.
What he got was a thrift market.
It was a massive complex. The interior was open and well lit by overhead fluorescent panels, with wide aisles that crisscrossed between rows of stalls and tables and makeshift display areas.
Traders sat behind their wares, calling out to passersby in the same loud, casual voices that vendors used in any open air market anywhere in the city.
Come look at this. Best price in the complex. You will not find this anywhere else, my friend.
The goods on display were where the difference lay. On a table near the entrance, a woman was selling type one relics, small trinkets and minor enchantments laid out on a faded cloth.
A few stalls down, a heavyset man with a thick beard had arranged a collection of type two weapons on a rack, each one tagged with a handwritten price card.
Further in, Dexter spotted type three items, including a set of gauntlets that faintly hummed with stored energy, and a shield that seemed to absorb the light around it.
But it was the stall near the far wall that made Dexter stop.
A man sat cross legged on the floor. His eyes were closed as though he were meditating rather than selling goods. In front of him was a blade.

It was a type 3 blade. Dexter could tell from the way the air around it seemed to bend slightly, the faint distortion that indicated a high concentration of refined mana sealed within the weapon’s structure.
Dexter was stunned, but not because of the blade.
He was stunned because the blade was sitting out in the open, unguarded, on a cloth mat on the floor of a black market, with the seller’s eyes closed and his attention clearly elsewhere.
A type 3 blade was worth a fortune. In the hands of a capable fighter, it could dramatically alter their combat capabilities.
There were people in this very complex who would kill for a weapon like that, so why exactly was he puttingvthebwepaon out there just like that?

chapters.title: Chapter 86 | Purchasing Tea
paragraphs: There were people in this very complex who would kill for a weapon like that.
Yet no one touched it. No one even approached the stall closely and their was even a wide space around the man.
People kept casting glances at the blade and then at the seated man, and then quickly moving on.
Dexter looked at the man more carefully. He was lean, with sharp features and dark hair that fell past his shoulders.
His clothes were plain.There was nothing about his appearance that immediately announced who or what he was.
But Dexter felt a faint pressure that was almost imperceptible as it distorted space around him.
’Ultra rank hero!’
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly. He had never seen an ultra rank hero in person before but he heard they were vastly powerful compared to Meta humans and Superhumans.
And he was sitting cross legged on the floor of a black market, selling a type 3 blade with his eyes closed.

Dexter could not make sense of it. An ultra rank hero had access to the Hero Association’s most exclusive resources. They could join various guilds receive funding, equipment, and support that ordinary licensed heroes could only dream of.
They were recruited the moment their rank was confirmed, courted by factions and organizations that competed for their allegiance.
An ultra rank hero could walk into any weapon dealer in the country and receive preferential treatment, the kind that came with VIP status and unlimited credit lines.
So why was this man sitting on the floor of a black market, selling a single type 3 blade to strangers?
Dexter stood there for a long moment, watching the meditating ultra rank hero,
’Forget it.’
Then he shook his head slightly, filed the mystery away for another time, and moved on.
He had come here for a specific reason, and staring at an ultra rank hero was not going to help him find an imitation necklace for his wives.
Dexter moved through the black market, checking stall after stall.
The first nine sellers either did not carry imitation jewelry or the quality of their work was so poor that even a casual glance would reveal the deception.
One man tried to sell him a necklace that was clearly just spray painted copper, and Dexter had to suppress the urge to drag the man by his collar to the nearest mirror.
By the tenth stall, he found what he was looking for.
The seller was a quiet woman with gray streaks in her hair and a display case that was noticeably better organized than her neighbors.
Inside, arranged on black velvet, were several pieces of imitation jewelry that actually resembled their higher tier counterparts.
They lacked the mana signature, durability, but visually, they were remarkably close.
Dexter pointed to a necklace that shared the same design elements as Mira’s. It was a type 1 necklace.
"I will take this."
The woman nodded and reached into the case.
Before Dexter could breathe a sigh of relief, the trader at the neighboring stall leaned over.
He was a short man with a wide grin and eyes that darted between Dexter’s face and the wallet in his pocket with the subtlety of a hungry dog watching a steak.

"My friend, my friend," the trader said, sliding around the edge of his own stall and inserting himself into the transaction with practiced ease. "You are buying for a lady, yes? Just one necklace? No, no, no. This is not how you impress a woman. You need the full set."
He produced a pair of earrings from his stall and held them up to the light. They were type one, modest in quality, but they caught the fluorescent light prettily.

"Look at this. Perfect match for the necklace. The same design language, the same finish. A woman notices these things, my friend. She sees the necklace and she thinks, where are the earrings? Where is the bracelet? You do not want her thinking you only care enough to buy one thing."
Dexter frowned. "I do not need..."
"And this," the trader continued, already reaching behind him, producing an anklet with a delicate chain and a small charm at the center.

"For the ankle. Very popular right now. All the fashionable ladies in the city are wearing them. And this bracelet, look, see the workmanship? This is not cheap garbage. This is quality type one craftsmanship."

The trader was relentless. Every time Dexter tried to decline, the man produced another item, held it up, explained why it was essential, why the girls would expect it, why buying just the necklace was somehow an insult to the very concept of gift giving.
He moved between his stall and the woman’s stall grabbing items from both displays and assembling them into an ever growing pile on the counter.
Dexter stood there, caught in the current of the man’s sales pitch, and realized with a distant sort of irritation that the trader was right about one thing.
He did not know what girls liked. He had no idea what they preferred, what they secretly wanted, what small things might make their day better.
He knew their personalities. But not the specifics of what brought them joy in the small, everyday sense.

By the time Dexter extracted himself from the trader’s gravitational pull, he had spent 20,000. Necklaces, earrings, anklets, bracelets, finger rings, and hairpins that the trader had slipped into the pile when Dexter was not looking.
The man had smiled the entire time, that wide, greedy grin that said he knew exactly what he was doing.
Dexter left the stall angrily.
He knew he had been manipulated. It was his own fault for not walking away sooner.
He put it behind him and walked towards where food stuffs were been sold.
The section smelled of earth and green things, cut grass and dried bark and the faint, sweet scent of flowers that had been set out in small buckets near the entrance.
Dexter moved through the herb section first.
Tea herbs lined one entire row, sorted by variety and origin.
Calming blends for sleep and relaxation sat beside energizing blends for morning routines.
Meditation aids, awareness enhancers and, aphrodisiac blends!
Dexter swallowed as he saw it but immediately removed his gaze.

chapters.title: Chapter 87 | Psychological Welfare
paragraphs: Dexter’s eyes drifted across the black market as he walked, scanning the stalls and tables without any particular purpose.
Then they stopped.
The ultra rank expert was still there.
He sat in the same position as before, cross legged on the floor, eyes closed while the type three blade lay there before him.
He then checked the weapon closely and saw it was incredibly beautiful.
The sword body was very dark but it was also incredibly beautiful.
It wasn’t flashy at all, nor was it dull
It looked more like elegant.
The steel had a faint silver sheen that seemed to shift depending on the angle, like moonlight on still water.

It was, without question, designed for a woman. It wasn’t decorated with much jewels or covered in elaborate engravings. In fact, its appearance was remarkably simple. Yet that simplicity made it elegant. The slender blade, graceful guard, and perfectly balanced design gave it a quiet beauty that would undoubtedly appeal to women.
More importantly...
It was a Type-3 Relic.
A weapon powerful enough to greatly enhance its wielder in battle.
The more Dexter looked at it, the more certain he became.
The girls would absolutely love this...
Dexter paused.
He should keep walking. He had already spent far more money than he had planned to spend.
The jewelries he purchased was enough and adding more expenses would be irresponsible.
But he was like a gambler. Just one last purchase. One last 100x investment opportunity.

Dexter stood there for several seconds, warring with himself. The rational part of his mind told him to walk away. The irrational part, already calculating his rewards and the smile on his girls faces.
The irrational part won.
’I bet the price would scare me away.’
He adjusted the bags under his arm and walked toward the trader.
He stopped in front of the cloth mat and looked down at the blade. Then he looked at the man.
"How much?" Dexter asked.
The man did not open his eyes. His response came in a voice that was low and unhurried, carrying the particular gravity of someone who had no need to rush anything.
"I am not selling it."

Dexter frowned. If you are not selling it, then what are you doing here? The question rose in his mind, but he kept it behind his teeth. Questioning an ultra rank hero’s choices seemed like a poor way to start a conversation.
"In that case, never mind."
Just as he turned to leave—
"I am not selling it," the man repeated, and this time his eyes opened, "but I am exchanging it for certain items."
Dexter paused mid turn. He looked back at the man over his shoulder and blinked his eyes thoughtfully. Then replied.
"What item do you wish to exchange it for?"
"A grade three heavenly material."
Dexter went still.
Heavenly materials. Heaven and earth treasures are rare treasure.
Unlike weapons, which could be used repeatedly and passed from owner to owner, heavenly materials were consumable.
They could only be used once, their power expended in a single moment of transformation or enhancement.
And because of that single use limitation, they were valued above almost everything else.
Obtaining a type three relic weapon was difficult but achievable. Enter a high grade dungeon, defeat the creatures within, and there was a chance, however small, of finding one.

But heavenly materials were different. They did not appear in dungeons with any reliability. They were found in places so dangerous that the mortality rate for expeditions was measured in percentages rather than fractions.
People died for grade three heavenly materials and here was an ultra rank hero, sitting on the floor of a black market, asking for one in exchange for a single type 3blade.
"No one in their right mind would trade a Grade-3 Heaven and Earth Treasure for a single Type-3 weapon."
The man’s eyes flashed, "Does not mean you do not have one."
Dexter met his gaze without flinching. "Maybe I do. Maybe I do not.
The man snorted, a sound of dismissive amusement, and closed his eyes again. The conversation, as far as he was concerned, was over.
Dexter stood there for a moment, then smirked. "Alright. It is your choice if you want to miss this opportunity. Who knows when the next one will come."
The man’s nostrils flared slightly. He inhaled, as though testing the air for something, then shook his head without opening his eyes. "You are bluffing. You do not have a grade three treasure."
"It is up to you whether you want to miss this opportunity or not," Dexter said, and this time he actually turned and started walking.
He did not look back in the slightest. Behind him, he could sense the man’s attention pressing against his back.
But Dexter simply kept walking.
"...Fine."
Dexter stopped walking.
A faint smile flashed across his lips before disappearing.
When he turned around again, his expression had become completely calm.
The man was looking at him now, his eyes open and it was obvious he was frustrated.
"What else do you want to exchange for the grade three treasure?" Dexter asked.
The man’s jaw tightened further. "I have one more weapon with me. I will exchange all two for the treasure."
Dexter shook his head reading three of his fingers. "Three grade three weapons."
The man’s expression darkened as his nose flared. "Why do you not just put a blade to my neck and steal it instead?"
"Three weapons or nothing," Dexter replied with indifference. "I don’t need the weapons. But it seems you need the trwaure. So what’s it gonna be?"
"Do you want to rob me?" The man’s voice had dropped.
Dexter sneered. "You have no other choice. You can exchange, or I leave. Those are your options."

The man leaned forward slightly, and the pressure in the vicinity intensified to the point where Dexter could feel it pressing against his skin like a physical force. "I could simply take it from you."

Dexter did not move. "Do you think I am dumb enough to bring a grade 3 heavenly material into a black market, in front of an ultra rank hero, without any protection? Of course I did not bring it with me. I left it somewhere safe. This is my first time in this place. Bringing a treasure here would be asking for death, and I am not seeking death anytime soon."

chapters.title: Chapter 88 | Buying Weapons For The Girls
paragraphs: The man’s eyes narrowed. For a long moment, the two of them stared at each other, the air between them thickened as the man glared at him.
Then the man exhaled slowly, and some of the pressure receded.
"Fine. Three weapons. Bring me the treasure."
Dexter frowned slightly. He had expected more resistance. But the man accepted so easily.
"Are you lying to me?" Dexter asked. "I am fairly certain no one has three type three weapons just lying around. If this is some kind of trick..."
The man flipped his hand.

Two more weapons appeared out of nowhere, materializing in midair and dropping to the cloth mat with soft thuds. One was fiery red like flames and the other gleamed with a silver so bright it seemed to glow.
Together with the original black blade, three type three weapons now lay on the mat in front of the ultra rank hero.
Dexter was stunned.

He had been toying with the man. He had pushed for three weapons specifically because he thought the demand was unreasonable enough that the man would refuse, and refusal would have been a clean exit.

He had not expected the man to agree. He had certainly not expected the man to produce the weapons on the spot, as though pulling out three type three relics was as casual as pulling out pocket change.
But the weapons were there and also real enough.
Dexter made a decision.
"All right," he said.
He flipped his hand, and a small orb appeared in his palm.
It was perhaps the size of a walnut, but it was different and looked really nice.
The surface shimmered with colors that seemed to exist outside the normal spectrum, shifting and flowing in patterns.
A grade 3 heavenly material.
The man’s eyes locked onto the orb with an intense hunger and his pupils shrank.
"A storage relic..."
His breathing became noticeably heavier.
So that was why...
No wonder he couldn’t smell the treasure on him. The young man has a Quantum Ring.
Dexter smiled faintly.
"Now you know why you couldn’t smell it on me."
The man’s gaze darkened for a brief moment.
For the first time...
Killing intent flickered deep within his eyes.
If he eliminated Dexter now...
Both the treasure and the storage relic would become his.
However—
Dexter simply stood there smiling.
Come on.
Try to take it.
See what happens.
The man stared at Dexter for a long, tense moment. He burst into laughter.
"Hahaha!"
"I nearly forgot myself."
"As an Ultra-ranked hero..."
"...breaking my word over greed would be truly disgraceful."
He accepted the Grade-3 Heaven and Earth Treasure before pushing the three relics toward Dexter.
"The deal is complete."
Dexter stored the three weapons inside his storage relic before smiling politely.
"Thank you. Thank you for the treasures."
The man waved a dismissive hand. "Thank you as well. It has been a long time since I encountered someone interesting in this place."
Dexter chuckled. "I will take that as a compliment."
"You should," the man said, closing his eyes again and returning to his meditative posture. "Now leave. You have what you came for, and I have what I came for. We are done."
Dexter nodded and left without hesitation.

Next was the food section. Dexter filled a basket with essentials: rice, flour, cooking oil, spices, fresh vegetables, meat, eggs, milk, and butter. He added dried fruit, honey, bread, and a few things he thought the girls might enjoy. By the time he finished shopping, the basket was overflowing.

He set everything down on a bench near the edge of the marketplace and took a moment to rest. Bags and bundles surrounded him in a small mountain of purchases. Pulling out his phone, he checked his remaining balance.
There was not much left but he still had enough to manage for a few days, but nothing more.

For a moment, he considered buying a vehicle. Nothing expensive, just something in the five to ten thousand dollar range to make getting around easier for him and the girls. It would save time and spare them from relying on public transport.
But the money from the dungeon kills was not here yet.
The payment for the beasts he had killed in the examination dungeon would arrive eventually. Thirty-one Armored Bears, including a Seventh-Tier boss. The money alone would be substantial.
He could wait.
Dexter abandoned the idea of buying a vehicle for now and started the walk home, carrying as many bags as he could manage.

The change from the marketplace district to his neighborhood was gradual. The streets narrowed, the buildings became shorter and older, and the smooth pavement gave way to cracked concrete and uneven patches.
It was rough around the edges, but not dangerous.
This was a working-class neighborhood. Quiet and lived-in. Far removed from the gleaming streets surrounding the Hero Association, yet comfortable in its own way.
A few stray dogs wandered the sidewalks, sniffing lampposts and ignoring passersby.
Dexter walked past a repair shop where a mechanic worked beneath the hood of a sedan, a convenience store with a faded sign, and a laundromat with steam-covered windows.
Then he passed a bakery.
It was a small shop wedged between a pawn shop and a closed pharmacy. The display window was modest, holding a few cakes beneath glass domes and a chalkboard listing the day’s specials.
But the smell drifting from the open door was irresistible.
Warm butter, vanilla, caramelized sugar, and toasted nuts filled the air.
Dexter stopped.
The girls would definitely like sweets.
Standing on the sidewalk with his arms full of shopping bags, Dexter made up his mind.
He shifted the bags to one arm, pushed open the door with his shoulder, and stepped inside.
The warmth hit him immediately.

Soft golden light filled the bakery, reflecting off cream-colored walls and polished wooden shelves stocked with preserves, specialty flour, and bundles of dried herbs that looked more suited to an apothecary than a bakery.
But it was the display case that captured his attention.
It stretched across the entire counter, filled with pastries unlike anything Dexter had ever seen.
The bottom shelf held Cloud Biscuits, pale pastries hovering just above their trays and glowing faintly.
Baked with refined cloud wheat flour. Levitation effect lasts approximately three minutes after removal from packaging.
Beside them sat Starfruit Tarts with deep violet crusts and fillings that swirled with gold and silver like miniature galaxies.

For a moment, he considered buying a vehicle.
Nothing expensive, just something in the five to ten thousand dollar range to make getting around easier for him and the girls.
It would save time and spare them from relying on public transport.
But the money from the dungeon kills was not here yet.
The payment for the beasts he had killed in the examination dungeon would arrive eventually.
Thirty-one Armored Bears, including a Seventh-Tier boss.
The money alone would be substantial.
He could wait.
Dexter abandoned the idea of buying a vehicle for now and started the walk home, carrying as many bags as he could manage.
The change from the marketplace district to his neighborhood was gradual.
The streets narrowed, the buildings became shorter and older, and the smooth pavement gave way to cracked concrete and uneven patches.
It was rough around the edges, but not dangerous.
This was a working-class neighborhood.
Quiet and lived-in.
Far removed from the gleaming streets surrounding the Hero Association, yet comfortable in its own way.
A few stray dogs wandered the sidewalks, sniffing lampposts and ignoring passersby.
Dexter walked past a repair shop where a mechanic worked beneath the hood of a sedan, a convenience store with a faded sign, and a laundromat with steam-covered windows.
Then he passed a bakery.
It was a small shop wedged between a pawn shop and a closed pharmacy.
The display window was modest, holding a few cakes beneath glass domes and a chalkboard listing the day’s specials.
But the smell drifting from the open door was irresistible.
Warm butter, vanilla, caramelized sugar, and toasted nuts filled the air.
Dexter stopped.
The girls would definitely like sweets.
Standing on the sidewalk with his arms full of shopping bags, Dexter made up his mind.
He shifted the bags to one arm, pushed open the door with his shoulder, and stepped inside.
The warmth hit him immediately.

Soft golden light filled the bakery, reflecting off cream-colored walls and polished wooden shelves stocked with preserves, specialty flour, and bundles of dried herbs that looked more suited to an apothecary than a bakery.
But it was the display case that captured his attention.
It stretched across the entire counter, filled with pastries unlike anything Dexter had ever seen.
The bottom shelf held Cloud Biscuits, pale pastries hovering just above their trays and glowing faintly.
Baked with refined cloud wheat flour.
Levitation effect lasts approximately three minutes after removal from packaging.
Beside them sat Starfruit Tarts with deep violet crusts and fillings that swirled with gold and silver like miniature galaxies.

chapters.title: Chapter 89 | The Bakery And Tessa
paragraphs: Nearby were Ember Rolls, their glossy surfaces glowing with a soft red warmth while wisps of steam rose from them despite being fully baked.
Infused with low-grade fire essence. Maintains ideal eating temperature for up to six hours.
The middle shelf displayed larger creations.
There was a Mooncake the size of a dinner plate, its surface patterned like lunar craters and its filling visible beneath translucent dough that shimmered like moonlight.
Next to it stood the Dewdrop Tower, a layered cake of pastel colors crowned with edible crystal clusters that scattered tiny rainbows across the glass.
The top shelf held the premium items.
Phoenix Feather Pastries rested inside a lacquered box, each one shaped like a flame-colored feather.
Produces a gentle warming sensation from throat to chest.
And beside them sat ten pastries unlike anything else in the display.
They were round and roughly the size of a fist, their golden crust threaded with a faint shimmer as though strands of light had been woven into the dough itself.
Through small openings in the top, a pale cream filling could be seen shifting between white and gold depending on the angle.
A handwritten card rested against the plate.
Celestine Dew Pastry. Family Recipe. Limited Batch.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
His mouth watered as he stared at the display case like a man who had lived on plain bread all his life and had suddenly wandered into a royal banquet hall.
"Dexter?"
The voice came from behind the counter.
He tore his gaze away from the pastries and looked up at the girl standing there.
She was about 15 years of age, with auburn hair tied in a messy bun dusted with flour and an apron smeared with vanilla cream. She wiped her hands on a towel and smiled at him with easy familiarity.
It took him a second to recognize her.
"Tessa," he said. "Hey. How have you been?"

"I’m actually doing alright," Tessa replied, leaning against the counter. "Though I feel I should be asking you that question. How are you doing after the monster outbreak and the attack at your home?"
Dexter shrugged and replied.
"I’m quite alright."
Tessa nodded. "What about your wives? Are they okay too?"
Dexter nodded in reply. "Yeah. They were not affected by the beasts."
"I thought the damage to your place made you move away from the area. When I heard about the monsters attack, I tried seeing you but you weren’t around so I figured maybe you left the neighborhood. "
Dexter shook his head.
"No. The Hero Association stepped in and moved me and my wives to a hotel while the repairs were being done."
Tessa’s eyes widened slightly.
"That explains the construction noises. I thought your building was being renovated."
"In a way, it was.
She laughed.
"Fair enough. My dad and some of the neighbors were worried about you."
Then a mischievous grin spread across her face.
"Though I guess I won the bet."
Dexter head tilted slightly and he blinked.
"What bet?"
"The neighborhood betting pool after the attack."
She held up five fingers.
"Some people thought you ran away. I said you didn’t. Looks like I just made five thousand dollars."
Dexter stared at her.
The neighbors had started a betting pool on whether he had fled.
Not whether he was safe or whether he needed help, it was whether he had run.
"The audacity of my neighbors," Dexter muttered.
Tessa laughed.
"What can I say? They’re quite entertaining when you get to know them."
A reluctant chuckle escaped him.
"Well, congratulations on the win."
Then he glanced back toward the display case.
"So, what’s good here?"
Tessa immediately pointed toward the top shelf.
"The Celestine Dew Pastries. Family recipe."
Her expression brightened as she spoke.

"The dough uses sun wheat flour grown on the eastern mountain slopes, and the filling is made with dew nectar harvested from dawnflowers. The ingredients are difficult to get, so we only make a small batch each day."
She pointed at the porcelain plate.
"And that’s the last batch."
Dexter looked at the pastries.
There were exactly ten left.
"I’ll take all ten.
Tessa froze.
"All ten?"
"All ten."
Lyra always ate more than everyone else, and if there were not enough to go around, she would be the first to notice.
Besides, if they tasted even half as good as they looked, everyone would want seconds.
Ten was not excessive.
Tessa laughed and reached for a pastry box.
"You really don’t do things halfway, do you? Most people buy one or two. You walk in and buy the entire batch."
With care, she placed each pastry into its own compartment before tying the box shut with a ribbon.
Dexter watched quietly as the scent of bread, vanilla, and warm sugar filled the air around him.
For a brief moment, despite the bags digging into his arms and the lingering ache in his body, everything felt peaceful.
Tessa set the box on the counter.
"There you go. Ten Celestine Dew Pastries."
She smiled.
"Tell me what the girls think."
"I will."
Dexter picked up the box carefully.
"Thanks, Tessa."
Tessa rested her elbows on the counter.
"So, how’s training to becoming a hero going?"
Dexter shifted the bags in his arms.
"Pretty well."
"Pretty well," she repeated.
Then she tilted her head.
"That’s funny, because I can’t sense you anymore."
Dexter’s expression remained calm, but his attention sharpened.
"It’s strange," Tessa continued. "Before, I could always sense and feel your strength."
She tapped the counter.
"Now there’s nothing much. It’s like you’re not even here."

chapters.title: Chapter 90 | Being Followed
paragraphs: Dexter’s strength had grown tremendously after improving his bloodline to Ancient Grade and also advancing to Gold Organs, the second stage of the Eternal Endurance Buddha Scripture.
Though he had not tested his limits yet, he estimated that his raw physical power was comparable to a 9th-tier superhuman, perhaps even peak knight tier.
Yet Tessa said she couldn’t sense him much.
She shouldn’t have been able to sense him at all. The Ancient Grade Chaos Flame Demon bloodline made sure of that.

Being part demon, one advantage was concealment. He gained the ability to conceal his energy waves from leaking out, yet Tessa said she couldn’t sense him much, meaning her strength had definitely surpassed Ultra rank.
Dexter kept his expression neutral.
An ultra-rank hero at her age should have been impossible. She looked no older than sixteen.
Reaching superhuman status took years of training, and advancing to ultra-human required even more talent, resources, and dedication. Most ultra-rank heroes were at least in their forties or fifties.
Yet the evidence was difficult to ignore.
Dexter filed the thought away.
"Where is your dad?" he asked, changing the subject.
Tessa straightened. "He went out for an errand. He should be back tonight."
Dexter nodded. "Greet him for me when he returns." He had never seen her dad, but he knew she wasn’t lying about him.
"Alright," she said with a small smile.
Dexter turned to leave, then remembered something.
"The old woman who sits in front of our building," he said. "Was she one of the people who placed the bet?"
Tessa’s smile became wry.
"Old lady Lucy? Yes."
"What did she bet?"
"Against you. Everyone did. I was the only one who bet that you wouldn’t run."
Dexter was silent for a moment before laughing.
"Then I suppose I should thank you for defending my honor, lady Tessa."
Tessa waved a hand.
"No need. I already got my reward. I can buy many things with 5000 dollars."
Dexter chuckled.
Several customers had entered the bakery during their conversation, and the staff was attending to them.
"I’ll see you later," he said.
"Come back soon."

Dexter pushed open the door and stepped into the afternoon air. The scent of fresh pastries faded behind him, replaced by the familiar smells of the neighborhood. Adjusting the bags in his arms, he started walking.
After about fifteen meters, he stopped.
Nothing had changed. The street remained quiet, with a few stray dogs wandering near a distant lamppost.
Yet something felt wrong.
It wasn’t a sound or a sight. It was a faint pressure at the edge of his awareness—the unsettling feeling of being watched.
And it was moving.
Someone was following him.
Whoever it was moved without sound or presence, blending into the surroundings so perfectly that they seemed part of the air itself.
Dexter continued walking, pretending not to notice.
A thief?
Unlikely.
Thieves were not this skilled, nor did they carry this subtle sense of danger. Well, not if you’re Batman’s parents.
Dexter turned into a narrow alley between two buildings. The afternoon sun barely reached inside, leaving the passage cool and shadowed.
There, he stopped.
Setting the bags against the wall, he slipped into the deepest shadow and waited.
Five seconds, ten seconds. Twenty.
But nothing.
No footsteps. No movement.
Frowning, Dexter unsheathed his blade as he focused hard, pouring mana into his eyes and activating his enhanced hearing talent; he extended his senses, stretching them to the max.
Even then, he couldn’t find a trace of the person.
Either the person was hiding without using energy, or their concealment was beyond his ability to detect.
He calmed his nerves and sheathed back his blade.
"You can come out now. I already know you’re following me."
Silence.
No response.
A thread of doubt crept into his mind.
He had barely slept in days due to the pain of sharing his wife’s pain, so he resorted to cultivation.
Maybe it was the exhaustion from that, and he was imagining it.
Maybe the pressure was lingering tension from the dungeon.
Exhaling slowly, he turned toward the bags.
However, it was at that moment that l the air shifted.
There was no flash of light or burst of energy.
One moment the space ahead was empty.
The next, it wasn’t.
A woman stepped out of nowhere as though emerging through an invisible curtain.
She wore a dark cloak that covered her from neck to ankle.
The fabric seemed to absorb light, making her appear almost like a living shadow. Her hood hid most of her face, though Dexter caught a glimpse of dark, practical clothing beneath.
She stood three meters away from Dexter, observing him as she said nothing.
The pressure Dexter had sensed since leaving the bakery exploded in intensity.
It wasn’t killing intent or harmful intent. It was just a curious interest.
Dexter’s mind rapidly spun—an Ultra human.
At the very least, maybe even stronger.
An ultra-human expert had been following him.
The woman smiled, an amused expression on her face.
"Relax," she said calmly. "I’m not here to kill you. If I wanted you dead, I could have killed you the moment you left the Hero Association."
Dexter didn’t lower his guard immediately, but her words sank in.
Since the Hero Association.
She had followed him through the streets, the black market, the shopping district, his neighborhood, and even the bakery. Yet he had never sensed her.
She was right. If she had intended to kill him, he would already be dead.
After a moment, Dexter pocketed the Type 3 hidden weapons.
The Flame Demon transformation retreated into its sealed state, no longer on the verge of exploding. He took a slow breath and forced himself to relax.
"Who are you?" he asked.
The woman lowered her hood, revealing long violet hair and matching violet eyes. She looked about his age, but with softer skin and a pretty figure.
"You don’t know who I am?" she asked.
Dexter studied her face. It seemed familiar.
Then he remembered. He slapped his palm and smiled.
"You’re that old man’s wife," he said. "The one I saw on the hotel balcony."
The lady was greatly stunned, and she actually choked on her own spit.

chapters.title: Chapter 91 | Spar With Me
paragraphs: "What the hell is running through your head?" she huffed and glared at him
Dexter rubbed the back of his head and chuckled embarrassedly. "I had no idea. That was why I said it. I did not know who you were."
The girl rolled her eyes with the most sass Dexter had ever seen. "I am his granddaughter, you idiot. That old geezer is almost five hundred years old. There is no way I am his wife."
Dexter nodded his head. "Right. Granddaughter, not wife."

But he was a bit surprised to hear that the old man was 500 years old. The old man still looked energetic, even more energetic than him, and he was nearly five centuries old. That explained a great deal about his presence and his power.

But then he remembered that this was the granddaughter the old man had used as a wager back then. Luckily for the old man, Dexter had rejected the marriage for his granddaughter as part of the wager; otherwise, it would have been something else.
’But what exactly is she doing here?’
Calming her nerves, the girl’s expression turned serious, and she stepped closer.
Her eyes glinted as she stared at him up and down as though she could see through him, and then her gaze settled on the base of his neck.
Her eyes suddenly brightened, and she stared intently at his neck, muttering.
"The old geezer really did give you the necklace."
Dexter blinked and unconsciously touched the necklace on his neck. ’Was she here for this?’
She looked at Dexter’s eyes and then said slowly.
"Can I have the necklace back?"
Dexter frowned. His hand moved unconsciously to his neck, where the necklace the old man had given him rested against his collarbone.
"Does the old man want it back?"
The girl tilted her head and slowly shook her head. "No. He said you won it fair and square. But you do not deserve to wear that key."
Dexter’s frown deepened. "The old man gave it to me. He knows perfectly well whether I deserve it or not. It is not your place to decide if I’m worthy of it or not."
If she had asked properly, he might have shrugged and given her the necklace. He didn’t know what it was, and she was the granddaughter of the old man.
But the way she asked irritated Dexter instead.
The girl’s face changed, and her eyes narrowed.
For a split second, the color of her eyes changed from violent to pure gold.
At the same split second, a wave of heat gushed outward like a volcano erupting.
And for that same split second, the hair on Dexter’s neck stood on end, and he felt a surge of something immense and terrifying brush against his awareness.
She held his gaze for a second, but Dexter felt it was an hour.
But just as she was about to do something, she shook her head, the gold fading from her eyes as they returned to their usual violet, and let out a deep breath.
Dexter sighed in relief. If they had truly battled here, it would be an insane battle, and Dexter had no idea who would come out on top, but he knew she would at least lose a layer of skin.
The lady rolled her eyes indifferently as she asked a question.
"How did you manage to learn Grand Cosmos?"
Dexter inhaled deeply and raised an eyebrow. "Was it really that difficult?"
The girl’s eyelid trembled. Dexter truly knows how to press her button.
Her eye twitched. "You have no idea what you are talking about."
Dexter frowned. "I’m positive I do since I learnt the technique fully."
The girl inhaled deeply, her chest rising and falling as she visibly tried to calm herself. Dexter could practically see her blood pressure rising.
He was not entirely sure why his responses were aggravating her so much, but he was not going to change them to make her feel better.
"The key would only cause you endless trouble. You should give it to someone who knows how to protect it."

Dexter shrugged. "You, me, and your grandfather are the only ones who know I have it. I won’t say anything, and I’m pretty sure your grandfather won’t either. That only leaves you. As long as you don’t say anything, I will be fine."
The girl gritted her teeth as she heard Dexter’s response.
"How about you tell me what this is and I will consider giving you or not." Dexter smiled deviously.
The girl glanced at him with her white eyes. "Even if I told you, you wouldn’t understand."
Dexter shrugged. "It was worth a try.
He then waved at her. "Alright. Enough chat. I need to go home."
He was walking when he realized the girl was walking with him.
Dexter frowned. "What do you want now?"
"Until I get my hands on the necklace, you are not leaving my sight." The girl suddenly smiled as she cracked her neck and stretched, making her large breasts pop out even more.
’What the hell is this girl talking about? Am I about to have my own personal stalker?’
"Do what you wish." With indifference in his tone, he replied.
The girl raised an eyebrow and smirked.
"Don’t think I won’t follow you to meet your wives."
Dexter’s face changed slightly. But he wasn’t worried because he had the Tier 4 protection.
"What would it take to leave me alone?" He sighed.
The girl’s eyes lit up. "Give me the —"
She wasn’t able to talk for long when Dexter cut her off. "Impossible, ask for another thing.
The girl glared at him for a second then spoke.

Dexter’s chuckle faded, replaced by a flat look. "You are an ultra rank. Possibly higher. How exactly is that supposed to be a fair fight? I’m not egoistic enough to think I can battle across realms."
The girl shook her head, and a small smile returned to her face. "Relax. I will suppress my power down to your level. I will spar with you at the same strength. What do you say?"

Dexter considered it. Part of him was genuinely curious. He had never fought an ultra rank before. He had never even been in the same room as one until today, and now he had encountered two or possibly three in a single afternoon.
The opportunity to experience what it was like to face someone at that level, even with their power suppressed to match his own, was tempting. He wanted to witness the power of an Ultra.

But then he shook his head and pushed the urge down. There was no logical reason to accept. He had nothing to gain from the spar itself, and the risk, however small with her power suppressed, was still present.
He had better things to do than indulge the strange whims of a five hundred year old man’s granddaughter.

"There is no need," he said. "I see no reason to spar with you. If I agree, you leave me alone. If I do not agree, what? You follow me forever? At some point, you will get bored and leave regardless."
The girl frowned, clearly not expecting his refusal.
She had probably assumed that the offer itself would be enough, that the chance to spar with an ultra rank would be too tempting for any young fighter to pass up.
She did not understand that Dexter did not operate on the same assumptions as other people his age.
"How about I give you twenty thousand dollars?" she asked.
Dexter frowned. "Twenty thousand dollars to spar with you?"
But he shook his head. "No."
The girl’s frown deepened. She thought he was being difficult. Unreasonable. "Everybody has a price," she said.
"Not me."
"Twenty thousand."
Dexter shook his head.
"Thirty thousand."
He shook his head again.
"Forty thousand."
No.
"Fifty thousand."
No.
"Seventy thousand."
Dexter was unmoved.
The girl smiled. "Eighty thousand."
Dexter shook his head slowly. "Do not bother."
"Two hundred thousand."
"6565436786 Starsoul Bank"
The girl was stunned. She had thought Dexter was a man of pride and honor, expecting him to refuse, but he actually caved in.
Her lips curled as she glanced at him with a glint in her eyes.

"The two hundred thousand is for when you win. I never said when I was going to give it to you. You asked me the condition for sparring, and I told you two hundred thousand. You agreed. You never asked if I was going to give it to you beforehand or whether it was conditional on winning."

Dexter was startled. That was true. He looked at the girl; a faint smile was on his lips and a hint of amusement in his eyes. "That is true. It is actually not your fault. I should have asked for clarification."
"When are we doing this?" he asked.
"Anytime you are ready," the girl replied.
Dexter thought for a moment. "I am ready right now."
The girl frowned and looked at him, then at the bags of food and items scattered on the ground behind him. "You are serious. What about all your food? It will go bad."
Dexter shook his head. "If I go home, it will take a while for me to come back out. So we do it now, or we do it tomorrow."
The girl paused, considering. Then she nodded. "Tomorrow is fine by me. So long as you keep your promise."
Dexter nodded. "I do not like to break promises. I try to keep them when they are within my power."
The girl gave him one last look, something unreadable in her violet eyes. Then she turned around.
In a single step, she vanished.

Not walked away. Not moved quickly. Vanished. One moment she was there, and the next moment the space where she had been standing was empty. No sound. No displacement of air. No trace that she had ever been there at all.
Dexter stood in the corridor for a long moment, staring at the space.

"Ultra rank," he muttered to himself. "They have the power of teleportation. Teleportation to anywhere within their line of sight. That is one of the signature abilities of the ultra rank. Unlike superhumans, whose visible capabilities are limited to..."
He trailed off and shook his head. He was talking to himself in an alleyway about power classifications. That was a sign that he needed to go home and rest.
He turned back, picked up the bags of food and items and the box of pastries, and continued walking toward his apartment.
The house was quiet when Dexter pushed open the door. He felt something was a bit off compared to when he left, and he frowned.
"Did something happen to the girls?"
He quickly set the bags down just outside the entrance and quickly entered inside.
What he saw stunned him.
