chapters.title: Chapter 93 | Back At Home [1st GT & Gift Bonus - s]
paragraphs: An extremely massive mansion lay within an ever stretching estate that radiated wealth and power.
Deep within the mansion was a massive room with toys and figurines of superheroes lined the shelves in countless rows.
And at the center of it all sat a thirteen years old, hunched over a desk, his pen moving steadily across paper as he did his assignments.
Soft music played in the background. The kids head bobbed rhythmically to the beat, completely absorbed in his work, oblivious to the world around him.
It was at that moment something happened.
The space itself seemed to fracture, the void rippling like disturbed water until it tore open.
From within that shifting void, a figure emerged and he stepped silently into the room, appearing directly behind the boy.
The kid didn’t seem to notice him as he continued bobbing his head to the music, writing his assignments, lost in his own world.
The man, however, did not advance further as his eyes glinted when he stared at the back of the youths head.
Suddenly —
THUD!
His knees hit the ground as he fell on his knees, bowed his head to stare at the ground as his body trembled violently like a kid caught stealing meat from the pot at midnight.
It was a shocking sight!
An ultra-rank expert actually kneeling on the ground, trembling before a thirteen-year-old boy as though he were a god.
He said nothing, it was as though he did not dare.
The boy continued working on his assignment as minutes passed.
Ten, twenty, then thirty.
For nearly half an hour, the man remained face-down on the floor, motionless except for his trembling body, waiting. The boy’s pen never stopped. His head never ceased its nodding to the music.
Finally, the youth yawned and stretched lazily then he set his pen down.
His eyes lifted from the assignment, but he did not turn to the man. Instead, he reached toward the speaker beside him and adjusted the music, changing the track with a casual flick of his fingers.
Suddenly, he spoke in a childish, almost playful tone.
"You failed."
The words hung in the air like a death sentence.
The man’s face drained of color instantly. Sweat erupted across his brow, his body pressing harder into the floor as though the weight of those two words had physically crushed him.
"Voss," the boy continued, his voice still carrying that unsettling youthful lightness. "You truly disappointed me."
Without hesitation, Ross threw himself onto the floor, prostrating so deeply that his forehead struck the polished marble.
"I... I deserve punishment, Sire," Ross said, his voice trembling.
Despite being an Ultra-Rank expert capable of making countless people kneel with a glance...
His breathing turned ragged. An ultra-rank expert, reduced to a trembling wreck by a child’s words.
It was a shocking sight.
The boy ignored him. He bobbed his head to the new track playing through the speaker,
His hands flying as he pretend rap to follow the music. The Ultra rank expert didn’t dare to live as he waited patiently.
The youth finally stopped fake rappinb and he chuckled as he said in an amused tone.
"Think Voss, and give me a reason why you failed. You have only ten words to save your filthy life."
Ross slowly lifted himself from the floor but did not stand fully. He remained on his knees, head bowed, as he reached into his clothing and produced a phone.
The phone screen was cracked and pathetic.
He quickly played a video and spoke with trembling tone.
"Here’s my reason, Sire."
He stretched out his hands towards the kid. The kid turned with a raised eye brow and took the phone from his hand.
He played it the video.
The recording showed an unclear figure using a single flaming strike killing a dark cloth man and then using flame breathe to kill another man.
The image wasn’t clear, the resolution poor and low quality but the events were unmistakable.
The figure who was Dexter had killed the assassins one after the other.
The boy’s eyes finally left the screen.
He turned to look at Ross for the first time.
Dexter pushed open the front door and stepped inside. Almost immediately, he stopped.
Something was wrong.
The moment Dexter stepped through the front door, he stopped.
A faint smell lingered in the air and Dexter immediately recognized it was smoke.
The smoke had been cleared but the smell of burnt stuffs could still be smelt.
Dexter sniffed the air before frowning.
Someone tried cooking...
His first thought was that the girls must have gotten hungry while he was away.
"I’m home," he called out.
Receiving no reply, he walked into the living room and the sight that greeted him made him pause.
The three girls were seated on the couch, Selene, and Lyra while Mira was seated in her wheelchair, beside them.
They weren’t watching television nor were they cultivating.
They were just sitting there, side by side, staring directly at him.
The three girls stared at him without blinking, It was as though they had been waiting for him.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "You guys need something for me?" he asked, his tone casual despite the strangeness of the scene.
Mira said nothing. Her expression remained flat, unreadable.
It was Selene who spoke first.
"Yes," she muttered in a small voice. "We were waiting for you."
Dexter blinked, puzzled by them suddenly caring about him and replied. "I’m alright. The licensing went really well with no accident." Of course he was lying through his teeth.
Changing the subject. "Did you girls cook something?" he asked with concern.
"Were you hungry? You should have just asked me to make something for you."
Mira rolled her eyes.
"We tried to cook something for you, obviously we failed." she said flatly, falling at him with the corner of her eye.
Dexter stared at her.
They tried to cook something... for him?
He was stunned. The girls had been distant and guarded toward him. He had always been the one taking care of them.
Cooking, cleaning, buying supplies and making sure they were comfortable.
He had never expected them to try doing something for him. The fact that they had attempted to do something for him felt strange and surprising.

paragraphs: The fact that they had attempted to do something for him felt strange and surprising.
His gaze softened slightly.
"Are you sure?" Dexter asked slowly. "If you were hungry, you just needed to ask. I would have made something for you."
Mira shook her head. "No. We. wanted to make something special for you."
Dexter fell quiet. The idea sat strangely in his mind.
Why would they make something for him?
He was the one taking care of them, providing shelter, food, protection.
They had never once tried to reciprocate. The gesture, while seemingly innocent, didn’t add up.
He looked at the three of them seated on the couch, his eyes narrowing with suspicion as he glared at Mira.
She must be the mastermind behind it. While the system said Lyra was the devious and two faced one, he felt like Mira was the true prankster.
Mira rolled her eyes even harder.
"Why are you looking at us suspiciously?" she said. "You’re the suspicious one."
Dexter frowned. "Suspicious about what?"
Selene spoke again, her voice still quiet. However its tone had changed.
"What do you know about second awakening?"
The question landed like a stone dropped into still water.
Dexter’s expression tightened as his mind raced. Did one of them finally awaken?
He knew Mira had already awakened but the other two, Selene and Lyra, hadn’t awakened yet. Had one of them finally manifested the second ability?
"I have no idea what you’re talking about," Dexter lied smoothly.
Instantly, Selene’s head snapped toward him. "You’re lying," she said quietly. "Your heartbeat skipped a beat just now."
Dexter feigned shock, his eyes widening as he looked between the girls.
"Wait—the two of you awakened a second ability as well?" He turned to Mira. "You already awakened the Spectral arms ability. But what about you two?"
He turned to Selene. "Selene, you said you heard my heart skip a beat. What did you mean by that?"
A small smile crept onto Selene’s face. She replied in a quiet, gentle tone.
"I can finally see things now."
Dexter’s eyes popped open in exaggerated surprise. "You can see?"

Selene shook her head. "Not really. I can’t see colors or details. But I can see through vibrations. I can see the outlines. It’s not true sight, but..." She paused, her smile growing faintly. "I can see."
Dexter nodded warmly. "Congratulations. Even if it’s not the same as true sight, it’s still better than nothing."
Selene’s expression flickered with something like gratitude, perhaps—but she remained quiet, her nature keeping her words to herself.
Dexter then turned to Lyra.
"Lyra, what did you—"
’I awakened telepathy.’
The voice resonated inside his mind again—clear, soft, unmistakable. Lyra’s voice.
’I can hear the surface level thought thoughts of other people. And if they open their mind to me, I can speak to them also.’
Dexter clutched his chest in mock astonishment. "That’s incredible," he said, his voice dripping with theatrical disbelief.
Then, recovering, he stroked his chin thoughtfully. "Maybe it’s because your body realized what it had lost. Your body compensated, and awakened a new one to replace it."
Mira scoffed loudly as she gestured around at the three of them, with her chin.

"Do you think we’re idiots? Countless people lose their abilities, but they don’t magically awaken a talent that perfectly bypasses their specific disability. Lyra can’t speak, so she gets telepathy. Selene is blind, so she gets echolocation. I can’t move, so I get spectral arms. There is no such thing as a coincidence this perfect."
Mira’s crimson eyes locked onto him. "The only thing linking the three of us together is you, Dexter."
The three girls stared at him, suspicion etched deeply into their faces.
Dexter stared back at them for a long moment and when it seemed he was about to crack, he burst out laughing.
"Wait—wait." He held up a hand, trying to contain his laughter. "Are you three seriously telling me you believe I have the ability to grant other people talents?"
The girls glanced at each other but didn’t respond.
Because they realized how ridiculous it sounded.
No one in the world had the ability to grant talents. The idea was absurd and they knew it. Mira, despite her stubborn nature, knew it.
And yet...

Dexter was the only person in their lives. The only constant. The only variable that had entered their world before these awakenings began. He was the only suspicious person they could point to. But accusing someone of granting abilities was like accusing them of controlling the reality.
Mira’s mouth tightened. She wanted to argue, but even she couldn’t rationalize it.
Dexter grinned sheepishly and waved his hand dismissively.
"I’m really happy," he said lightly, "that the three of you managed to awaken abilities that can assist you. That’s all that matters, right?"
Then, seemingly as an afterthought, he turned toward Lyra and spoke aloud while projecting his thought to her at the same time.
"Lyra, your voice is incredibly sweet. Like a thousand sirens calling out at the same time. Its’s really nice and soothing."
Mira smirked. "Greedy pervert."
A faint blush crept across Lyra’s cheeks. Her voice fluttered softly in Dexter’s mind.
’Thank you.’
Dexter chuckled, then turned to Mira with a teasing grin. "Are you jealous? If you are, just beg me and I’ll compliment you too."
Mira sneered. "As if I’d need your compliments."
Dexter shrugged dramatically. "Alright. Suit yourself." He paused, then leaned in with a sly smile. "Jealous brat."
"I am not jealous," Mira shot back immediately.
Her quick response only made Dexter’s smile widen.
"Sure you aren’t."
Mira rolled her eyes, refusing to continue the argument.
"Anyway, I got you girls something."

He walked back to the entrance of the house, where he had dropped several bags earlier when he first arrived. He scooped them up and carried them into the living room, setting them down on the floor in front of the couch.
From the first bag, he pulled out a massive egg the size of a watermelon. It was the ancient egg he got from the system.

chapters.title: Chapter 95 | The Ancient Eggs [3rd GT & Gift]
paragraphs: The egg shell wasn’t smooth like an ordinary bird’s egg. Instead, it was covered with overlapping scales that resembled the scales of an ancient dragon. Tiny cracks ran across its surface, giving it an ancient and mysterious appearance.
Dexter held it up for the girls to see.
"This," he announced proudly, "is the egg of an ancient beast."
Mira stared at it. Then she looked at Dexter.
"You got scammed again," she said flatly.
Dexter’s rolled his eyes. "You can’t scam a scammer. I’ve been in the business since I was 13, of course I know if I’m been scammed."
Life in the Ashford family hadn’t been kind. He had to scam a few kind souls just to survive.
Lyra and Selene were faintly curious.
They was the first time they were curious about anything other than the second awakening ever since Dexter had met them.
Selene’s vibration-sense picked up the egg’s outline and Lyra curiously looked at it.
The egg sat in Dexter’s hands like a relic from another era.
Mira, however, wasn’t impressed. "You should probably go collect your money from whoever sold you this," she said, her voice dripping with skepticism.
Dexter shook his head slowly. "Do you want it or not?"
He began to pull the egg away, as if to take it back.
Before he could move more than a few inches, two glowing Mana arms glowing faintly with pale light. shot out from Mira’s side and snatched the egg from his hands.
Dexter smirked. "I thought you said it was a scam."
Mira said nothing. Her spectral arm gently carried the egg toward her and settled it carefully onto her lap.
While her expression remained neutral, but the fact that she had claimed it so quickly spoke volumes.
Selene and Lyra immediately moved closer, drawn by curiosity. They reached out and touched the egg’s surface.
As they touched it, their expressions changed when they realized they couldn’t see through the egg with their mana but the egg was actively sucking any mana they provided like a sponge.
The egg didn’t feel like a fake.
Mira felt it too. But she said nothing. She simply held the egg in her lap and stared at it.
"I heard it will hatch if one cultivates beside it. With the three of you cultivating by it, it would be faster than me cultivating with it. "
Dexter watched them for a moment, smiling faintly, then reached into the bag again.
"That’s not all I got for you.
He pulled out three weapons.
They had been wrapped casually in a grocery bag and bundled together like ordinary purchases. But the moment he unwrapped them, it was clear they were anything but ordinary.
The first was a beautiful black sword that seemed even darker than the shadows.
The second was a silver sword and the third was crimson sword.
He handed the black sword to Lyra.
"This one’s yours."
Then he passed the silver one to Selene.
"And this belongs to you."
Finally, he gently laid the crimson sword across Mira’s lap.
Mira stared at it before slowly looking back at him.
"You do remember that I’m paralyzed... right?"
Dexter shrugged unconcerned.

"When you become more proficient with your spectral arms," he said calmly, "you’ll be able to wield it. This weapon has a fire attribute. Once your control improves, it should complement your abilities perfectly."
Mira opened her mouth to argue, but Dexter had already turned away.
He faced Lyra next.
"The relic weapon has shadow attributes and will enhance your shadow abilities and amplify your overall talents."
Lyra’s reached out and took the weapon, her fingers curling around its dark surface.
Then Dexter turned to Selene.

She was already looking at him—or rather, looking in his direction. Her new echolocation ability painted the world in shapes and outlines, vibrations forming a three-dimensional map of everything around her.
She could see him now, not in color, but in form.
Dexter held up the silver weapon, letting her sense its outline through vibration.
"And this one," he said, "is for you."
Suddenly, Mira noticed something.
"You bought three Type 3 weapons?" Her tone was a bit high.
Dexter nodded casually. "Yeah. Got them at a discount, too. Really great deal."
The room went quiet.
Relic weapons were supposed to be rare and expensive, not the kind of thing an ordinary house husband could just walk into a store and buy three of, discount or no discount.
And yet, Dexter had done exactly that.
Mira’s eyes narrowed, a knowing smile crept onto her face.
"Now I know," she said. "There are people backing you up."
Dexter shrugged. "I never said its true."
"You never denied it either," Mira countered.
Dexter simply laughed at her observation, offering neither confirmation nor denial. Then he reached into the bag again.
This time, he pulled out two necklaces.
He had already given Mira one before, so he had purchased two similar ones for Lyra and Selene. He didn’t want the other two girls feeling left out or jealous.
He handed the necklaces to Lyra and Selene.
The two girls hesitated, wanting to refuse, but the necklaces were genuinely stunning.
They glanced at Mira, at the way her necklace sat against her neck, how perfectly it complemented her, how astonishingly beautiful it looked against her skin.
Mira noticed them looking. Her smirk returned.
"I see," she said, her voice dripping with implication. "You forcefully gave me a collar. Now you’ve gotten two similar ones for them." She tilted her head, her eyes boring into Dexter.
"Why? Are you branding us as your property?"
Dexter was momentarily stunned. Then he rolled his eyes.
"I know exactly what you’re doing. Nice try though."
Mira’s smirk didn’t falter, but she didn’t push further.
Dexter reached into the bags one final time and began pulling out the rest of the jewelry he had purchased.
Anklets, bracelets, earrings. He had even bought gold mirrors for the girls.
One by one, he laid them out on the center table, dragging it closer to the couch so they could see everything clearly.

chapters.title: Chapter 96 | S-so Warm! [4th GT]
paragraphs: The jewelry was dazzling.

Selene and Lyra stared at the display, slightly overwhelmed. But rather than reaching for the jewelry, they simply took the necklaces Dexter had handed them, stood up from the couch, and walked to the bedroom without a word.
They didn’t take anything else. They didn’t say thank you. They didn’t say anything at all.
Dexter watched them go, noting the shift in their demeanor. Their mood had soured visibly and the warmth and curiosity from moments ago had evaporated as they appeared more distant.
’Weren’t we just making progress?’
Mira smirked from her wheelchair, watching Dexter’s expression shift as realization dawned on him.
"You think you’re trying too hard. " she said, indifferently.
Dexter blinked, then sighed. "The vendor forced me to buy all of this," he muttered. "I just wanted to get a few things, and the vendor practically shoved the rest at me."
Mira shrugged. "Do what you want."

Her spectral arm extended slowly, trembling slightly with the effort, and gripped the wheel of her chair. She began rolling herself forward toward the bedroom. She didn’t ask Dexter to push her even though she could barely control the Mana arms.
Dexter watched her go, her wheelchair creaking slowly across the floor. He opened his mouth as if to offer assistance, then thought better of it and closed it.
He simply stood there as the last of the three girls disappeared into the bedroom.
He shrugged to himself and turned toward the kitchen.
The moment he stepped inside, the source of the smoke became apparent.
The girls had attempted to make noodles and somehow, impossibly, they had burnt even that.
Dexter chuckled in amusement. The fact that they had tried to cook for him was really nice.
But it also meant he had work to do.
He sighed and rolled up his sleeves.

As he cleaned the kitchen, scrubbing the burnt pot, wiping down the counters, clearing the smoke, then he noticed that the food he had cooked that morning for the girls had also run out. They had eaten everything, or rather Lyra had eaten everything.
So he pulled out the ingredients he had purchased earlier, spread everything across the counter and set to work.
He didn’t use the Diamond rice this time. He already planned on using them once a day.
So he made spaghetti, incorporated with heavenly materials like the cosmic star origin Necter and other herbs that elevated it beyond a simple meal.
Moreover, he used his Heavenly Flame: Emperor Void Flames to make the dish.
The pure white flames cooked the food rapidly.
By the time he finished, a massive pot of steaming plates of beautifully crafted spaghetti sat on the counter.
[Name: MoonFire Pasta]
[Grade: 2 Arcane Meal]
[Effect: Restores 25% of stamina and 15% of mana over five minutes. Increases mana recovery by 10% for the next 30 minutes.]
[Special Effect: Moonfire Warmth — Grants immunity to cold environments below 0°C and increases Fire-attribute spell power by 5% for 20 minutes.]
The aroma filled the kitchen—rich, savory, inviting.
He looked up.
Selene was standing in the doorway of the bedroom, staring directly at him.
He chuckled and thought she was staring at him.
"Are you hungry?" But she didn’t answer and stared at his chest instead, reluctance and hesitation on her face.
Beside her stood Lyra. But Lyra wasn’t looking at Dexter. Her gaze was locked firmly on the food, her attention captured entirely by the plates of spaghetti on the counter.
Two girls. Two very different stares. And Dexter stood between them, spatula in hand, wondering what either of them was thinking.
Dexter raised an eyebrow, looking between the two girls standing in the doorway.
"Are you girls hungry? Do you want to eat?" He glanced at the clock on the wall. "It’s still afternoon and a bit early for dinner. But if you want, I can give you a portion of what I made."
Lyra nodded immediately. Her mouth was already watering, with her eyes fixed on the steaming plates of spaghetti.
Dexter could feel her voice echoing in his mind
’Give me. Give me. Give me. Give me.’
Over and over, like a hungry child begging for treats.
Dexter chuckled. "So cute," he said—not in his mind, but out loud.
Lyra froze. Her neck flushed a deep crimson that crept up to her ears. But the embarrassment lasted only a fraction of a second before the pull of the food overpowered it.
She remained rooted in place, eyes locked on the plates, waiting with barely contained patience as Dexter scooped a generous portion onto a plate and handed it to her.
Lyra immediately took it and disappeared.
Selene, however, hadn’t moved.
She was still standing there, her white eyes fixed on Dexter.
Dexter frowned slightly and met her gaze spoke gently.
"You can tell me if you need something. I’ll get it for you. Do you also want a portion of the food?"
She slowly shook her head.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Then what is it?"
She hesitated. Her lips parted, then closed. Then parted again.
"I..." Her voice was barely audible. "Can I touch you?"
Dexter blinked.
Touch him?
This was the girl who had always avoided contact, kept her distance, always shied away from him but now she was asking to touch him?
He chuckled at the irony. "Sure," he said. "You can—"
He hadn’t even finished the sentence before her hands shot out and grabbed his arm.
She held on to his left arm tightly.
Her fingers wrapped around his forearm and locked there, squeezing as though she feared he might vanish at any moment.
She closed her eyes, pressing herself closer, and took in the warmth radiating from his skin.
"So warm," she whispered unconsciously, her voice soft and dreamy. She sighed a gentle, contented sound that came out like the purr of a kitten. "So warm. Very warm."
Dexter smiled. She was really beautiful. Her white eyes, her delicate features, the way her expression softened when she let her guard down.
It was so stunning it blew Dexter’s mind away for a split second before he recovered.

Their mood had soured visibly and the warmth and curiosity from moments ago had evaporated as they appeared more distant.
’Weren’t we just making progress?’
Mira smirked from her wheelchair, watching Dexter’s expression shift as realization dawned on him.
"You think you’re trying too hard.
" she said, indifferently.
Dexter blinked, then sighed.
"The vendor forced me to buy all of this," he muttered.
"I just wanted to get a few things, and the vendor practically shoved the rest at me."
Mira shrugged.
"Do what you want."
Her spectral arm extended slowly, trembling slightly with the effort, and gripped the wheel of her chair.
She began rolling herself forward toward the bedroom.
She didn’t ask Dexter to push her even though she could barely control the Mana arms.
Dexter watched her go, her wheelchair creaking slowly across the floor.
He opened his mouth as if to offer assistance, then thought better of it and closed it.
He simply stood there as the last of the three girls disappeared into the bedroom.
He shrugged to himself and turned toward the kitchen.
The moment he stepped inside, the source of the smoke became apparent.
The girls had attempted to make noodles and somehow, impossibly, they had burnt even that.
Dexter chuckled in amusement.
The fact that they had tried to cook for him was really nice.
But it also meant he had work to do.
He sighed and rolled up his sleeves.
As he cleaned the kitchen, scrubbing the burnt pot, wiping down the counters, clearing the smoke, then he noticed that the food he had cooked that morning for the girls had also run out.
They had eaten everything, or rather Lyra had eaten everything.
So he pulled out the ingredients he had purchased earlier, spread everything across the counter and set to work.
He didn’t use the Diamond rice this time.
He already planned on using them once a day.
So he made spaghetti, incorporated with heavenly materials like the cosmic star origin Necter and other herbs that elevated it beyond a simple meal.
Moreover, he used his Heavenly Flame: Emperor Void Flames to make the dish.
The pure white flames cooked the food rapidly.
By the time he finished, a massive pot of steaming plates of beautifully crafted spaghetti sat on the counter.
[Name: MoonFire Pasta]
[Grade: 2 Arcane Meal]
[Effect: Restores 25% of stamina and 15% of mana over five minutes.
Increases mana recovery by 10% for the next 30 minutes.]
[Special Effect: Moonfire Warmth — Grants immunity to cold environments below 0°C and increases Fire-attribute spell power by 5% for 20 minutes.]
The aroma filled the kitchen—rich, savory, inviting.
He looked up.
Selene was standing in the doorway of the bedroom, staring directly at him.
He chuckled and thought she was staring at him.
"Are you hungry?" But she didn’t answer and stared at his chest instead, reluctance and hesitation on her face.
Beside her stood Lyra.
But Lyra wasn’t looking at Dexter.
Her gaze was locked firmly on the food, her attention captured entirely by the plates of spaghetti on the counter.
Two girls.
Two very different stares.
And Dexter stood between them, spatula in hand, wondering what either of them was thinking.
Dexter raised an eyebrow, looking between the two girls standing in the doorway.
"Are you girls hungry?
Do you want to eat?" He glanced at the clock on the wall.
"It’s still afternoon and a bit early for dinner.
But if you want, I can give you a portion of what I made."
Lyra nodded immediately.
Her mouth was already watering, with her eyes fixed on the steaming plates of spaghetti.
Dexter could feel her voice echoing in his mind
’Give me.
Give me.
Give me.
Give me.’
Over and over, like a hungry child begging for treats.
Dexter chuckled.
"So cute," he said—not in his mind, but out loud.
Lyra froze.
Her neck flushed a deep crimson that crept up to her ears.
But the embarrassment lasted only a fraction of a second before the pull of the food overpowered it.
She remained rooted in place, eyes locked on the plates, waiting with barely contained patience as Dexter scooped a generous portion onto a plate and handed it to her.
Lyra immediately took it and disappeared.
Selene, however, hadn’t moved.
She was still standing there, her white eyes fixed on Dexter.
Dexter frowned slightly and met her gaze spoke gently.
"You can tell me if you need something.
I’ll get it for you.
Do you also want a portion of the food?"
She slowly shook her head.
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"Then what is it?"
She hesitated.
Her lips parted, then closed.
Then parted again.
"I..." Her voice was barely audible.
"Can I touch you?"
Dexter blinked.
Touch him?
This was the girl who had always avoided contact, kept her distance, always shied away from him but now she was asking to touch him?
He chuckled at the irony.
"Sure," he said.
"You can—"
He hadn’t even finished the sentence before her hands shot out and grabbed his arm.
She held on to his left arm tightly.
Her fingers wrapped around his forearm and locked there, squeezing as though she feared he might vanish at any moment.
She closed her eyes, pressing herself closer, and took in the warmth radiating from his skin.
"So warm," she whispered unconsciously, her voice soft and dreamy.
She sighed a gentle, contented sound that came out like the purr of a kitten.
"So warm.
Very warm."
Dexter smiled.
She was really beautiful.
Her white eyes, her delicate features, the way her expression softened when she let her guard down.
It was so stunning it blew Dexter’s mind away for a split second before he recovered.

chapters.title: Chapter 97 | Sorting Out Rewards [5th GT]
paragraphs: Selene held on to his left arm tightly.
But as she held onto his arm, he noticed something else.

Her body was cold, deeply, unnaturally cold. The kind of cold that seeped through fabric and skin and settled into bone. It crawled up his arm and shot straight down his spine, making him shudder involuntarily. No wonder she had wanted warmth. Her body was practically radiating frost.
Although he shared her pain, he didn’t share her discomfort.
’Should I activate it?’
Dexter pondered a while but then shrugged and activated Flame Will within his body.
His blood heated instantly as it almost turned into molten magma in his body. But with the Chaos Flame Demon Bloodline, he was resistant to the heat.
The change was immediate and dramatic. Heat poured off his skin in waves, turning his arm into a furnace.
"Mmmh..."
Selene moaned unconsciously as her grip tightened and her fingers dug in harder, clutching his arm like a child gripping a teddy bear.

She pressed herself against him, absorbing every bit of warmth she could, and purred and moaned continuously and unconsciously as she simply held on, eyes closed, drinking in the heat like a flower turning toward the sun.
They stood there for ten minutes.
Dexter finally leaned down and whispered.
"Should we head to the living room?"
Selene didn’t respond. Her eyes remained closed. Her body continued absorbing the heat, and she gave no indication that she had heard him at all.
Dexter sighed.

He began walking slowly, toward the living room. Selene didn’t let go. She shuffled along beside him, her arms still wrapped around his, her eyes still closed, her body still pressed against his side.
When they reached the living room, he settled onto the couch. Selene sat beside him, still hugging his arm, her head gradually drifting down until it rested against his shoulder.
Dexter reached for the remote with his free hand and turned on the television.

The screen flickered to life. He scrolled through the channels—news, news, more news. He hadn’t purchased any subscription packages yet, so the available options were limited to free broadcasts. Everything was either news or mind-numbingly boring.
He kept flipping.
Then he landed on something unexpected.
A telenovela.
The episode was already in progress.
Two characters arguing passionately on screen, their dramatic confrontation underscored by swelling music and tight camera angles. Within moments, Dexter was hooked.
The plot twists came fast and furious, each one more outrageous than the last.
Beside him, Selene’s eyes were still closed. But through her echolocation, she could feel his heart rate spiking up sis she ended up listening to the drama on the tv.
Within minutes, she was as captivated as Dexter was. Her expression shifted with every scene and her eyes widening at shocking reveals.

Sometimes, she would even shake her head shaking slowly when someone did something spectacularly stupid. Occasionally, a small smile would creep onto her face when a character displayed unexpected cleverness.
Dexter didn’t notice any of this. He was too absorbed in the drama unfolding on screen to realize that the girl attached to his arm had quietly become his viewing or better still, his ompanion.
They sat for an hour.
When the episode ended, Dexter sat back, slightly dazed.
"That was..." he murmured. "That was really good."
Then he noticed something.
The temperature in the room had dropped.
A cold, biting fury radiated from Selene, it was directed squarely at the television.
Dexter’s eyes traveled downward.
The wooden TV stand beneath the television was frozen.
A layer of frost had crept across its surface. The cold had spread to the wall behind it.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
"Wait, wait, wait—" He held up his hands. "The TV—let’s not break the TV."
He lunged for the remote and switched off the television.
He let out a breath he didn’t realize he’d been holding, then turned to Selene.
"So," he said, his voice careful and measured. "You like telenovelas?"
Selene blinked.

Her eyes focused—as though she were waking from a dream. She looked down at her hands, still wrapped around Dexter’s arm. She looked at the frost-covered TV stand. She looked at the ice crawling up the wall.
The realization hit her all at once.

She immediately released his arm instantly, as though it had burned her. A deep blush erupted across her cheeks. It was so vivid against her pale skin. She stumbled backward, turned, and fled the room like a rabbit being pursued by the predator as she disappeared down the hallway toward the bedroom.
Dexter stood there, arm suddenly cold and empty.
He touched his nose, a crooked smile spreading across his face.
"After you used me, now you’re abandoning me."
He stood there for a moment longer, shaking his head softly. Then he turned off the lights in the living room and headed to his own room.
It was time to cultivate.
And more importantly, it was time to sort out his previous rewards.
[1. Professional Rank Promotion: Great Grandmaster Foodsmith (Early Stage) ➔ Great Grandmaster Foodsmith (Middle Stage)]
[2. Special Physical Constitution: Heavenly Gastronomy Body]
[3. Elemental Evolution: Alchemist Flame ➔ 9th Heavenly Flame: Emperor Void Flame]
[4. Raw Materials: 1,000kg of Premium Diamond Rice]
[5. Rare Liquids: 100kg of Cosmic Star Origin Nectar]
[6. Premium Alcohol: 100kg of Burning Sun Lava Wine]
[7. Talent Evolution: Mana Affinity (SS-Rank) ➔ Mana Affinity (SSS-Rank)]

chapters.title: Chapter 98 | Heaven Gastronomy Body [6th]
paragraphs: [Name: Heavenly Gastronomy Body]
[Grade: Divine Constitution]
[Description:

A legendary physique said to have been created by the Heavenly God of Cuisine. Every ingredient consumed is perfectly refined, allowing the body to absorb 100% of its nutritional, spiritual, and magical essence while eliminating all impurities.

Unlike ordinary physiques that merely strengthen the body, the Heavenly Gastronomy Body transforms every meal into cultivation. The rarer and more powerful the ingredients, the greater the evolution of the user’s body.]
[Passive Abilities]
• Cooking Efficiency: +200%
• Alchemy Success Rate: +200%
• Fire Attribute Damage: +200%
• Infinite Nutrient Absorption
Absorbs 100% of all nutrients, mana, spiritual essence, and life force contained within food.
• Gourmet Evolution
Every first-time consumption of a rare ingredient permanently increases one or more attributes.
• Arcane Metabolism
Magical meals grant twice their original effects and their duration is increased by 100%.
• Monster Cuisine
The flesh of magical beasts, dragons, demons, and divine creatures can be safely consumed regardless of toxicity.
• Culinary Insight
Instantly understands the quality, freshness, rarity, grade, and hidden effects of any ingredient upon sight.
• Divine Appetite
The body instinctively craves ingredients capable of triggering future evolutions.
[Current Evolution Stage]
Heavenly Gastronomy Body (Awakened)
[Name: Emperor Void Flame]
[Classification: 9th Heavenly Flame]
[Grade: Divine]
[Description:

One of the Nine Heavenly Flames in the world. The Emperor Void Flame burns not only matter but souls and even strong enough, can burn even mana, curses, and even fragments of space itself. It possesses intelligence and recognizes only a single master.]
[Abilities]
• Absolute Incineration
Burns nearly anything regardless of elemental resistance.
• Void Devour
Consumes other flames and permanently strengthens itself.
• Heavenly Refinement
Raises the success rate of forging, alchemy, cooking, and enchantments by 500%
• Soul Flame
Damages both the physical body and the soul simultaneously.
• Emperor’s Dominion
All flames of lower rank become suppressed within a large radius.
• Flame Regeneration
The user rapidly regenerates stamina, mana, and injuries while surrounded by the Emperor Void Flame.
• World Scorch
Creates a domain where everything within is gradually consumed by divine void fire.
[Passive Effects]
• Fire Resistance: ∞
• Poison Resistance: 100%
• Heat Resistance: Absolute
• Cooking Efficiency: +500%
• Alchemy Success Rate: +300%
• Fire Attribute Damage: +1000%
• Mana Consumption of Fire Skills: -70%
Dexter was quite satisfied with the physique and also the heavenly flames. With them, failing to cook headed meals would be impossible.
In fact, if he knowingly wanted to cook ordinary meals, it would automatically be Arcane meals, making it physically impossible for Dexter to cook ordinary meals.
’Sigh, it’s so lonely at the top.’
As a Great Grandmaster food Amith, barely anyone in the entire Stargate city could rival his cooking ability!
’Maybe I should become a chef and sell my food for money.’
The more he thought about it, the more the idea expanded in his head and he smiled. "Perfect. I will start after the sparring battle."
As for the heavenly flames, he wondered if that’s the reason Selene clung to him. Since it could melt anything in the world, does it mean it could melt the Eternal Winter Ice that was afflicting her?
He would find a time to test this theory. He simply needed to wait for her to come to him. She was like a rabbit after all.
He then began pondering other things.
Why hadn’t he gotten his rewards yet from the system?
But he figured out that probably because the beds hadn’t arrived yet so the system couldn’t calculate his rewards based on what the girls hadn’t seen and reacted to yet.
Dexter returned to his room feeling deeply satisfied. The power coursing through his veins was a constant reminder of how far he had come in such a short time.
However, rather than resting, he immediately sat cross-legged on his airbed and closed his eyes, intending to use the remaining hours of the afternoon to cultivate.
He had barely begun circulating the Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture when a sudden, sharp warning flared at the back of his mind.
It was his Frost Sense.
Selene.
Her internal cold energy was spiking rapidly which meant she was about to have a seizure.
Dexter’s eyes snapped open instantly. He lunged toward the pile of groceries and supply bags he had left beside his bed, until his fingers closed around the ice-suppressing serum.
Gripping the syringe tightly, Dexter activated Flame Burst.
"BOOM!"
A violent explosion of heat erupted beneath his feet. The air in his small bedroom distorted wildly as his body became a blur of crimson light.
He vanished from his room, leaving behind a scorch mark on the floorboards and a wave of displaced air that sent his bedsheets flying.
The lady’s room was dim as the curtains were half-drawn. The three wives were arranged in a loose circle.
Mira sat in her wheelchair near the bedside, facing the mattress.
Lyra and Selene sat cross-legged on the bed, and resting at the center of their triangle was the massive, dragon-scaled ancient beast egg as they cultivated around it.
"Bam!"
Dexter burst through the girls’ bedroom without knocking.
The sudden commotion drew their attention. Mira cracked one eye open, glanced at him with indifference, and then closed it again, resuming her meditation without a word.
Lyra peered at him curiously through her type 2 AI smart glasses wondering why he came and if he brought something with him.
While Selene simply raised her slender pale arm, presenting it to Dexter.
"I’m sorry for barging in," Dexter said quickly as he stepped toward the bed.
He lined the syringe up against Selene’s exposed wrist and pressed the plunger, injecting the warm, thick serum directly into her bloodstream.

chapters.title: Chapter 99 | Dinner’s Ready
paragraphs: The moment the needle pierced her skin, Dexter felt the pain instead of Selene feeling the sharp prick of the needle, because ikf the Ring of Shared Burdens.
As the serum entered her system, Selene inhaled deeply.
The violent tremors that had begun to ripple through her body slowly subsided and her breathing steadied, the dangerous buildup of frost within her body began to recede.
Unconsciously, her cold fingers wrapped tightly around Dexter’s forearm, pulling it closer to her body as she sought out the comforting warmth radiating from his Flame Demon bloodline.
Dexter administered the full dose and carefully withdrew the empty syringe. But Selene still didn’t let go.
He stood there in an increasingly awkward position. He was hunched slightly over the bed, one arm trapped in Selene’s surprisingly strong grip.
Mira sat mere feet away with her eyes closed, though there was a fault smirk at the corner of her lips,
Meanwhile, Lyra kept glancing curiously at Dexter.
’This foodie.’
Dexter could tell immediately what Lyra wanted. He made a mental note to buy a variety of snacks the next time he went out, something she could munch on whenever she felt hungry between meals.
That way, she wouldn’t have to wait for him to cook every time her bottomless stomach demanded attention.
After a few more minutes of standing there like a human radiator, Dexter gently tapped Selene’s hand.
"Selene," he whispered. "It’s done. You can let go now."
Her eyes fluttered open. For a brief, disoriented moment, she seemed confused about why Dexter was saying to let go.
Then she immediately realized she had been holding him all these time.
"I- sorry."
Her pale cheeks flushed and she immediately released his arm as if his skin were burning hot.
She quickly pulled her hand back to her lap and lowered her head, unable to meet his gaze.
Dexter chuckled softly, pocketed the empty syringe, and turned to leave. As he reached the doorway, he paused and glanced back at the three girls.
Then he quietly closed the door behind him and returned to his room.
Sitting back down on his bed, Dexter reached into his system storage and pulled out three shimmering crystals.
They were the Bloodline Evolution Stones, the rewards he had received from the system quite some time ago.
In the chaos and emotional turbulence of the past few days, he had nearly forgotten they existed.
A Bloodline Evolution Stone was a priceless treasure.
According to the system, it could grant an entirely new bloodline to someone who possessed none, or it could evolve an existing bloodline by one full grade.
With these stones, the girls could potentially awaken bloodlines that would drastically increase their overall strength, accelerate their healing, and amplify their existing talents.
He had three stones. One for each wife.

The question was how to give them. If he simply handed the crystals over, the girls would immediately bombard him with questions about where he obtained such impossibly rare treasures. They were already suspicious of him after the second awakenings. Handing them bloodline stones would only add fuel to that fire.
He would need to find a subtle way to deliver them, perhaps integrating them into their meals, or slipping them into their bodies while they slept.
For now, he placed the three stones carefully back into his storage ring and closed his eyes.
It was time to cultivate.
Dexter sank deep into meditation and the two blazing Star Nodes within his inner universe began to spin, generating a powerful gravitational force that reached outward into the physical world.
Across the hallway, the three girls resumed their own cultivation of the Grand Cosmos Scripture.
Mira’s five awakened Star Nodes hummed with power. Selene’s four nodes pulsed steadily. And Lyra’s two nodes rotated along.
As the four of them cultivated simultaneously, something extraordinary began to happen.
Invisible currents of mana started flowing through the entire house.
But as the minutes passed and their absorption rates climbed, the flow intensified dramatically.
The mana in the surrounding neighborhood began to drift toward the bungalow.
The phenomenon was identical to what had occurred the day before.
A Mana Hurricane.
There was no wind. No physical force moved through the house. Yet the window curtains billowed outward as if caught in a violent gale.
Outside, anyone with even a basic sensitivity to mana would have felt it if it weren’t for the protective barrier.
Dexter didn’t fully understand the phenomenon himself. He knew it was a byproduct of their cultivation, but he didn’t realize the true significance.
Three girls with S-Rank mana affinity and one man with an SSS-Rank affinity, all cultivating simultaneously using a 7th-Tier technique and 9th tier technique.
It was like placing four massive vacuum tubes in a single small room and turning them all on at maximum power.
Dexter cultivated through the afternoon and deep into the evening.
"RIIIIIING!"
He only stopped when the alarm on his phone rang out, breaking his meditation.
He had meticulously set alarms for every meal, as well as an alarm every four to five hours specifically to take Mira to the restroom.
It was a necessary schedule, given her paralysis.
Rising from his bed, he walked to the girls’ bedroom door and knocked twice.
Come in,’ a soft, melodic voice echoed directly inside his mind.
Dexter chuckled. Even after hearing it a few times, Lyra’s telepathic voice was endearingly cute.
"It’s dinner time already," Dexter projected back, leaning against the doorframe. "You guys should come and—"
He hadn’t even finished the sentence before the door snapped open. Lyra’s face popped out, her eyes wide and sparkling with hunger.
Dexter let out a laugh and pointed toward the kitchen. She didn’t need to be told twice; she practically teleported toward the dining table.
Feeling Lyra move away, Selene opened her eyes.
"Dinner is ready," Dexter told her softly. He then looked toward Mira. "Dinner is ready, Mira."
Selene nodded and stood up. She glanced between Dexter and Mira’s wheelchair, but Dexter simply shrugged. "I’ll take her. You go ahead."

chapters.title: Chapter 100 | Hope!
paragraphs: Selene opened her eyes.
Selene nodded and left the room. Mira kept her eyes closed as Dexter stepped behind her wheelchair.
"I’m cultivating," Mira stated flatly, her voice carrying a hint of annoyance at being interrupted.
Dexter chuckled, unlocking the wheels. "Okay, do something about it then."
Mira cracked one eye open to glare at him, but seeing his amused smile, she simply closed her eyes again and conceded.

Instead of heading straight to the kitchen, Dexter wheeled her into the bathroom. For the first time since they had moved in, she was wearing trousers instead of a dress, which made the process slightly different. With practiced efficiency, Dexter removed her trousers and panties, lifting her carefully and placing her on the toilet.
Both of them remained silent. Even after doing this countless times, a faint flush still crept up Mira’s pale cheeks.
Dexter’s neck was also slightly red, but his face remained perfectly indifferent.
"Call me when you’re done," he said, stepping outside the bathroom to wait.
He listened for the rush of water, waiting thirty seconds after the sound faded before stepping back inside. He dressed Mira, flushed the toilet, and lifted her back into her wheelchair.
Pushing her out to the dining table, he found Lyra and Selene already waiting.
Dexter hadn’t dished out the food yet. Lyra was staring at the covered pots with ravenous intensity, while Selene sat with her eyes closed.
She no longer needed to keep her eyes open to see; her Echolocation talent painted a perfect three-dimensional map of her surroundings through sound and vibration.
Dexter served the meals. He placed a portion in front of Selene, and her hand immediately snapped out, accurately finding the fork without needing any guidance.
"Nice!"
Dexter smiled at her progress.
Next, he placed three extra portions in front of Lyra, who instantly dove into her food.
The moment the first forkful of pasta entered her mouth, she sighed exaggeratedly, her eyes fluttering shut as the heavenly taste burst across her taste buds.
She swallowed and immediately shoved another bite in, sighing in contentment again.
Finally, Dexter placed the plate in front of Mira. He picked up the fork, about to feed her as usual, but Mira shook her head.
"Let me try feeding myself," she said quietly.
Dexter raised an eyebrow, frowning slightly. "You aren’t really proficient with the arms yet."
"If I don’t try, how will I become proficient?" Mira countered, meeting his gaze stubbornly.
Dexter shrugged. "As long as the food doesn’t spill."
Mira rolled her eyes. Two glowing orange spectral arms materialized behind her shoulders.
Selene watched curiously, while Lyra couldn’t care less, her mind was entirely devoted to devouring her pasta.
Mira controlled one of the spectral arms. It reached down, clumsily wrapping translucent fingers around the iron fork.
It lifted the pasta, trembling slightly from the uneven mana distribution. Mira opened her mouth, leaning forward to receive the bite.
"Snap."
The iron fork instantly shattered into tiny pieces, crushed to dust by her inability to regulate the spectral arm’s strength. The pasta tumbled down, staining her clean clothes.
Mira froze, her eyes unblinking but she was stubbornly refusing to be humiliated.
Dexter didn’t say a word.
He simply stood up, walked to the drawer, brought out ten more forks, and set them on the table beside her plate.
Then, he sat back down, picked up his own fork, and continued eating as if destroying cutlery was a perfectly normal dinner event.
Mira glanced at him, her heart skipping a beat.
A warm, unfamiliar feeling trickled into her chest as she knew Dexter was actually considering her feelings and didn’t want to embarrass her.
Swallowing her pride, she grabbed another fork with her spectral arm and tried again.
It took her seven attempts. Six crushed forks and stained napkins later, she finally managed to regulate the pressure, guiding a neat bite of pasta into her mouth.
Dexter looked up, gave her a thumbs-up, and smiled. "Nice."
Mira rolled her eyes, though a tiny, reluctant smile tugged at her lips.
She continued to feed herself. It was incredibly slow.
But thanks to the properties of his Grade-Two cooking, the meal never lost its heat or its taste, remaining perfectly warm as if freshly cooked even after hours on the plate.
It took an hour and half for Mira to finish her dinner, but by the end of it, her proficiency with the spectral arms had increased drastically.
Dexter was genuinely happy; she could finally feed herself.
After dinner, the girls went to freshen up. When Dexter offered to help Mira bathe, she shook her head.
"I don’t need to bathe twice a day," she muttered. "Once is enough. I’ll bathe tomorrow."
Dexter shrugged. "Alright."
He wished the girls goodnight and retreated to his room to cultivate.
He suddenly remembered he was in pain as the Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture tempered his organs.
The chronic pain absorbed from the girls was a constant, agonizing companion, but the scripture was slowly converting that suffering into raw strength.
To bear it, he forced himself into a deep meditative trance. He mediated for five solid hours before exhaustion finally pulled him into a dreamless sleep.
Later that night, inside the girls’ bedroom, the room was silent.
Mira was lying at the edge of the bed. Her eyes were open, staring blankly at the ceiling as she silently cultivated the Grand Cosmos Scripture.
Suddenly, she felt it.

A phantom sensation. She had felt them countless times over the past three years the cruel, psychological torture of thinking she could move her limbs, only to realize it was just a phantom sensation from her severed nerves.
But this time, it felt... different. More real.
Out of curiosity, Mira shifted her gaze to the corner of her eye, looking down at her right hand resting on the mattress.
Suddenly, her expression changed as her breathing froze.
She could see something moving and that something was actually her index finger!
It wasn’t a phantom sensation but was real instead! And she was actually moving her finger!
Without knowing, tears fell down her eyes and rolled down the side of her head, soaking into the pillow.

She didn’t sniffle or make a sound, as if terrified that if she acknowledged it too loudly, the miracle would vanish. She just lay there, crying silently as a wave of desperate, long-abandoned hope crashed over her like a tide!
